factors.name: Phase-Aligned Time-Delay Aggregation of Detrended Mid-Price (Volume-Coherence Gated)
factors.description: For each ticker, causally detrend close with a trailing moving average (SeriesDecomp), estimate the autocorrelation R(tau) of the residual over a trailing window via FFT (Wiener-Khinchin), select the top-k lags tau_i >= horizon whose softmax-weighted, volume-coherence-gated delay aggregation predicts the residual 6 bars ahead as sum_i w_i * s_{t+6-tau_i}; the factor is the predicted residual change (forecast minus current residual), normalized by residual volatility and cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Institutional execution schedulers (TWAP/VWAP/POV slicers) release child orders on quasi-regular clocks, so a stock's intraday mid-price residual around its local trend often carries a name-specific quasi-period rather than white noise. Autoformer's core insight is that the informative structure lives in sub-series at the SAME PHASE of an estimated period, recovered by FFT autocorrelation and exploited via time-delay aggregation instead of point-wise extrapolation; we apply exactly that machinery causally, per name, per bar. The edge is gated on cross-field coherence: we only trust a price period tau when the detrended traded-volume series shows autocorrelation at the same tau, which is the fingerprint of a mechanical order-slicing clock rather than a spurious spectral peak. The other side is the scheduled executor who must trade on their clock regardless of phase; the inefficiency persists because the periods are per-name, non-stationary, decay within minutes, and capacity is tiny, so slow-moving capital ignores them. Falsifier: if replacing the argmax-autocorrelation lags with randomly drawn lags (placebo) yields the same IC, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Self-Calibrating Multi-Scale Haar Detail Fusion
factors.description: Computes causal, non-decimated Haar detail coefficients of log mid-price at dyadic scales (1,2,4,8,16,32 bars), volatility-normalizes and cross-sectionally demeans each band, then combines the bands with adaptive weights equal to an EWMA of each band's past cross-sectional rank IC against realized 6-bar forward returns (lagged by more than the horizon so no future data is used), optionally modulating the finest bands by relative bar volume; the output is the cross-sectional rank of the fused score.
factors.trading_idea: The LMWT paper's core object is not a transformer but a multi-scale Haar decomposition whose per-scale coefficients are *learned* rather than fixed, so the model can decide how much each frequency band contributes. Applied to intraday price paths, each Haar detail band has a genuinely different economic content: the finest bands (1-2 bars) are dominated by quote bounce, inventory-driven liquidity provision and impatient-order noise, which decays and reverses; the coarser bands (8-32 bars) carry slower informed accumulation that persists. A single momentum or reversal factor forces one sign on all bands and therefore averages these opposing effects away; here I estimate, causally and online, the sign and magnitude of each band's cross-sectional predictive weight (the empirical analogue of the paper's learnable alpha/beta/gamma/delta) and fuse the bands with those weights. The edge should persist because market makers and short-horizon liquidity demanders are structurally forced to trade against transient price pressure at specific timescales, while slower informed flow is not arbitraged within a minute; the idea is falsified if the online per-scale weights are unstable in sign (i.e. no stable scale structure exists) or if the fused signal adds nothing over the single best band.

factors.name: Kalman Beta-Uncertainty-Weighted Innovation Reversal
factors.description: Runs a causal per-ticker Kalman filter of bar returns on the cross-sectional market return with a random-walk beta, then signals minus the one-step standardized innovation v/sqrt(H) scaled by the filter's transient-noise share sigma_e^2/H, lightly EWMA-smoothed and cross-sectionally standardized, with a secondary negative tilt on the recent change in beta-forecast conditional volatility sqrt(H).
factors.trading_idea: Brigida (2025) treats a loading as an unobserved random-walk state and shows the useful object is not the point estimate but the Kalman filter's one-step forecast variance H_t|t-1 = x'P_t|t-1x + sigma_e^2, which decomposes a surprise into a persistent state shift versus transient noise. Applied intraday, each stock's market beta genuinely drifts (inventory, index flow, sector rotation), so a bar's residual return is ambiguous: it is either a real re-loading on the market (persistent, must NOT be faded) or transaction noise / one-off liquidity demand (transient, should be faded). The filter supplies the exact Bayesian split: the noise share sigma_e^2 / H_t|t-1 is the posterior probability weight that the innovation is temporary, so fading residuals in proportion to that weight buys reversal only where reversion is actually warranted. This persists because market makers and stat-arb desks price residuals off static or slowly re-estimated betas and therefore over-fade genuine loading shifts and under-fade pure noise; it is falsified if reversal strength is flat in the noise share, i.e. if interacting the standardized innovation with sigma_e^2/H adds nothing over the raw residual.

factors.name: Speed-of-Adjustment-Gated Sector Error-Correction Term
factors.description: For each stock, rolling causal OLS of log close on a cap-weighted sector log-price level gives a standardized error-correction term z; a second rolling regression of the stock's bar return on lagged z gives its adjustment speed phi_i, while a mirror regression of the sector-level return on lagged z gives the reverse-causality loading psi_i. The factor is the expected 6-bar correction, -(1-(1+phi_i)^6)*z_i, kept only where the relation is stable (|1+phi_i|<1) and where own-adjustment dominates the reverse channel (|phi_i|>|psi_i|), then cross-sectionally demeaned within sector.
factors.trading_idea: The Nigeria APT/VECM paper's real object of interest is not the macro variables themselves but the *error-correction machinery*: a cointegrating level relation, a per-equation speed of adjustment (phi), and a direction-of-causality test showing that some series adjust to the system while others push it (ROA drove EXCH, not the reverse). Ported to 10-second equity bars, each stock's log price is cointegrated with a cap-weighted log-price level of its own GICS sector; the residual is a disequilibrium (ECT) that liquidity providers close over seconds. The edge is not the raw residual (over-mined pairs reversion) but conditioning it on a causally-estimated, per-name adjustment speed plus a reverse-causality gate: names that historically snap back to their sector get full weight, names whose disequilibrium instead drags the sector level (informed leaders, index/ETF-driven flow) get zero or suppressed weight, so we stop fading genuine information and only fade transient inventory pressure. Falsifiable: if the trailing-window phi has no out-of-sample stability, the gated signal will not beat the ungated residual, and if leaders were not being wrongly faded, the reverse-causality gate would add nothing.

factors.name: Equity-Credit Hazard Intensity Carry (volume-clock path residual)
factors.description: Builds lambda_it = fragility_i * exp(kappa * volatility-normalised drawdown of close vs a rolling anchor), where fragility_i is a bounded cross-sectional composite of point-in-time leverage/coverage/liquidity/accrual fields (debtToEquity, debtToAssets, netDebtToEbitda, -interestCoverage, -cashRatio, -currentRatio, -incomeQuality); integrates lambda over a ~30-minute window using traded volume as the business-time increment to get the hazard process Gamma_it, then cross-sectionally residualises Gamma against window log return, realized vol, log marketCap and log turnover and z-scores the residual (positive = long the unpaid survival premium).
factors.trading_idea: In the equity-credit reduced-form setup of Qiao & Yao, the pre-default stock has risk-neutral drift (r + lambda(S,t)) and lambda is an increasing, convex function of how far equity has fallen — so a fragile name whose price has been sitting in a drawdown must earn a visible per-bar compensation for jump-to-default risk conditional on survival. Because the compensation is an integral of a convex function of the price path (not a function of the endpoint), two names with identical 30-minute returns accumulate different hazard: the one that spent more trade-weighted time deep in drawdown owes more carry. I harvest that by building a state-dependent intensity from fundamental fragility times a convex drawdown elasticity, integrating it on a volume (business-time) clock, and stripping out the parts explainable by simple endpoint return, realized vol, size and turnover — the residual is the unpaid survival premium, expected to be earned as positive drift over the next minute. This is falsified if residual accumulated hazard predicts *negative* forward returns (i.e. flight-from-fragility / continuation dominates the compensation); it should persist because intraday liquidity providers price fragile, jumpy names by widening spreads rather than by continuously paying the hazard drift, and slow-moving credit-aware capital does not trade at 10-second resolution.

factors.name: Directional Queue-Depletion Hazard Race (ask vs bid resilience asymmetry)
factors.description: Over a rolling window, split bars by the sign of (close-open), attribute bar volume to that side, and estimate side-specific inverse depths lambda_up = sum(positive mid moves)/sum(up-bar volume) and lambda_dn = sum(|negative mid moves|)/sum(down-bar volume); the signal is the normalized race imbalance (lambda_up - lambda_dn)/(lambda_up + lambda_dn), computed only from trade-driven (above-median-volume) bars and scaled by the trade-driven share of total directional travel, then cross-sectionally standardized.
factors.trading_idea: Cont-Stoikov-Talreja show the next mid-price move is decided by a race between the bid and ask queues to hit zero, so the direction odds are governed by each side's depletion hazard per unit of incoming order flow, not by the recent price path itself. From 10-second bars we cannot see queue sizes, but we can infer each side's *inverse depth* separately: how much mid-price travel one unit of volume buys on up-bars versus down-bars. A name whose ask queue gives way cheaply (large mid move per share on up-bars) while its bid absorbs volume without moving (small move per share on down-bars) has an asymmetric race in favour of further up-moves over the next few queue lifetimes, even if its net recent return is negative — so this is explicitly orthogonal to signed momentum/reversal. The model's cancellation term (theta*x, rate proportional to queue size) also implies that depletion achieved with almost no trading is cancellation-driven and gets refilled at rate lambda, so those moves should be discounted / treated as reverting; the resiliency gate encodes that. Falsifier: if the up/down inverse-depth spread adds nothing beyond the sign of cumulative return, or predicts reversal rather than continuation, the mechanism is dead. The other side is market makers who quote asymmetric depth to manage inventory; the edge persists because queue shape is unobservable to anyone trading off bars and depth asymmetry decays only over minutes.

factors.name: Inter-Event Duration Tail Regime & Aging-Hazard Gate on Last Price Move
factors.description: For each ticker, build the causal series of inter-event durations (bars between mid-price changes exceeding a small rolling-quantile threshold) over a ~1-hour trailing window, fit a Weibull/Pareto-type duration law (shape from coefficient-of-variation plus a Hill/log-survival tail index), evaluate the conditional hazard at the current elapsed time since the last event relative to the unconditional rate, and multiply the vol-scaled signed size of the last price move by tanh(log hazard ratio) so that fast-clearing clocks give continuation and aging/stale clocks give reversal; the result is cross-sectionally demeaned and ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Cappellini & Ferraris show that in a continuous double auction the pending/inter-event waiting-time law is the market's structural fingerprint: bulk durations look exponential (memoryless, queue cleanly cleared) while the tail is a power law (aging, orders sitting unexecuted). That distinction has a direct trading implication that is almost never exploited: whether the *last* mid-price move is information (and continues) or a queue-clearing accident (and reverts) depends on the hazard regime of the name's event clock, not on the move itself. In a fast-clearing, memoryless/self-exciting clock the next execution is imminent and same-signed flow persists over the next few bars; in an aging, heavy-tailed clock the elapsed silence since the last move signals a thin, stale book where the move was one lonely market order and the resting opposite-side queue pulls the mid back. The trade is against liquidity demanders who read stale mid moves in slow-clearing names as signal; it persists because measuring the *shape* of a name's duration law (not just its mean) requires per-name causal estimation that slow-moving, cross-sectionally-standardised risk models never carry.

factors.name: Fallen-Angel Downside Semi-Beta Dislocation
factors.description: Estimates rolling upside/downside semi-betas of each name to an equal-weighted market factor of 10s log returns, forms the downside-minus-upside convexity gap and the recent down-tick excess loss relative to the elasticity implied by the firm's own debt-to-(debt+marketCap), then signs that dislocation by a cross-sectional 'fallen-angel' credit-quality score (interestCoverage, netDebtToEbitda, freeCashFlowYield, cashRatio, incomeQuality, debtToAssets) so the signal is long over-punished solvent-levered names and short under-punished fragile-levered names.
factors.trading_idea: Milken's core insight was that the market systematically overprices the cost of leverage-related distress and that 'fallen angels' — heavily levered names with real asset and cash-flow backing — are indiscriminately dumped by mandate- and rating-constrained holders. The 10-second analogue: equity of a levered firm is a call on firm value, so during down-ticks of the market factor, high-debt names get sold with an amplified (convex) elasticity by liquidity-demanding, risk-limit-driven flow that cannot distinguish leverage from credit quality. When a name's realized DOWNSIDE semi-beta overshoot exceeds what its own balance-sheet leverage elasticity justifies, and the balance sheet is in fact cash-flow-solvent (high interest coverage, low net-debt/EBITDA, strong FCF yield and cash ratio), the excess drawdown is a transient liquidity discount that reverts within roughly a minute; the mirror case — fragile-balance-sheet names that did NOT sell off as much as their leverage implies — is the short leg. The factor dies if the post-overshoot drift is continuation, or if the reversion strength is invariant to the fundamental credit-quality interaction (i.e., it is just plain beta-residual reversal).

factors.name: Dropout-Pooled Impulse Fragility (Max vs. Probabilistic-Weighted Pooling)
factors.description: Over a rolling window (~30 bars) builds two non-negative activation channels per name, volume-participation-weighted up-moves and down-moves; for each channel it computes the max-pool M and the dropout probabilistic-weighted pool P = sum_i p*(1-p)^(n-i)*a_(i) over sorted activations (p≈0.5), forms a fragility index F=(M-P)/(M+eps), and outputs the cross-sectional rank of [F-·M- − F+·M+] (fragile one-bar spikes fade) plus a smaller-weighted corroborated-pressure continuation term [(1−F+)·P+ − (1−F-)·P-].
factors.trading_idea: Wu & Gu show that max-pooling under dropout is really a draw from a multinomial over the *sorted* activations in a pooling region, so the robust test-time statistic is a geometrically-weighted blend of order statistics rather than the raw max — the gap between the two measures how much a pooling region's signal rests on a single, non-corroborated unit. Mapping this to a short rolling window of directional trade impulses: if the window's largest up-pressure bar dwarfs its 2nd/3rd largest (large max-vs-probabilistic-pool gap), the move was one liquidity-demanding sweep against a thin book, and market makers replenishing depth push price back; if the pressure is spread across several bars (small gap), it is corroborated informed flow and tends to persist. The other side is the impatient sweeper (or a stop cascade / iceberg slice) paying for immediacy; the edge persists because absorbing and re-quoting after a sweep is inventory- and latency-constrained, so replenishment is not instantaneous. Falsifier: if the fragility gate carries no incremental information over the raw signed impulse magnitude — i.e. concentrated and dispersed spikes of equal size revert identically at 6 bars — the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Cap/Turnover-Residualized Hill Tail Exponent Gate on Price Impulses
factors.description: Estimates a causal rolling Hill tail exponent of standardized 10s log returns per ticker (both tails, |r| above the in-window 90th percentile), cross-sectionally residualizes it on log(marketCap), log(rolling turnover = dollar volume / marketCap) and log realized volatility, then multiplies the negative of that residual's cross-sectional z-score by the z-scored recent short-window price impulse, yielding continuation for thin-tailed and reversal for fat-tailed names.
factors.trading_idea: Mu & Zhou show the power-law tail exponent of intraday returns is not universal: it falls (tails fatten) with turnover rate and rises with market capitalization. That means each name has a *predicted* tail thickness given its size and trading intensity, and the deviation from that prediction is informative about which mechanism is generating its current large moves. When a stock's live tail exponent is much fatter than its size/turnover peer group implies, its jumps are dominated by transient liquidity shortage (Farmer et al.'s channel) rather than information, so the latest impulse should partially retrace; when its tails are anomalously thin (near-Gaussian, well-supplied book) a same-sized impulse is more likely order-flow/information driven and continues. The signal therefore signs the last impulse by the tail-fatness residual: reversal on fragile-tail names, continuation on thin-tail names. It dies if the interaction term carries no incremental IC over unconditional short-horizon reversal, or if the tail residual is purely a proxy for realized volatility (which is orthogonalized out).

factors.name: Asymmetric Liquidity-Vacuum × Self-Excited Jump Hazard
factors.description: For each name, form causal rolling sums of upper and lower bar shadows and of volume over ~30 bars, build a signed depth-elasticity asymmetry (sum(U)-sum(D))/(sum(U)+sum(D)), scale it by an own-history-normalised total illiquidity level (sum(U)+sum(D))/sum(volume), and multiply by an exponentially-decayed self-excited jump-hazard count of bars whose |return| exceeded c times a bipower-variation local vol estimate; the product is cross-sectionally ranked/demeaned each bar.
factors.trading_idea: Makinen et al. show that the minute before a mid-price jump the book becomes *one-sidedly* thin: market makers pull quotes on the side they fear being picked off on, so tiny volumes move the mid a long way on that side only, and jump arrivals cluster in time (self-excitation). With only bars we can still measure this: the failed-excursion shadows U = high - max(open,close) and D = min(open,close) - low are how far the mid travelled per unit of executed volume on each side, so U/volume vs D/volume is a direct bar-level proxy for one-sided depth elasticity, and it is only informative when the overall book is thin (high total shadow per unit volume). The paper concluded jump *direction* was unpredictable from its 144 generic features; the falsifiable claim here is that the sign of the depth-elasticity asymmetry, gated on an elevated Hawkes-style jump hazard, does carry direction over the next ~1 minute, because the vacuum side is where the next liquidity-demanding order will walk the book. Who is on the other side: liquidity providers who have withdrawn (they are not competing) and slow, size-insensitive liquidity takers; the edge persists because trading it requires paying the same thin-book impact and is capacity-limited, so slow capital cannot arbitrage it away.

factors.name: Fundamental Knowledge-Graph Diffusion Lag Catch-Up
factors.description: Builds a row-normalised multi-relational adjacency over tickers from point-in-time fundamental attribute co-membership (sector, industry, evToEbitda / grossMargin / debtToAssets / assetTurnover / marketCap rank buckets), diffuses recent bar log-returns through it (one-hop plus a damped two-hop term, self excluded), fits a shrunk causal rolling regression of each name's own return on its lagged graph-diffused peer return to get a per-name loading, and outputs the volume-conviction-scaled, cross-sectionally z-scored gap between the loading-implied move and the stock's own realised move over the same short window.
factors.trading_idea: The KGE paper's core claim is that forecasting improves when a *conceptual* graph over variables (built from domain knowledge, not learned from price data) is injected as a propagation structure, and then given a dynamic, learnable loading. Mapped to equities: the true peer network of a stock is not just its GICS sector but a multi-relational graph over point-in-time fundamental characteristics (sector/industry, valuation multiple bucket, gross-margin bucket, leverage bucket, asset-turnover bucket, size bucket). Order flow that hits one node of such a graph is priced instantly in the traded name but diffuses only slowly to fundamentally-linked names, because almost nobody hedges or arbitrages 'same-margin/same-leverage/same-multiple' baskets — the standard vehicles are single names and sector ETFs, so these non-obvious edges have no fast-moving capital policing them. The factor therefore measures how far a stock has lagged the diffusion-weighted move of its knowledge-graph neighbourhood over the last few minutes, scaled by a causally-estimated, name-specific loading (the 'dynamic KGE' analog), and predicts catch-up over the next 6 bars. It dies if the rolling loadings estimated on trailing data are unstable/near-zero out of sample, or if all the signal collapses into the plain same-sector mean, which is the natural control.

factors.name: Codifference Yule-Walker Projection with Selective-Memory Jump Gate
factors.description: Per ticker, robustly rescale 10s log-returns by their rolling mean absolute deviation, estimate the normalized autocodifference rho_k = CD_k/CD_0 at lags 1..K from the rolling empirical characteristic function (CD(X,Y) = -logRe(Phi_X(1)) - logRe(Phi_Y(-1)) + logRe(Phi_{X-Y}(1))), solve the codifference-Toeplitz (Yule-Walker-style) system for projection weights and form a one-step forecast; a tail-dominance gate (rolling max|z| share of total |z| plus a characteristic-function slope estimate of alpha) blends this forecast with a decayed anti-jump drift term in the selective-memory regime, and the blended forecast is cross-sectionally standardized.
factors.trading_idea: Ten-second mid-return series are strongly leptokurtic, so the covariance-based linear predictors that most short-horizon reversal models implicitly assume are badly calibrated: under alpha-stable increments the second moment is (near-)undefined and the serial dependence should instead be measured by the codifference, which is built from the empirical characteristic function (Garcin, Sawaya & Valade 2025). We therefore build a causal one-step-ahead linear projection whose Toeplitz system uses the *autocodifference* rather than the autocovariance, and — crucially — we exploit the paper's newly identified fourth dependence regime: when the tail index is small and a few very large increments dominate the estimation window, the usual alternating (antipersistent) prediction inverts into a locally persistent, gradually decaying drift away from the jump. Edge: Gaussian-calibrated reversal engines over-predict immediate mean reversion right after a dominant tick-level jump and under-predict the slow, monotone recovery drift that follows it, so a signal that switches between the two regimes should earn the residual. Falsification test: if a covariance-Yule-Walker predictor with the same lag depth and the same jump gate reproduces the IC, the alpha-stable/codifference machinery adds nothing and the idea dies.

factors.name: Capital-Dependent Knowledge Multiplier Gated Impulse Persistence
factors.description: Estimates a per-name endogenous-knowledge feedback coefficient µ = (productivity growth: asset-turnover / revenue-per-asset and gross-margin improvement, boosted by rdToRevenue and intangiblesToAssets) divided by capital growth (assetGrowth / PPE-investedCapital growth), winsorized and mapped to the amplification multiplier 1/(1-µ) and cross-sectionally centered; this gate is multiplied by a volatility-normalized, volume-weighted short-run signed price impulse over the last few 10-second bars, so the factor forecasts continuation for high-multiplier names and reversal for low-multiplier names.
factors.trading_idea: Szydlowski & Krawiec's model makes knowledge growth endogenous in capital accumulation (A/A = g + µ K/K), so an economy's response to an investment impulse is amplified by the feedback multiplier 1/(1-µ): with high µ a shock compounds, with µ≈0 it dies out at the exogenous rate. I map µ to a firm-level, point-in-time estimate of how much *productivity* (knowledge) a firm extracts per unit of *capital* it puts to work — productivity growth (revenue-per-asset / asset-turnover and margin gains, tilted by R&D and intangible intensity) divided by contemporaneous balance-sheet capital growth. The trading claim is that this fundamental feedback coefficient governs how intraday order-flow impulses resolve: in high-µ 'compounder' names, informed/news-driven flow is self-reinforcing and short-run price impulses continue over the next minute, whereas in low-µ capital-sinks (heavy investment with no productivity payoff, the classic asset-growth losers) the same impulses are inventory/liquidity noise and mean-revert. The counterparty is a horizon-mismatched intraday liquidity provider who treats every 10-second impulse as uninformative regardless of the issuer's underlying growth feedback; the edge persists because nobody conditions second-scale flow on quarterly capital-productivity elasticities. It is killed if high-µ names show the same or stronger 6-bar reversal as low-µ names, i.e. if the interaction term's IC is indistinguishable from the unconditional impulse-reversal term.

factors.name: Rare-Transition HMM Drift Decode with Filtering-Entropy Gate
factors.description: Per ticker, run a causal log-domain forward (filtering) recursion of a 3-state hidden Markov model on volatility-standardized 10s close-to-close returns, with a rare-transition generator P = I + pA (p ~ 0.02, i.e. expected regime length ~50 bars) and Gaussian emissions with means {-mu,0,+mu} in sigma units; the raw signal is the posterior drift mean E[state_t] multiplied by a confidence gate (1 - H_t/log 3, where H_t is the posterior entropy, the paper's h(X|Y) proxy) and by a freshness weight exp(-age_t/tau) where age_t is bars since the posterior argmax last flipped, then cross-sectionally demeaned and ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Peres & Quas show that when a latent Markov state switches rarely and is observed through a noisy channel, the state is almost perfectly recoverable except in a short window around each switch, where the conditional entropy h(X|Y) concentrates; causal filtering (no future data) pays an extra Cp|log p| recognition lag exactly at those switch epochs. Ten-second mid-price returns are a textbook noisy channel on a rarely-switching latent drift state (a persistent directional imbalance from a parent order or a repriced quote). The tradable inefficiency is the causal-filtering lag: once the online posterior has *just* resolved onto a new drift state with low entropy, most participants running symmetric/EMA smoothers are still averaging over the stale regime, so the decoded drift continues for a handful of bars. Falsification: if the signal's IC is unchanged after removing the entropy gate and the flip-freshness weight (i.e. it is just signed smoothed return), or if freshly-flipped names mean-revert rather than continue, the mechanism is wrong.

factors.name: Operational-Clock Hurst Gated by Trap-Release Speed
factors.description: For each stock, build a causal operational clock from activity (volume relative to its trailing norm, with frozen-price/zero-volume bars contributing ~0 clock time), resample the log-price path onto an equally spaced grid of this clock, estimate a local Hurst/variance-ratio exponent H_op from the resampled increments, and emit signal = (H_op - 0.5) x standardized last operational increment x current clock speed (trap-release gate), sector-neutralised and cross-sectionally z-scored.
factors.trading_idea: Shokrollahi & Magdziarz model prices as fractional Brownian motion run on an inverse alpha-stable clock: the asset is literally motionless during heavy-tailed trapping periods, and the fBm's long memory (H>1/2) lives in *operational* time, not calendar time. The practical consequence is that calendar-time trend/reversal estimators are contaminated by trapping: the same price path looks memoryless in wall-clock seconds and strongly persistent (or anti-persistent) once you strip out the frozen intervals. I therefore estimate each name's persistence exponent on a volume/event-subordinated clock and only act when its subordinator is currently *running* (a trap has just released), because a forecast of the next operational increment cannot be realised inside 6 calendar bars while the name is trapped. Falsifiable: if operational-time variance ratios are indistinguishable from 1, or if conditioning on clock speed adds nothing above the raw calendar-time signal, the factor is dead. The edge persists because most systematic participants and execution algos measure trend and reversal on fixed calendar grids, so they systematically mis-weight quiet, sparsely-traded names relative to names whose activity clock is currently accelerating.

factors.name: AR(1) Barrier-Survival Sampling Clock with Event-Sparsity Gate
factors.description: Per ticker, fits a rolling AR(1) on the volatility-normalised deviation of close from its local mean, computes analytic upper- and lower-barrier survival probabilities (Markov product of Gaussian conditional in-band probabilities) to get expected bars-to-crossing on each side, forms the imminence asymmetry 1/tau_up - 1/tau_down, and multiplies it by a cross-sectionally ranked event-sparsity gate (sign-flipping in the recent count of realised band crossings), then cross-sectionally standardises.
factors.trading_idea: Kalfa et al. derive an optimal non-uniform sampling clock for a scalar AR(p) sensor: given the current state, they compute the two-sided barrier survival probability psi_k = prod_i P(x_i in (l,u) | x_{i-1} in (l,u)) and sample just before the missed-detection budget is exhausted, so the clock accelerates as a threshold crossing becomes imminent. Applied to prices, this yields a model-based, asymmetric time-to-barrier hazard for each name (how soon the mean-reverting deviation is expected to pierce its upper vs lower band) rather than a raw distance-to-high/low. Their second insight is that the value of a detected event scales with its rarity (compression rate is driven by the rate of innovation of interesting patterns): a barrier crossing in a name whose recent 'semantic' event stream has been idle is genuine information and tends to be followed by continuation from liquidity-seeking flow, whereas in a name that has been oscillating across its bands the crossing is noise and mean-reverts. The edge exists because market makers price distance-to-extreme, not the state-dependent crossing hazard conditional on mean-reversion speed and volatility, and because the sparse-event names are exactly where inventory-constrained liquidity providers step back. It is killed if the sign of the interaction (sparse -> continuation, frequent -> reversion) does not flip: a monotone response to imminence alone would mean this is just a rebranded breakout/reversal factor.

factors.name: RFSV Unforecastable Log-Volatility Shock, Leverage-Signed
factors.description: For each name, builds a per-bar spot-vol proxy from the OHLC range (Garman-Klass style, log-transformed), estimates the local Hurst exponent H by regressing log of the q=1,2 structure functions of log-vol increments on log lag over a rolling window, forms the fBm conditional-expectation forecast of current log-vol from lagged log-vol with the Nuzman-Poor kernel cos(Hp)/p * (t-s+D)^-1 (t-s)^-(H+1/2), and takes the standardized residual (realized minus rough forecast) as the unforecastable vol shock; the factor is the cross-sectional rank of minus (standardized recent 6-bar return) x (residual z-score), damped by a (0.5 - H) roughness weight so the reversal branch loads where the vol path is genuinely rough.
factors.trading_idea: Rough volatility (Gatheral-Jaisson-Rosenbaum; confirmed on option data by Livieri et al.) says log-spot-volatility behaves like fBm with H well below 1/2, which means most of the log-vol path IS forecastable from a long, power-law-weighted history via the fBm (Nuzman-Poor) prediction kernel, and only a small residual is a genuine surprise. My claim is that the *forecastable* part of a vol expansion is information/scheduled-flow driven and price moves that accompany it persist, while the *unforecastable* rough residual is inventory/liquidity noise: a market maker being run over, an iceberg sweep, a momentary depth vacuum. Hence a 1-minute price move accompanied by a large positive rough-vol residual should revert (liquidity providers reload, mid snaps back), whereas the same move with a residual below the roughness-implied forecast is an orderly, informed drift that continues. Who is on the other side: short-horizon liquidity providers and momentum-chasing takers who cannot decompose realized vol into predictable-persistent versus surprise components in real time; the edge persists because the decomposition requires a per-name Hurst estimate and a long causal kernel, and the pay-off (a few bps over 60s) is only harvestable by inventory-tolerant participants.

factors.name: Winner's-Curse-Corrected CUSUM Flow Regime Shift vs. Unpriced Drift
factors.description: Over a rolling 90-bar window of tick-rule signed volume per name, computes the mean-and-variance likelihood-ratio CUSUM path with a minimum segment length (k=10), an autocorrelation-inflated null threshold, and a MAD-based scale estimate; takes tau-hat = argmax LR, shrinks the post-minus-pre flow jump by a winner's-curse penalty lambda*sigma*sqrt(1/tau + 1/(n-tau)), weights it by changepoint freshness exp(-(n-tau)/h) and by LR exceeding the inflated threshold, then subtracts the volatility-normalised price move already realised since tau-hat; the residual 'unpriced flow re-basing' is cross-sectionally demeaned and ranked.
factors.trading_idea: A parent order or informed participant switching on produces a genuine step change in the *level* of signed trade flow, not a smooth trend — exactly the change-in-mean object the likelihood-ratio/CUSUM machinery is built to localise (Fearnhead & Fryzlewicz, Ch. 'Detecting A Single Change-point'). The paper's three practical warnings are the alpha: (i) false detections pile up at the window boundaries unless a minimum segment length is imposed, (ii) autocorrelated noise inflates the CUSUM null so the threshold must be scaled by sqrt((1+rho1)/(1-rho1)) — and 10s signed flow is strongly autocorrelated, so naive detectors mostly fire on noise, and (iii) the naive post-detection jump estimate suffers a winner's curse and must be shrunk. Applying all three corrections isolates the small set of names where flow has genuinely re-based; if price has *not yet* moved commensurately since the estimated changepoint, the remaining child orders should push it over the next minute. The trade is against liquidity providers and passive queue-sitters who mean-revert against flow they have not yet recognised as persistent; it persists because detecting a level shift in a heavy-tailed, autocorrelated flow series in real time is statistically hard and most participants use simple rolling averages that lag the break. Falsifier: if the debiased jump size carries no more forward information than a plain rolling flow imbalance, or if the edge is entirely captured by the already-realised return since tau-hat, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Marked-Hawkes Residual Excitation & Fill-Clock Flow Switch
factors.description: Per ticker on a rolling window, treat bar volume as marked point-process increments: estimate the branching ratio and power-law kernel exponent from the multi-scale Fano factor (Var(L_T)/E[L_T] versus aggregation T), form the mark-shape statistic as the empirical Laplace transform / dispersion of normalized bar marks, then compute the model-implied expected additional volume over the next 6 bars (kernel convolution of past marks plus the renewal self-generation term) divided by the volume realized over the last 6 bars — a 'residual excitation' fill clock. The factor is the exponentially weighted signed flow direction (sign(close-open) x normalized volume) multiplied by tanh of the centred residual-excitation ratio and scaled by the heavy-mark statistic, cross-sectionally demeaned and ranked, so it goes with the flow for young heavy-mark clusters and against it for exhausted thin-mark ones.
factors.trading_idea: Gao-Zhou-Zhu show that for a marked Hawkes execution process the future filled volume of a resting order depends on (i) how much of the self-excited cluster is still ahead (the renewal term with branching ratio and kernel shape) and (ii) the whole distribution of trade marks, not just their mean — fatter-tailed marks make complete fills slower, so a large parent order stays in the market far longer. Translating this to a lit tape: a directional volume burst is worth chasing only when the point-process state implies the cluster is young (large expected residual excitation) and marks are heavy-tailed, because then the metaorder behind it still has size left to execute; when the estimated excitation is already exhausted and marks are thin/homogeneous the burst was exogenous and market makers' refills produce reversion instead. The counterparty is the short-horizon reversal / liquidity-provision crowd that leans against every flow burst indiscriminately, and the edge persists because distinguishing an unfinished endogenous cluster from a one-off print requires estimating branching ratio, kernel decay and mark-Laplace shape rather than reading a volume z-score. It is falsified if the interaction with residual excitation and mark shape adds nothing over raw signed-flow imbalance.

factors.name: Singular-Kernel Volterra Signature Area (level-1 × level-2 persistence)
factors.description: Per ticker over a rolling window, builds the causal singular-kernel Volterra path z1_t = sum_s (t-s+1)^-gamma * r_s (r = vol-standardised log return) and the Ito level-2 area z2_t = sum_r (t-r+1)^-gamma * m_r * r_r with inner memory m_r = sum_{u<r} (r-u+1)^-gamma * r_u; the signal is the directional level-1 path multiplied by a bounded, kernel-RV-normalised persistence score (z2 - 0.5*z1^2)/(kernel-weighted realized variance), optionally shrunk by the near-diagonal freshness term z1^{tau=t} - z1^{tau=t+6}, then cross-sectionally demeaned/ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Harang–Tindel–Wang construct a two-level Volterra signature (z1, z2) for a path driven by a singular memory kernel k(t,s)~|t-s|^-gamma, where the second level is a convolution-type Levy area that must be taken in the Ito (left-point) sense because the Stratonovich correction diverges under kernel singularity. Read financially: z1 is a power-law (rough, long-memory) weighted accumulation of recent order-flow-driven returns, and the Ito area z2 measures whether new increments keep arriving *aligned* with their own kernel-weighted memory (endogenous self-excitation, genuine continuation) or systematically *against* it (transient impact being unwound by market makers). Direction alone (z1) is over-mined; the edge is the interaction — the same accumulated push should continue over the next minute when the area is positive (self-reinforcing flow from slow order slicing) and revert when the area is negative (anti-persistent, impact-driven), because liquidity suppliers absorb and recycle uninformed marketable flow. It is falsified if z1 alone carries the same forward IC as the sign-conditioned product, or if the area term's conditioning IC is flat across its own cross-sectional quantiles.

factors.name: Signed Peer-Graph Dislocation with Hidden-Node Column-Sparsity Gate
factors.description: On a rolling window of 10-second log returns (vol-standardized), computes the correlation matrix, removes the top-K eigen-components as hidden nodes, forms a per-name top-m sparse signed graph from the residual correlations (W+ = positive part, W- = negative part), predicts each name's recent short-horizon standardized move as the signed-weighted consensus of its peers, and returns the negative of the dislocation (own move minus signed consensus), multiplied by a gate that shrinks names with anomalously high hidden-node eigen-loading, then cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: SGL-HNCS argues that an observed correlation structure is the sum of a genuine signed peer graph (positive edges = co-movement/smooth signal, negative edges = anti-movement/substitution) plus a low-rank, column-sparse contamination from hidden nodes that are never observed. In equity microstructure the hidden nodes are the market/sector factors and non-sampled instruments (ETFs, futures, off-universe names): a name's short-run deviation from its peers is only tradable mean-reversion if it is NOT explained by those hidden drivers. So I strip the top eigen-components (hidden nodes) from the rolling correlation matrix, build a sparse SIGNED peer graph from the residual, measure each name's graph total-variation dislocation (its own recent move minus the signed-smooth consensus of its positive peers net of its negative peers), and shrink the signal for names whose hidden-node loading column-norm is anomalously large. The other side is impatient uninformed flow hitting one leg of a tight peer cluster; market makers absorb it and re-align over seconds, but they will not lean against a name whose move is really a hidden common-factor shock — which is exactly what the column-sparsity gate encodes. Falsifiable: if the negative-edge term carries no incremental IC over a positive-only correlation consensus, or if high-hidden-loading names revert identically to low-hidden-loading ones, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Lévy-Area Follower Score × Untraded-Tape Peer Spillover
factors.description: For each name, compute the discrete Lévy area between its volatility-scaled cumulative return path and its sector peers' (ex-self) composite path over a rolling window, normalised to a bounded lead(+)/lag(−) leadership score; take the follower part of that score, multiply it by the peers' recent volatility-scaled drift and by a gate measuring peer-volume surge minus own-volume surge, then demean/rank cross-sectionally within sector.
factors.trading_idea: Li & Ferreira use the second-level signature (Lévy area) of a pair of volatility-scaled price paths to decide, without assuming a fixed lag, which market leads and which follows, then push the leaders' trend onto the followers. Intraday the analogous object is each name versus its own sector's composite path: names whose Lévy area against the peer composite is negative are structurally reacting to sector information late, and those names should keep drifting in the direction the peer composite has just moved. The edge should be strongest where the follower's own tape has not yet woken up — low own-bar volume relative to a surge in peer volume means the information event has hit the sector but not yet been intermediated in this name, so the price adjustment is still pending rather than already paid away. The counterparty is a liquidity provider / slow quote-updater in the less-actively-traded follower, and the inefficiency survives because cross-name monitoring capacity is finite and concentrated in the highly traded leaders. Falsifiable: if the negative-Lévy-area group shows no more peer-trend continuation than the positive group, or if the volume-asymmetry gate adds nothing, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Self-Excited Chatter Band: Informative-Packet Phase Extrapolation
factors.description: On a causal rolling window of market-mode-removed log mid returns, run a level-3 wavelet-packet decomposition, select the 'informative packet' as the non-trend band maximising energy-ratio x narrowbandness (Q-factor from the band's one-step autocorrelation), reconstruct that band, estimate its instantaneous amplitude/frequency/phase, and output the harmonically extrapolated cumulative displacement over the next 6 bars — multiplied by a chatter gate (band energy ratio and crest factor high, impulse/kurtosis and volume-spike contamination low) and cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Yesilli-Khasawneh-Otto detect machine-tool chatter by decomposing a vibration signal into dyadic bands and keeping the *informative* packet — the narrowband, self-excited eigenmode — explicitly rejecting both the highest-energy low-frequency content (the 'trend') and the broadband impulse-like events ('chip breakage', tagged 'unknown'), and distinguishing self-excited chatter from *forced* vibration at the spindle-rotation frequency. Order books chatter in the same sense: inventory-cycling market makers, passive-then-aggressive execution schedulers and quote-matching bots create idiosyncratic limit-cycle ringing in mid-price at a stock-specific timescale, whereas market-wide oscillations are the forced mode and news prints are the impulse class. If a name is currently in a chattering regime, the oscillation is a limit cycle with real phase persistence, so the next-60-second displacement is predictable by extrapolating the reconstructed mode's phase — an edge that survives because it is capacity-limited, name-specific, and invisible to anyone looking at raw returns (where the mode is buried under trend, market beta and jump noise). It dies if the dominant idiosyncratic band-limited component has no autocorrelation of phase beyond one bar, or if the chatter gate fails to separate ringing regimes from impulse regimes.

factors.name: RMT Noise-Subspace Shock with Network-Redundancy Sign Switch
factors.description: On a rolling window of 10-second log returns, eigendecompose the cross-sectional correlation matrix, define the market subspace as the eigenvalues exceeding the Marchenko-Pastur edge (rescaled by the top eigenvalue), project out that subspace to get each name's noise-subspace residual shock over the last few bars, then multiply the standardized residual by a centered, cross-sectionally ranked weight built from the Onnela-weighted local clustering coefficient (and degree/eigenvector centrality) of the thresholded market-mode graph, so redundant hub-embedded names get a reversal sign and low-clustering bridge names a continuation sign, with the whole signal scaled by the top eigenvalue's explained-variance share.
factors.trading_idea: Achitouv shows that the return correlation matrix splits cleanly into a few collective 'market modes' (eigenvalues above the rescaled Marchenko-Pastur edge, driven by a handful of high-eigenvector-centrality hubs) and a near-GBM 'noise' bulk, and that the *topology* of the filtered network — local (Onnela-weighted) clustering versus structural-hole position — differs sharply across names. My claim is that what happens next to a purely idiosyncratic shock depends on that topology, not on the shock's size: a name sitting inside a dense, redundant neighbourhood has many substitute instruments through which relative-value desks can immediately hedge and arbitrage a dislocation, so its noise-subspace shock mean-reverts within a minute; a high-degree but low-clustering 'bridge' name has no redundant hedge basket, so market makers widen rather than lean against it and its shock continues as genuine information diffusing between clusters. The trade is therefore a sign-switched residual: short the shock for redundant, densely-clustered names and ride it for bridge names, with the whole signal amplified when the top eigenvalue's variance share (the paper's coupling strength) is elevated, because tight coupling makes idiosyncratic deviations easier to arbitrage. Falsification: if the reversal/continuation coefficient on noise-subspace shocks is statistically indistinguishable across clustering-coefficient terciles once liquidity and volatility are controlled, the mechanism is dead and the factor collapses to plain reversal.

factors.name: Game-Theoretic Trust Coefficient on the Market's Implied Tick-Up Odds
factors.description: For each ticker, form a naive 'announced' up-tick probability p_t = logistic(z_t) from prior-bar close-location value and volume-weighted signed pressure, then fit online (exponentially-weighted, ridge-prior recursive IRLS using only data through t-1) the logistic model logit(p_hat_t) = beta_t*logit(p_t) + theta_t'c_t on the binary outcome x_t = 1{close_t > close_{t-1}}; the raw signal is the Kelly bet fraction nu_t = (p_hat_t - p_t)/(p_t(1-p_t)), multiplied by an evidence gate tanh(S_t'V_t^{-1}S_t / log det V_t) from the paper's SLLN bound and cross-sectionally demeaned/ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Kumon et al. show that a forecaster (the Japan Meteorological Agency) is beatable not because its forecasts are uninformative but because they are systematically shrunk toward 50%: the hindsight coefficient on the announced log-odds was beta ~ 1.5, so the skeptic profits by *amplifying* the forecaster's own signal. In a 10-second bar tape the analogous 'Forecaster' is the naive microstructure predictor everyone reads off the last bar (close-location within the bar range, signed volume pressure, run persistence); market makers who shade quotes and passive flow that leans against short-term pressure compress this predictor's realised hit-rate away from its face value, and the compression is not uniform across names or regimes. Running the paper's Bayesian logistic betting strategy per ticker gives a causally-estimated trust coefficient beta_t (amplify when beta_t>1, fade when beta_t<1) plus a Kelly bet fraction; the game-theoretic capital process supplies a built-in evidence gate so we only take the bet where accumulated miscalibration is statistically real. This is falsifiable: if the estimated beta_t hovers at 1 with theta_t ~ 0 and the capital-process statistic S'V^-1 S stays below log det V, the factor should have zero IC.

factors.name: Stability-Selected Sparse Tracking Basket Transmission Gap
factors.description: Every K bars, a sparse non-negative sector-capped replicating basket of the cap-weighted market return is estimated on a rolling window with stability selection (inclusion frequency across bootstrapped sub-windows as the weight, per the paper's 'count of holdings' weighting); each stock then gets a causal loading and R-squared on that basket, and the signal is the cross-sectionally ranked short-horizon gap (loading x cumulative basket return minus own cumulative return), gated up for names outside/weakly in the sparse support and for names with high basket explanatory power.
factors.trading_idea: Zhang (2023) shows a *sparse*, sector-capped, non-negative tracking portfolio can reproduce a broad benchmark, and — crucially — that selection *frequency* ('number of holdings') is a more robust weighting scheme than coefficient magnitude ('market cap of holdings'). Intraday the same object exists: at any moment a handful of high-turnover 'hub' names carry almost all of the common factor because basket/ETF and institutional program flow lands on them first, so they are the sparse support of the market return; the remaining names are *tracked* rather than tracking, and receive the same factor impulse with a delay of seconds. The factor builds that sparse support by stability selection (non-negative, per-name-capped, per-sector-capped greedy replication of the cap-weighted market return, repeated on bootstrapped sub-windows, weighting names by inclusion frequency), forms the basket return, and trades the gap between each stock's basket-implied return and its realized return — long the names whose loading says they owe the market a move they have not yet made. Who is on the other side: liquidity providers in the slow, non-support names who widen after hub moves; the edge persists because re-hedging the periphery is capacity-constrained and disclosure/execution of the true crowded basket is stale (the paper's central friction). It dies if the gap is driven by genuine idiosyncratic news, in which case high-gap names should continue to diverge rather than converge, and if the signal survives only in the sparse support names themselves (the opposite of the transmission story).

factors.name: Patch-Shape Basis Decomposition with Scale & Volume Context Gate
factors.description: For each ticker, the last 36 bars of close are split into 6 non-overlapping patches; patch means are z-normalized within the window to give a scale-free 6-dim shape vector, which is projected onto an orthonormal discrete basis (linear/slope, quadratic/curvature, Haar step, alternating Nyquist). The same patching is applied to volume to build a confirmation weight; the final cross-sectionally ranked score is +step*confirmation (persistence) minus unconfirmed step, minus the alternating component, all scaled by the window amplitude relative to the name's own longer-run amplitude (scale context re-injection).
factors.trading_idea: The time-series LLM paper's core engineering insight is that a path should be perceived as (i) non-overlapping normalized patches, (ii) a scale-free shape whose latent axes correspond to canonical characteristics (trend, level shift, oscillation, amplitude), and (iii) a magnitude context re-injected separately, with extra channels (multivariate signals) fed as tagged parallel streams. Applied to 10-second bars, this says the *same* recent price excursion has opposite forward implications depending on which shape axis carries it and whether the amplitude/volume context corroborates it: a genuine level-shift (step) patch accompanied by a coincident volume patch spike is informed repricing and persists over the next minute, whereas the identical step with flat volume is a liquidity/queue-depletion artefact and mean-reverts, and the high-frequency alternating (Nyquist) component is almost pure quote-bounce noise that always reverts. Market makers and short-horizon liquidity providers are on the other side: they must post continuously and cannot condition on the shape/volume interaction fast enough across the whole cross-section, so the mis-attribution of shape to information persists. It dies if step components revert regardless of volume confirmation, or if the alternating component shows continuation.

factors.name: Variable-Lag DTW Alignment Backlog Catch-Up
factors.description: For each name, over a rolling window (~180 bars) build the stock's cumulative log-price path and the volume-weighted cumulative log path of its sector peers (stock excluded), both scaled by window volatility, then run band-limited DTW (Sakoe-Chiba width δmax ≈ 12 bars) to get the warping path; retain (i) the emulation-direction score s(P) = mean sign of warp offsets, (ii) the endpoint lag Δ_T, (iii) the emulation gain β from regressing follower increments on the warp-reconstructed leader increments, and (iv) a variable-lag-vs-fixed-lag residual-variance gate (VL residual must beat both own-past and best fixed-lag residual). The signal is β × (leader cumulative return from t-Δ_T to t), gated to names with s(P) > 0, sufficient alignment similarity, and a passing VL gate, then cross-sectionally demeaned/ranked within sector.
factors.trading_idea: Amornbunchornvej et al. show that follower series track leaders with *time-varying* lags, so fixed-lag cross-correlation/Granger tests miss real lead-lag structure; the DTW warping path itself carries the two objects we care about: the direction of emulation (average sign of the warp offsets, s(P)) and the *current* lag at the endpoint of the window. If a stock's intraday price path is a low-distortion, positively-lagged emulation of its sector's volume-weighted path, then at time t the stock is still 'replaying' the leader's state from t-Δ_t, and the leader's move over (t-Δ_t, t] is a mechanically identifiable, not-yet-emulated backlog that the follower should traverse next. The other side of the trade is slow-reacting liquidity in the follower name (thin queues, index/basket flow hitting the liquid leaders first), and the edge persists because measuring elastic (not fixed) lag requires path alignment that standard lead-lag screens do not run; it would be falsified if backlog-scaled forecasts show no incremental IC over a plain fixed-lag sector-beta residual or if the sign of s(P) carries no information about which side leads.

factors.name: Second-Order Peer-Graph Flow with Velocity Damping on an Event Clock
factors.description: Builds a per-bar, sector-restricted proximity graph (edge active only when two names' volatility-normalised price displacements are within a cross-sectionally calibrated radius and both names have recent trade events), forms the second-order graph vector field a_i = -alpha*(L_G x)_i - beta*(L_G v)_i on displacement x and velocity v, and outputs the interaction-driven displacement 0.5*a_i*(h*dt_i)^2 integrated over each name's event-clock step dt_i, cross-sectionally standardised within sector.
factors.trading_idea: The GDE paper's decisive result is that a *second-order* graph ODE (state = position AND velocity, with a radius-activated, time-varying adjacency and a viscoelastic spring-drag interaction) extrapolates a networked system far better than either a first-order graph flow or a graph-blind ODE. Mapped to equities: a name's short-horizon relative price is a particle whose neighbours are same-sector peers that are *currently close* in normalised price-state space (the radius gate), and the force pulling it back has two components — an elastic term in the peer-relative dislocation level and a damping term in the peer-relative dislocation *velocity*. Relative-value market makers quote and hedge off peers that are presently co-moving, so a name separating fast from a tight peer cluster is absorbing liquidity-demanding flow that gets damped within seconds; the level term alone is the over-mined pairs-reversal, while the velocity-Laplacian (damping) term is the under-exploited conditioning. Following the paper's irregular-timestamp handling, the ODE is integrated over each name's own *event clock* (fraction of recent bars with actual trading), so illiquid, rarely-traded names get a shorter effective integration interval and a proportionally smaller forecast displacement. Falsifiable: if setting the damping coefficient beta to zero (or removing the radius gate so all sector peers are neighbours) leaves the IC unchanged, the mechanism is just repackaged peer reversal and the idea dies.

factors.name: GP Covariance-Break Persistence Flip (idiosyncratic GLRT gate)
factors.description: Per name, over a rolling window of 10s log returns split at its midpoint, fit AR(1)/exponential GP kernels (Yule-Walker) to the whole window and to each half, form the exact closed-form Toeplitz GLRT statistic 2L = r'Sigma^-1 r - r'Sigma_block^-1 r + ln(|Sigma|/|Sigma_block|), z-score it against its own trailing distribution and subtract the cross-sectional median (isolating idiosyncratic covariance breaks); the factor is this break confidence times tanh of the pre-to-post change in estimated persistence times the standardized post-break cumulative return, cross-sectionally demeaned — i.e. continuation when the path just became smoother, reversal when it just became choppier.
factors.trading_idea: Han et al. show that fitting one stationary kernel across a covariance structural break badly mis-states the smoothness (length-scale) of a path, and that a likelihood-ratio test on block-diagonal vs full covariance detects the break long before a Bayesian run-length filter does. At the 10-second scale the return autocovariance IS the microstructure regime: a high-persistence regime (long length-scale, positive lag-1 autocorrelation of mid returns) means order flow is being worked through the book and recent drift extends, whereas a low/negative-persistence regime means quote bouncing and inventory-driven noise, so the same recent move reverts. Most participants estimate one persistence parameter over a fixed lookback and therefore keep trading continuation just after the path has switched to choppy (and vice versa); the mispricing persists because re-estimating persistence in real time is a modelling cost, not an arbitrage capital cost. Falsifier: if the sign of (post-break minus pre-break) lag-1 persistence carries no interaction with the sign of the recent move, or if the effect is identical for market-wide breaks as for idiosyncratic ones, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: GARCH-Filtered Magnitude Long-Memory Continuation/Reversal Switch
factors.description: Per name, run a fixed-parameter causal GARCH(1,1)-style recursion on 10s log returns to get standardized residuals, take their absolute value (magnitude series), estimate a rolling detrended-fluctuation-analysis Hurst exponent H of that magnitude series over box scales ~8-64 bars, and multiply the cross-sectionally standardized recent 6-bar standardized-return impulse (amplitude-gated by current |residual| and bar volume) by tanh of the cross-sectionally demeaned excess memory (H - 0.5), so high residual memory implies continuation and low memory implies reversal.
factors.trading_idea: Oh, Kim & Eom show that at high frequency the long memory of the |return| (magnitude) series is only partially explained by GARCH-type conditional heteroskedasticity: after GARCH(1,1) filtering, daily volatility memory collapses to H~0.5 but intraday volatility memory survives at H~0.6-0.65. That surviving memory is the footprint of genuinely endogenous, self-exciting activity (order-splitting, herding, slow information diffusion) rather than a mechanically decaying variance level, and it is exactly the state in which a signed price impulse gets pushed further in the same direction by the follow-on flow. Conversely, when the standardized-residual magnitude series is memoryless (H<=0.5, i.e. the local variance model already accounts for the burst), the impulse looks like an isolated liquidity shock and the usual 10-second reversal dominates. So the sign series (unpredictable on its own, per the paper) becomes tradable once conditioned on residual magnitude memory: the switch predicts whether the last minute's move continues or snaps back. Falsification: if the cross-sectional sign of forward 6-bar returns given a recent impulse is invariant to the residual DFA exponent, the mechanism is dead; the persistence story requires market makers who cannot tell endogenous from exogenous bursts and therefore mis-price continuation risk.

factors.name: Machado-Mata Quantile Decomposition of Cross-Sectional Returns (Covariate vs Price-of-Characteristic)
factors.description: Each bar, cross-sectional quantile regressions (theta grid 0.1/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.9, check-loss via smoothed IRLS, coefficients EW-smoothed over time for causal stability) of the trailing ~30-bar cumulative log return on standardized rank characteristics (log marketCap, earningsYield, grossMargin, assetGrowth, debtToAssets, plus a dollar-turnover-intensity and share-of-active-bars 'labor supply' control); each stock's implied theta is interpolated from where x_i'beta_theta matches its realized return, its return is split into a covariate component x_i'beta_0.5 and a coefficient component x_i'(beta_theta_i - beta_0.5), and the signal is minus the coefficient component plus a smaller weight on the covariate component, with the mix weight rising in theta (mirroring the paper's rising coefficient share up the distribution), vol-normalized and shrunk for low-activity names.
factors.trading_idea: McKinney-Abowd-Janicki decompose earnings gaps at each quantile into a 'covariate' part (differences in characteristics, priced at common coefficients) and a 'coefficient' part (differences in the *returns* to those characteristics), and find the covariate part dominates in the lower tail while the coefficient part dominates above the median. Ported to the cross-section of stocks, a name's recent move can likewise be split into (a) what its point-in-time fundamentals justify at the prevailing median cross-sectional price of those fundamentals, and (b) the part that only fits once you let the *slope* on those fundamentals swing to a tail quantile. Part (b) is a transient repricing of the characteristic itself — typically liquidity-demanding flow tilting a whole style for a few minutes — and should decay, while part (a) reflects slow-moving fundamental repricing that keeps grinding in the same direction because sluggish, mandate-constrained capital arrives late. The mechanism dies if the coefficient component shows zero 6-bar reversal or if the covariate component reverses instead of persisting.

factors.name: Labouchère Ruin-Proximity Capitulation Drift
factors.description: Per ticker, run a causal Labouchère state machine over 10-second bar returns (a contrarian bet each bar: win if the bar reverses the prior bar, loss if it continues; on loss append the stake to the sequence, on win strip first and last, reset when empty), then form signal = smooth ruin-hazard logistic( next stake / capital capacity ) × sequence-depth weight × sign of the cumulative return since the round started, where capital capacity is a liquidity/vol capacity proxy (short-vs-long EWMA volume ratio divided by short-vs-long EWMA absolute-return ratio); finally cross-sectionally demean/rank.
factors.trading_idea: Billings & Del Barco show that a Labouchère (negative-progression) staker enjoys long stretches of smooth wins and then dies in one burst, because the required stake grows with the unrecovered-loss ledger while capital is finite — ruin arrives when stake > bankroll. Intraday dip-buyers and inventory-averaging market makers behave exactly like Labouchère players: they fade each move, add size after each adverse tick, and their 'sequence' of unrecovered losses grows during a persistent trend. The falsifiable claim is that when the *implied next stake* implied by the loss ledger exceeds the *capital capacity* implied by current liquidity and volatility, these players stop absorbing and capitulate, so price continues in the trend (loss-streak) direction over the next ~1 minute rather than reverting. Counterparty: leveraged mean-reverters and passive liquidity providers whose margin/inventory limits are mechanical; the edge persists because their constraint binds fastest exactly when depth thins and vol spikes, and it would be killed if high ruin-proximity names instead reverted over the horizon.

factors.name: Peer-Chain Backpressure Bottleneck Discharge Gate
factors.description: Builds a per-ticker latent queue state (rolling traded volume minus the volume 'served' by realised price displacement via a rolling per-name impact coefficient) plus a signed pressure state (tick-rule signed volume), lays each industry's tickers out as a marketCap-ordered tandem route, evaluates the paper's geometrically-weighted piecewise-linear prefix test function to find the dominant prefix and its bottleneck node, and outputs signed pressure gated positively for bottleneck/discharging names and negatively for spillback-held names (downstream queue >= own queue), sector-demeaned and cross-sectionally standardised.
factors.trading_idea: Xie & Jin's model-data-independent control shows that whether a queue discharges depends not on local load but on where the *bottleneck* sits in a route: a node that is 'dominant' while its immediate downstream node is not will discharge, whereas a node whose downstream is congested is forced into holding (artificial spillback) and its backlog cannot clear. I read each ticker as a server whose queue is latent, unexecuted order-flow backlog (volume absorbed with little net price displacement), and each industry's marketCap-ordered chain (large-cap -> next-smaller-cap) as a route along which liquidity demand and information propagate. Signed backlog at a bottleneck node should therefore *discharge directionally* over the next few bars (continuation), while the same signed backlog at a spillback-blocked node is being warehoused by market makers and should revert. The bet is falsifiable and cheap to kill: if signed-flow continuation is identical for bottleneck and blocked nodes, the topological gate adds nothing; it persists because cross-name, chain-aware inventory reasoning is not something fast market-neutral capital prices at the 10-second scale, and mandate-bound liquidity providers must keep absorbing the blocked flow.

factors.name: Haar-Projection Ensemble Precision Dislocation with Jensen-Gap Trust Gate
factors.description: Over a rolling window of N bars of demeaned log returns (N deliberately smaller than the ticker count, so the sample covariance K is singular), draw a fixed causal pool of R random L-by-M orthonormalised (Haar) projections with L <= N; for each projection compute z_Phi = Phi' (Phi K Phi')^{-1} Phi r on the latest short-horizon return shock r, take the ensemble mean zbar (the invcov precision-weighted dislocation) and the cross-projection standard deviation sd; the factor is the cross-sectionally standardised value of -zbar multiplied by a monotone trust gate in |zbar| / (sd + eps), so only robustly identified hedged residuals are traded for reversal.
factors.trading_idea: In the short-window, many-name regime the sample covariance of 10-second returns is genuinely singular (N bars < M tickers), so any hedge built from it is undefined along the null space — exactly the situation Marzetta-Tucci-Simon address by inverting randomly dimension-reduced covariances and averaging the projected-back inverses over the Haar ensemble (invcov). Applying that ensemble precision estimate to the latest cross-sectional return shock gives a multi-asset-hedged dislocation: the part of a stock's recent move that its correlated peers did NOT share, weighted by how confidently that hedge is identified. Crucially, the paper's Jensen argument (a single random projection is strictly worse than the ensemble average) implies a usable second moment: the dispersion of the hedged residual ACROSS random subspaces measures how much of the stock's signal lives in the unidentified null directions, so residuals that survive many independent random subspaces are real liquidity-demand shocks that revert, while high-dispersion residuals are estimation artefacts to be discarded. The other side is a liquidity demander pushing one name away from its peer-implied level; the edge persists because practitioners either impose a rigid factor model or heavy diagonal loading, both of which over-hedge and blur exactly these short-lived idiosyncratic pushes.

factors.name: Inverse-Frequency (SIF) Rare-Bar-Token Signature Path, Thin-vs-Heavy Impact Split
factors.description: For each bar/ticker, assign a discrete token from sign(return) x trailing own-volume-intensity tercile, estimate each token's causal cross-sectional frequency f over a trailing window (all tickers), form SIF weights a/(a+f), build two rarity-weighted cumulative return paths over a ~30-bar window (thin-tape channel and heavy-tape channel), extract the level-1 signature (net rarity-weighted drift) and the time-Levy-area term (back-loadedness gate) of each channel, and cross-sectionally rank the combination -(thin drift x thin recency gate) + lambda*(heavy drift x heavy recency gate), sector-demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: SigBERT's key representational trick is not BERT but Smooth Inverse Frequency weighting: tokens that appear everywhere ('stopwords') carry almost no patient-specific information, so the path is built almost entirely from rare tokens, and only then is the truncated signature taken. Mapping this to a tape: each 10-second bar emits a 'token' (signed-return sign x own-name volume-intensity bucket), and the currently common tokens across the universe are market-wide stopwords (beta sweeps, quiet no-trade bars) whose price moves are permanent and unforecastable, whereas rare tokens are exactly the informative ones - a sizeable move printed on an unusually thin tape (liquidity vacuum, transient impact, must revert) versus a rare heavy-tape print (informed accumulation being worked, impact persists). The factor therefore builds an inverse-frequency-weighted return path, splits it into thin-tape and heavy-tape channels, and uses the signature's time-area term to measure whether the move is front- or back-loaded (a stale front-loaded vacuum has already been repaired; a fresh back-loaded one has not). Falsification: if an unweighted, unsplit short-horizon reversal on the same window matches or beats it, the rarity weighting and the impact split add nothing and the idea is dead; the counterparty is the liquidity-consuming impatient trader whose transient impact we absorb, and it persists because inventory-bearing capacity at the 1-minute scale is structurally scarce.

factors.name: Ingleton-Slack Conditional-Independence Trust Gate on Peer-State Drift
factors.description: For each ticker, over a rolling causal window of 10s bars, quantize four discrete variables at each in-window timestamp s: A=sign-state of own return at s, B=sign-state of sector-peer (ex-self) median return at s, C=sign-state of own return at s+1, D=state of own volume shock (log volume minus rolling median) at s+1; compute plug-in Shannon entropies over the 2x2x2x2 joint table to get the Ingleton slack box(AB,CD) and the double-Markov constraint terms I(A:D|C), I(A:C|D), debias the slack against block-permuted surrogates, then multiply the window's nonparametric conditional next-bar drift for the *currently observed* (A,B) state by a constraint-satisfaction gate and by +1 if the debiased slack is non-negative (trust) or -1 if it is significantly negative (regime-break, fade), and cross-sectionally demean/standardize the result.
factors.trading_idea: Kaced & Romashchenko show that the Ingleton box quantity box(AB,CD)=I(C:D|A)+I(C:D|B)+I(A:B)-I(C:D) must be non-negative for (almost) entropic points once the double-Markov constraints I(A:D|C)=I(A:C|D)=0 hold (inequality I4'), and that this bound is *essentially* conditional — it cannot be relaxed by any Lagrange multiplier on the constraints. So a plug-in estimate of the box that comes out significantly negative *while the constraints are empirically satisfied* is not a property of any single stationary joint law: it is a fingerprint of the estimation window being a mixture of two different dependence regimes (a structural break in how the stock's price path and its trade-intensity co-move with peers). The tradable consequence: the naive nonparametric predictor 'what did this stock do next, historically, when its own sign-state and its sector's sign-state looked like today' is trustworthy in the entropic-consistent regime and is stale/inverted in the violation regime. Who is on the other side: participants running fixed-lookback conditional or state-dependent predictors (pairs/peer-relative execution and short-horizon stat-arb) who keep trading a lead-lag map that the last few minutes have already broken; the edge persists because detecting the break requires a higher-order information-geometry test rather than a mean or variance shift, and 10-second horizons are too small for slow capital to police.

factors.name: De-stationary Analog-Attention Forecast (stationarized shape × restored non-stationarity)
factors.description: Within a rolling ~60-bar window of mid-prices per ticker, z-score the path (Series Stationarization), form a query patch from the last few bars and key patches from all earlier causal positions, weight them by softmax(tau * <query,key>/sqrt(d) + Delta) where tau = (recent return-scale / window return-scale)^2 and Delta = standardized drift of recent bar volume versus the window baseline, average the realized post-patch stationarized moves as the value, then de-normalize by the window sigma and cross-sectionally standardize.
factors.trading_idea: Liu et al. show that z-scoring a window before pattern matching makes the series predictable but produces indistinguishable attention across regimes ('over-stationarization'), and that the discarded statistics (window scale sigma, mean drift) must be re-injected as a temperature tau and a shift Delta to recover the true dependency. At 10-second frequency almost every practitioner signal is implicitly stationarized (z-scored returns, normalized imbalance ranks), so the level/scale regime information is systematically thrown away by the crowd; names whose local volatility and activity regime is *shifting* are exactly the ones where a normalized analog match is either far more reliable (sharp attention) or pure noise (flat attention), and nobody is pricing that distinction. The trade: run a causal within-window analog (nearest-patch attention) forecast on the stationarized mid-price path, sharpen or blur the match weights with a de-stationary temperature built from the price-scale ratio and a shift built from the volume-regime drift, then de-normalize the forecast back into return units and rank cross-sectionally. Falsifiable: if forcing tau=1, Delta=0 (plain stationarized analog forecast) delivers the same IC, the de-stationary mechanism adds nothing and the idea is dead; the counterparty is the liquidity provider whose scale-invariant quoting rule under-reacts in regime-shifting names.

factors.name: Informative-Missingness Masked Drift Split
factors.description: For each name over a short trailing window, split cumulative vol-scaled log returns into an 'observed' component (bars with trades) and a 'missing' component (zero-volume/stale bars), and compute a conditional observation-surprise score A = sum of standardized residuals of the trade-occurrence indicator against a per-name baseline intensity modulated by the contemporaneous market-wide observation rate (logit-linear co-observation model); the factor cross-sectionally ranks +observed-drift weighted by positive A minus missing-drift weighted by negative A (idiosyncratic silence while peers trade => strongest reversal of stale-quote drift).
