factors.trading_idea: The BAT/ICU foundation-model paper's central empirical claim is that the *observation mask* itself is informative: with a masked loss and forward-fill imputation, models learn that *when* a sensor is measured (and when it is silent) carries as much signal as the measured value. At 10-second resolution the same structure exists in equities: a bar with zero traded volume is a 'missing' observation whose mid nonetheless drifts, because market makers forward-fill/reprice the quote off index, ETF and peer moves rather than off any name-specific information. My claim is that price drift accumulated on *unobserved* (no-trade) bars is mechanical repricing and mean-reverts, whereas drift accumulated on *observed* bars is trade-confirmed and persists — and that the strength of each leg is governed by a conditional observation-intensity residual: how surprisingly active (or silent) a name is relative to a market-wide co-observation model, i.e. the informative-missingness score. It is falsifiable: if untraded-bar drift continues, or if the interaction with the observation residual is flat, the idea is dead. It should persist because the arbitrageur must trade a name that is by construction illiquid at that instant, so slow-moving capital cannot compete away stale-quote drift at a 1-minute scale.

factors.name: MMPP Belief-Hysteresis Wedge Drift
factors.description: Runs a causal two-state Markov-modulated marked-Poisson filter per ticker on trade-arrival events (bars with non-trivial volume, mark = standardised bar volume): deterministic between-event decay toward the invariant law plus multiplicative Bayes jumps at events, giving posterior pi_active; overlays a hysteretic declared-regime process that flips only at asymmetric boundaries (switching-cost inertia), and outputs volume-weighted signed recent pressure gated by the signed distance of pi_active to the not-yet-crossed upper boundary while the declared regime is still 'quiet' (suppressed/flipped once declared active), cross-sectionally standardised.
factors.trading_idea: Bayraktar & Ludkovski show that an agent tracking a hidden state through a Markov-modulated marked point process holds a continuously-updating posterior, but because re-labelling the regime is costly she only switches her declared policy when the posterior crosses an asymmetric boundary — producing inertia and 'shortcircuiting' (belief moves, policy does not). Liquidity providers behave the same way: their quote/width/inventory regime is a sticky discrete decision, so a name can already be in a high-intensity, information-rich trade regime while quoting is still set for the quiet regime. In that wedge — posterior on the active state elevated but not yet past the switching boundary, and the declared regime still 'quiet' — price has not fully absorbed the arriving flow, so recent signed pressure should keep drifting for a handful of bars; once the boundary is crossed and the regime is declared, the adjustment is done and the same pressure carries no (or reversed) edge. Falsified if drift conditional on the pre-boundary wedge is indistinguishable from drift in the post-switch region.

factors.name: Piecewise-Measurable Conditional Drift with Elliptic-Scaled Feedback Gain
factors.description: For each ticker/bar, form a 2-D causal state: (i) displacement of close from an EWMA anchor scaled by trailing realized vol (Parkinson high-low + return vol), (ii) a liquidity/vol regime index from volume and range relative to their trailing medians; bin both into a small grid, then estimate, from a rolling pooled cross-sectional panel using only forward returns already fully realized (lagged by >= horizon+1 bars), each cell's mean 6-bar return (measurable drift) and its variance (elliptic diffusion), and output drift/variance, clipped (bang-bang saturation), zeroed inside a hysteresis dead-band near cell boundaries and where the cell sample count is too small, finally cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: De Feo's control problem is built on drifts that are merely *measurable* in the state (e.g. 'image deterioration under different regimes depending on the level of goodwill') while the diffusion stays uniformly elliptic; the optimal policy is then a measurable selection from argmin of the Hamiltonian, i.e. a piecewise/bang-bang feedback law in state space rather than a smooth linear rule. Markets at the 10-second scale plausibly share this structure: mechanical actors (stop levels, band-triggered market makers, VWAP/participation schedulers, inventory-limit desks) make expected short-horizon drift a discontinuous step function of a name's normalized displacement from its local anchor, interacted with the prevailing liquidity/vol regime — not the monotone linear reversal that standard factors assume. We therefore estimate the drift nonparametrically per state cell (no smoothness imposed), divide by the cell's conditional variance (the elliptic diffusion coefficient) to form the Hamiltonian-minimizing feedback gain, and saturate it like a bounded control set U=[-u,u]. Falsifiable: if the estimated cell drift is monotone/linear in displacement the factor collapses to plain reversal and adds nothing over the seeds; if cell drifts are pure sampling noise, out-of-sample IC is zero.

factors.name: Residual-Verified Koopman Mode Forecast (ResDMD trust gate)
factors.description: Per ticker, on a rolling window of 10s bars, build a time-delay (Hankel) dictionary of standardized log returns augmented with nonlinear observables (|return|, signed volume share, high-low range), solve the EDMD generalised eigenproblem, compute each eigenpair's ResDMD relative residual, discard eigenpairs above a tolerance, and propagate the current state 6 bars forward using only the verified modes; the factor is the cross-sectionally standardized 6-bar forecast of cumulative return, multiplied by the verified-mode energy share (a per-name trust weight).
factors.trading_idea: Short-horizon mid-price dynamics contain a few genuinely recurrent transient structures — market-maker inventory unwind cycles, order-splitting rhythms, and post-impact decay — embedded in a sea of noise. A Hankel/EDMD (Koopman) fit to a rolling window will always produce eigenpairs, but most are spectral pollution: artefacts of fitting a finite dictionary to noise, and extrapolating them is pure overfit. Following Colbrook et al.'s ResDMD, we compute the infinite-dimensional relative residual res(lambda,g) for every candidate eigenpair using the extra Gram matrix Psi_Y*W*Psi_Y, keep ONLY modes whose residual is below a tolerance, and extrapolate 6 bars with the verified modes alone, scaling the resulting forecast by the share of window energy those verified modes explain. The edge persists because most participants either fit unverified linear/AR extrapolations (and are whipsawed by spurious modes) or ignore the transient cyclical component entirely; the residual acts as a real-time, per-name confidence that separates physically recurrent dynamics from noise. Falsification: if forecasts built from HIGH-residual modes predict 6-bar returns as well as low-residual ones, the verification mechanism adds nothing and the idea is dead.

factors.name: Fleeting-Quote Drift Reversal Gated by Reflected Spread State
factors.description: Splits the recent cumulative mid return of each name into a traded component (bars whose volume exceeds the name's own recent activity floor) and an untraded/fleeting component (near-zero-volume bars), normalizes both by a latent spread-state scale estimated as the paper's per-trade volatility sqrt(sum r^2 / #trade-bars) (linear spread-volatility relation), and outputs the cross-sectionally ranked signal minus(untraded drift) weighted by spread-compression relative to its own rolling median, plus a small positive loading on the traded drift when the spread state is wide.
factors.trading_idea: Blanchet & Chen argue the economically meaningful price process is the price-per-trade: mid-quote movement between market orders is dominated by fleeting limit orders that are placed and cancelled within fractions of a second, and their model further implies the innovation scale is proportional to the prevailing spread, which is a reflected process pushed back toward its lower boundary between jumps. This means mid drift accumulated in bars with no (or negligible) market-order flow is largely unbacked repricing that should be given back once queues replenish, whereas drift accumulated in bars carrying actual trades is the informative, jump/market-order component. The reflection mechanism sharpens this: when the latent spread state is compressed toward its boundary, incoming increments are truncated and quote flicker dominates, so untraded drift reverts hardest; when the spread state is wide (just after a book-depleting jump) untraded quote moves are genuine repricing and should not be faded. Liquidity providers who generate the flicker are on the other side; the inefficiency persists because participants who read the mid as a price signal cannot distinguish queue-driven mid moves from trade-driven ones at 10-second granularity.

factors.name: Jump-Reset Exercise Boundary with Survival-Density Sign Flip
factors.description: For each name, detect return jumps against a causal robust local scale, reset a segment at each jump, and measure signed proximity of close to the segment's running max/min normalised by segment volatility and widened by an indifference-style penalty proportional to a self-excited (exponential-kernel) jump intensity; this signed barrier-proximity is then multiplied by a cross-sectionally standardised conditional survival probability of no jump over the next 6 bars so the signal flips from breakout-continuation to extreme-reversion as jump hazard rises.
factors.trading_idea: Bayraktar–Zhou show that in a controller–stopper problem with jumps the optimal stopping rule is NOT a global hitting time: between jumps the agent uses a level barrier, and every jump RESETS that barrier, while the effective barrier is shifted by the log conditional survival density of the next jump (H = R - (1/p)ln alpha). Mapping this to intraday equities: discretionary liquidators / stop-users anchor their trigger levels on the extremes established since the last discontinuity, and they widen those triggers when the perceived hazard of another discontinuity is high (jump risk makes waiting cheaper than exercising). Therefore price arriving at the post-jump running extreme should CONTINUE through it when the conditional survival probability of no further jump is high (barriers are tight, exercise flow fires and cascades), but should REVERT from that extreme when jump hazard is high (barriers have been pushed out, no exercise flow arrives and liquidity providers absorb the probe). Falsifiable: if the sign of the extreme-proximity payoff does not flip with the estimated survival probability, or if the barrier does not need to be re-anchored at detected jumps (unconditional extremes work equally well), the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Tick-Grid Bindingness & Penny-ness Flow-Continuation Flip
factors.description: Estimates a per-ticker tick grid from a trailing distribution of nonzero |Δmid|, forms (i) relative tick size (tick/price) and (ii) the mid's grid phase as a one-tick-lock/spread-parity proxy, builds these into a bindingness gate, and multiplies a volume-normalised signed order-flow imbalance by a gate that flips sign between coarse-grid/locked (continuation) and fine-grid/wide (reversal) states, tilted by cross-sectional small-marketCap rank.
factors.trading_idea: The penny-stock paper's real economic content is not 'cheap stocks earn more' but that *nominal price level* — not beta, not raw liquidity — is the state variable that governs how a name trades, because the minimum price increment is a large fraction of a low price (Bollen-Christie's endogenous price-dependent tick sizes). I take that mechanism intraday: estimate each name's price grid causally from the smallest nonzero mid increments (on a mid-price feed the minimum move is half a tick), then read the mid's *phase* on that grid, which reveals spread parity — a mid sitting on the half-tick grid implies a one-tick locked book, a mid on the tick grid implies a wider spread. When the grid is coarse relative to price (high relative tick = 'penny-like') and the book is locked at one tick, market makers cannot price-improve, so directional trade pressure must accumulate against a fat queue and only discharges as a full-tick jump — flow imbalance predicts *continuation*. When the grid is economically negligible (fine relative tick, wide/even spread), the identical imbalance is mostly transient price impact paid to liquidity suppliers and predicts *reversal*; the sign of the flow loading therefore flips with the bindingness gate, and the effect is amplified in low-marketCap names where the paper's size/asymmetry premium and retail lottery demand concentrate. It is killed if the estimated grid phase is uniformly distributed (no discreteness to exploit) or if the flow-continuation coefficient shows no monotonic dependence on relative tick size.

factors.name: SIRSD Activity-Contagion: Susceptible Ignition vs. Waning-Immunity Cohorts
factors.description: For each ticker, causally classify a per-bar SIRSD state from trailing-window volume/range abnormality (infected = current burst; recovered = burst within last K bars with exponentially waning immunity; deceased = prolonged activity collapse; susceptible = the rest), aggregate s,i,r,d fractions per sector, form the transmission intensity beta_hat * s*i/(1-d) together with the volume-weighted signed flow direction of the infected cohort, and score each name as (susceptibility * peer-exposure * sector force-of-infection * infected-cohort direction) minus a waning-immunity-weighted reversal term on its own recent burst return, then cross-sectionally standardize.
factors.trading_idea: Treat intraday trading activity as an epidemic on a sector's name-set: a burst of volume/price pressure in one name 'infects' peers through index/basket hedging, screen-driven attention and market-maker inventory recycling, then names 'recover' (temporarily immune: their queue is cleared, liquidity replenished, further pressure has little price impact) and only slowly become susceptible again as immunity wanes, while some names 'die' (activity collapses, no participation). Following the SIRSD/Koopman paper, the key object is not the level of activity but the frequency-dependent force of infection beta*s*i/(1-d): contagion pressure is largest when a sector has many still-uninfected susceptibles, an already-burning infected cohort, and a shrunken living (participating) population that amplifies the transmission term. The tradable inefficiency is that the *next* recipients of contagion are predictable — susceptible, high-exposure names in a high-force-of-infection sector should drift 6 bars ahead in the signed direction of the infected cohort's flow, while recently-infected (immune/recovered) names should not follow and instead give back their burst. It is falsifiable: if activity bursts at the 10-second scale do not propagate within sector to structurally similar names, or if recovered names continue rather than revert, the factor's IC collapses; the counterparty is the liquidity provider who prices each name in isolation, and the edge persists because cross-name inventory recycling is slow-moving and mandate-constrained.

factors.name: Growth-Adjusted Payback Duration Factor: Residual Snapback
factors.description: Builds a point-in-time growth-adjusted payback duration per name (P/E from earningsYield, g from epsGrowth blended with netIncomeGrowth3Y, using the paper's g→0 limit P/E and its non-convergent-case ranking N* = Nmax − gP/(E(1+g)) when g ≤ −E/(P+E)), forms a duration-tilted common return factor F_t as the cross-sectional duration-z-weighted mean of 10-second returns alongside the equal-weighted market factor M_t, causally EWMA-regresses each stock's returns on [M_t, F_t] over a ~30-minute window, and signals the negative of the last-6-bar accumulated regression residual, scaled down for names near the payback singularity (unstable duration) and for residuals realised on abnormally high relative volume (likely informed).
factors.trading_idea: Baird-Dodd-Middleton show the P/E is really a *time* — the number of years of (growing) earnings needed to repay the price — and that the growth-adjusted payback period N = log(1 + g·(P/E)/(1+g))/log(1+g) separates stocks far better than P/E alone. Read N as the equity's earnings duration: long-N names are the ones whose value sits in distant, extrapolated cash flows, so they are the natural target of indiscriminate basket / macro-discount-rate flow, and they should share a *common intraday return factor* beyond the equal-weighted market. My claim is that this duration-mimicking factor exists at the 10-second scale, that basket flow pushes individual names off their duration-cohort loading, and that the idiosyncratic part of that push snaps back within about a minute because the liquidity providers absorbing it are compensated, not informed. Falsification is clean: if a duration-sorted long-minus-short return series carries no incremental cross-sectional loading over the market factor (b_F ≈ 0 for most names), or if residual gaps are momentum rather than reversal at 6 bars, the factor is dead. It persists because joining point-in-time quarterly fundamentals to 10-second order flow is operationally awkward for pure microstructure players and irrelevant to slow fundamental investors.

factors.name: Chance-Constrained Safe-Set Margin: Contraction vs. Free-Drift Policy Blend
factors.description: Per ticker, build a 2-D state x = [(close - EW anchor)/scale, k-bar velocity/scale], fit a causal rolling 2x2 one-step map Â and residual covariance Σ on past bars, form the chance-constrained slack min_l (g_l - F_l Âx) / (k_l*sqrt(F_l Σ F_l')) over a hexagonal admissible polytope in (deviation, velocity), convert it to an intervention weight φ ∈ [0,1], and output the blended one-step forecast φ*(-(1-λ)*deviation) + (1-φ)*((Âx)_1 - x_1), scaled by signal-to-residual-noise and cross-sectionally standardized.
factors.trading_idea: Esmaeili et al. never let a single controller run: they estimate the closed-loop map directly from data, tighten each polyhedral constraint row by a variance term k*sqrt(FΣF'), and then blend a performance (RL) policy with a λ-contractive safe backup via a scalar φ that is zero deep inside the safe set and rises as the risk-tightened boundary is approached. Real intraday markets have exactly this structure: market makers and intraday risk books let price drift freely while inventory/deviation state sits well inside their soft limits, but as the joint (deviation, velocity) state approaches a *variance-tightened* limit — which shrinks mechanically when local noise is high — capacity is withdrawn and the state is forced to contract toward the local anchor. The falsifiable claim is that neither pure reversion nor pure drift-following works alone: the sign of the 6-bar edge should flip as a function of the chance-constraint slack, with reversion strength scaling in the *tightened* (volatility-adjusted) margin rather than the raw deviation, and the effect should vanish if we replace the variance-tightened margin with an unscaled one. The inefficiency persists because the intervening agents are risk-mandate driven (hard VaR/inventory limits, not alpha views) and their withdrawal is predictable from public price geometry, while slow-moving directional capital cannot arbitrage the 1-minute window.

factors.name: Rough-Path Jacobian Gain: Ordered Propagation of the Latest Flow Shock
factors.description: Per ticker, estimates a rolling causal 2x2 local response matrix between log-return and signed-volume channels, forms the time-ordered product ∏_t (I + dM_t) of bar-level increment matrices over a short window, and outputs the return-coordinate of that Jacobian applied to the latest (return, flow) innovation, compressed by its top-singular-value gain and shrunk when the path's p-variation + |Levy area| control function is extreme; cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Inahama's object of interest is the derivative (Jacobian) process J of a rough differential equation: the time-ordered product J = ∏(I + dM), dM = ∇σ(Y)dX, whose size is controlled by the driving path's p-variation and Levy area (sup|J| ≤ exp(C·ω^γ)) and whose moments are heavy-tailed. Translated to a book: the price response to a fresh order-flow shock is not a fixed impact coefficient but a state-dependent flow-map derivative, and because the local return/flow coupling matrices do not commute, the *order* of recent events (flow-then-drift vs drift-then-flow) changes how a new shock will be amplified over the next few bars. I therefore estimate a causal 2-channel (return, signed-flow) local coupling matrix per name, build the time-ordered matrix product over a short window, propagate the most recent innovation through it, and gate the result by the rough-path control function ω (p-variation plus |Levy area|) since the theory says amplification is exponential in ω and hence untrustworthy/heavy-tailed in the roughest states. Falsifiable: if the ordered-product propagation adds nothing over last-bar return, realized vol and plain signed volume, the mechanism is dead; the counterparty is the market maker quoting off an average, order-insensitive impact model, and the edge persists because ordered path dependence is expensive to estimate in real time.

factors.name: Intraday Arousal–Valence Emotion Shares, Glamour-Gated Enthusiasm Reversal
factors.description: Soft-assigns each 10s bar to excitement / fear / neutral emotional states from a volume-arousal z-score times intrabar valence (close position within high-low range and signed return), exponentially aggregates the state shares over ~30 bars into a composition summing to one, residualizes the excitement-minus-fear share cross-sectionally against the same-window cumulative return and relative volume, and takes the negative of that residual scaled by a fundamental sentiment-proneness composite (loss / low netMargin, zero dividendYield, high psRatio and pbRatio, small marketCap) and by current participation intensity.
factors.trading_idea: Vamossy (2020) shows that pre-event investor *enthusiasm* (high-arousal, positive-valence emotion) coincides with contemporaneously high prices but predicts LOWER subsequent returns, while fear predicts higher subsequent returns — mood inflates the price level, not the expected payoff, and the effect is strongest for volatile, sentiment-prone names and when crowd engagement is high. At 10-second frequency the tape carries a direct arousal/valence analogue: arousal is the bar's volume burst relative to the stock's own recent baseline, and valence is where the bar closes inside its own range together with the sign of its return, so bars can be soft-assigned to 'excited', 'fearful' or 'neutral' states and averaged into probability-like shares exactly as the paper averages message emotions into shares. Crucially the excitement share is residualized cross-sectionally against the same window's raw return and volume level, so the signal is the *emotional composition* of trading, not another short-horizon reversal or order-flow imbalance; the paper's own tests survive controls for pre-event returns and realized surprise, which is what we mimic. The trade is short the excited/euphoric tail and long the fear tail among sentiment-prone (loss-making, non-dividend, high price-to-sales, small-cap) stocks, where attention-chasing retail buyers are the counterparty and liquidity providers absorbing their arousal-driven demand harvest the ~1-minute give-back; the inefficiency persists because retail attention flow is behavioural and slow-moving while intraday inventory risk limits arbitrage capital. Falsification: if the residualized excitement share has no incremental forward-return sign once the window return and signed volume are projected out, or if the glamour gate does not amplify it, the mood-level mechanism is dead and the effect was plain reversal.

factors.name: Volume-Weighted Ordinal-Partition Network Loop Persistence Regime Flip
factors.description: Over a rolling window of recent bars, embed close-to-close returns with delay coordinates (n=3-4, tau=1), map each embedded vector to its ordinal pattern, and build the symmetrized pattern-transition graph with edge weights equal to the volume traded across each transition; convert weights to lengths (1/omega), form a lazy-random-walk diffusion dissimilarity matrix, extract the exact H0 persistence diagram (single-linkage / MST edge deaths) plus an H1 surrogate (each non-tree pair born at its dissimilarity and dying at the maximum dissimilarity along its MST path), and summarize with total persistence, persistent entropy and max lifetime. The factor is the cross-sectionally ranked interaction between this loop-dominance-vs-fragmentation score and the negated z-scored return of the last few bars, so loop-dominated names are traded as reversals and topologically fragmented names as continuations.
factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution a mid-price path alternates between two qualitatively different shapes: (a) queue-driven oscillation around a pinned level, where the trajectory in ordinal-pattern space keeps re-entering the same small set of states via high-volume transitions, producing a dense recurrent cycle (a long-lived H1 loop in the flag filtration of the transition network); and (b) a directional take-out phase, where the pattern trajectory is quasi-transient and tree-like, so the network fragments (large H0 total persistence, high persistent entropy, essentially no loops). Following the complex-network-to-persistent-homology pipeline of Güzel (2026) — ordinal partition network, reciprocal-weight/diffusion dissimilarity, Vietoris-Rips persistence — the topology of the *volume-weighted* OPN classifies which regime the name is currently in, and that classification signs the next ~1 minute: loop-dominated names revert their last move, fragmented/transient names continue it. The other side of the trade is the impatient taker who reads any move as information and the passive maker who quotes through a genuine trend; the edge persists because the discriminating object is a nonlinear path-shape invariant, not something visible in realized volatility, return autocorrelation, or signed-volume imbalance. Falsification: if the loop-dominance statistic has no interaction with the sign of the recent move (i.e., the interaction term's IC is flat while each leg alone is noise), the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Infinite-Dimensional Cross-Section Curve Lévy-Area Rotation
factors.description: Builds a rolling E-valued path from Legendre-mode projections (level/slope/curvature over an earningsYield-rank coordinate) of the cross-sectional cumulative-return curve, computes the antisymmetric second-order signature (Lévy areas) between mode pairs over a ~60-bar window, uses the area signs to forecast each lagging mode's next increment from the leading mode's recent increment, and scores each stock by its Legendre loading on those forecast mode increments, shrunk by the path's rolling α-Hölder roughness relative to its own history.
factors.trading_idea: Cox–Khedher–Maessen treat the state as a path taking values in an infinite-dimensional space (an HJM-style forward *curve*) and show that continuous functionals of such a path are approximated by LINEAR functionals of its signature; because of the shuffle identity, the symmetric part of the second-order signature is already determined by the first-order increments, so the only genuinely new second-order information is the antisymmetric Lévy area between two projections of the curve. I map this literally to equities: at each 10s bar the market state is not a scalar but a curve c_t(u) = cross-sectionally demeaned cumulative log-return profile across a fundamental coordinate u (rank in earningsYield, tie-broken by marketCap rank), projected onto orthogonal Legendre modes (level, value/size slope, curvature). The Lévy areas between these modes measure which mode's motion *precedes* the others' — index/ETF and macro flow typically hit the level mode first, and single-name relative-value capital propagates it into the slope/curvature modes with a lag, so a positive area L→S says the tilt modes will still catch up to the level mode's recent move. The signal is dead if areas are pure noise (no rotation), and the paper's weak-* UAT only holds uniformly on Hölder-norm-BOUNDED sets, which gives a falsifiable conditioning: the signature-linear forecast should degrade sharply in high-roughness (jump/news) windows, so we shrink it there.

factors.name: Log-Vol Scaling Plateau (Estimation-Noise Share) × Roughness Reversal Gate
factors.description: Builds a causal range-based (Garman-Klass) log-volatility proxy per ticker, measures its second-moment increment scaling m(2,Delta) over dyadic lags, regresses log m(2,Delta) on log Delta at intermediate lags to get the fractional slope 2H and extrapolates it down to Delta=1 to isolate the small-lag noise-plateau excess N; the factor is minus the vol-normalized 6-bar return multiplied by tanh(z_cs(N) - rho*z_cs(H_hat)), i.e. reversal when estimation-noise share is high and vol is very rough, mild continuation when noise share is low and vol scaling is persistent.
factors.trading_idea: Mouti (2023) shows that a range-based log-volatility proxy decomposes as log sigma_hat = nu*W^H + estimation noise, so the empirical scaling curve log m(2,Delta) vs log Delta breaks into a NOISE-dominated flat plateau at the smallest lags and a fractional slope 2H at intermediate lags (his Fig. 14). Cross-sectionally, a large small-lag plateau excess means the name's price path is dominated by transient jitter (quote flicker / bid-ask bounce / fleeting liquidity) rather than genuine vol-of-vol, so its last directional move is mostly non-informational and should snap back within a minute; a small plateau plus a steep (high-H, persistent) vol scaling means the recent move accompanied a genuine, persistent volatility regime shift and is more likely to extend. Liquidity providers must quote continuously and cannot distinguish these two states in real time, and fast reversal capital is capacity-constrained at the 10-second scale, so the mispricing persists. The idea dies if reversal strength is unrelated to the plateau excess once one controls for the level of volatility and the raw magnitude of the recent move.

factors.name: Fundamentalist-vs-Chartist Force Blend with Switching Hysteresis
factors.description: Builds two causal force proxies per name — a chartist trigger (signed 3-bar run indicator scaled by run magnitude) and a fundamentalist gap (own recent cumulative return minus that of its sector x value/quality-composite peer bucket, using earningsYield, freeCashFlowYield, roic, evToEbitda, incomeQuality ranks) — then blends them with rolling ridge weights fitted on strictly lagged 6-bar realized returns, shrinking the chartist leg by an exponential penalty on the recent flip rate of force dominance, and cross-sectionally demeans the result.
factors.trading_idea: Toth & Scalas simulate a market populated by three force types — value-anchored fundamentalists, trend-triggered chartists, and noise traders — and show (a) which force dominates price formation is a dynamic, performance-driven state that flips (their Markov-chain 'state pairs'), and (b) only the best-informed fundamentalist force is a persistently profitable anchor while the mid-informed churn between strategies and lose. Mapping this to real 10-second bars: at any instant a name's next few bars are pushed either by chartist continuation (activated by short same-sign runs, exactly the 3-step trigger in their code) or by fundamentalist pull toward the value implied by comparably-valued/quality peers, and the relative potency of these two forces is itself estimable causally from recent realized outcomes. Edge comes from adaptively weighting the two forces per name instead of assuming a fixed continuation or reversal regime, and from the paper's asymmetry result: when the dominance of the two forces has been flipping a lot recently (churn regime, mid-informed traders in control), the chartist term is noise and the value-anchored pull should get essentially all the weight. It is falsifiable: if the rolling estimated force weights have no persistence over their own re-estimation lag, or if the fundamentalist term stops working precisely in high-flip regimes, the mechanism is dead. The other side is short-horizon trend-chasing/liquidity-taking flow; it persists because reconciling intraday price with slow fundamental peer information requires patient capital that is scarce at the 1-minute scale.

factors.name: Transitive Lead-Lag Closure with Sector Landmark Relay
factors.description: Detects discrete signed shock events per ticker (standardised return jumps confirmed by volume), estimates a sparse directed lead-lag relation graph from event-conditioned forward responses at lags 1..L keeping only edges above a confidence threshold and minimum event count, adds sector-aggregate 'landmark' nodes so thinly-evented names stay connected, then forms each ticker's score as the lag-decayed relay of still-in-flight leader shocks propagated over both direct edges and transitively composed two-hop paths (with the composed term weighted up where the direct edge failed the confidence test).
factors.trading_idea: GraphTREx's central claim is that pairwise, locally-estimated temporal relations are noisy and sparse, but that a confidence-thresholded relation graph plus transitive composition and global 'landmark' nodes recovers long-range orderings that direct pairwise estimation cannot see (their largest gains, +8.9%, are exactly on distant pairs). The market analogue: direct 10-second lead-lag correlations between two individual names are mostly estimation noise, but the chain A leads B and B leads C implies an A->C ordering that is statistically far better supported than the raw A-C cross-correlation. Trading a follower off the composed second-hop path, rather than off a directly measured (and hence over-fit) leader, should pick up genuinely delayed information diffusion that slow, capacity-constrained cross-sectional arbitrage does not immediately erase. Falsifier: if the 2-hop composed edges add no incremental IC over direct 1-hop edges (or if their sign flips out-of-sample), the transitivity mechanism is dead and the signal collapses to a repackaged peer-flow factor.

factors.name: Censored Binomial Transition Pinning under OU Vol Forecast
factors.description: Per ticker, fit a causal rolling AR(1)/OU on log realized bar volatility to forecast next-bar sigma_hat (node spacing g = sigma_hat), compute the grid-adjustment residual K = nearest-node offset of cumulative log price on that grid plus a short volume-weighted drift term, form the raw lattice up-probability q = 0.5*(1 + (K + drift)/g), and output the cross-sectionally demeaned product of the censoring severity (how far q lies outside [0,1], plus the recent frequency of censoring events) and the signed pinning direction sign(q - 0.5); interior/uncensored names get weight near zero.
factors.trading_idea: When a diffusion is approximated on a recombining binomial lattice whose node spacing is set by the *forecast* volatility (Nelson-Ramaswamy / censored-lattice construction in the source paper), the local risk-neutral up-probability q = 1/2*(1 + (K + mu*dt)/(sigma_hat*sqrt(dt))) must be censored at 0 or 1 whenever the drift plus grid-adjustment residual exceeds one node spacing: the process can no longer be locally martingale on that grid and is forced to move deterministically in one direction. Mapping this to 10-second bars: the effective node spacing is the one-step-ahead conditional volatility (log-vol is strongly mean-reverting, so spacing shrinks exactly when recent vol is above its own OU long-run level), while the numerator is the recent volume-weighted drift plus the price's offset from the nearest grid node. Names whose lattice probability is *censored* (drift dominates the shrinking vol grid) should continue in the pinned direction over the next few bars, because symmetric mean-reversion market-makers quoting around mid are on the other side and get run over during low-forecast-vol trending micro-regimes; names with interior (uncensored) probabilities are genuinely martingale and carry no directional edge. Falsifiable: if the gate adds nothing over a plain drift/volatility ratio, or if censored names revert rather than continue, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Transaction-Cost Price Wedge with Equilibrium-Restricted OU Flow Decay
factors.description: Signs each bar's volume by intrabar close-open location to proxy the trading rate, accumulates it into a name-specific OU/EWMA state whose decay kappa_i is set by the equilibrium restriction kappa_i ∝ sigma_i / sqrt(ILLIQ_i) (both estimated causally from rolling windows), forms the wedge as cross-sectionally normalised ILLIQ_i x OU flow state, and outputs minus that wedge times its predicted 6-bar decay fraction (1 - exp(-kappa_i * 6)), gated to bars where the recent price move is flow-consistent (flow-driven, hence transitory) rather than flow-free (fundamental).
factors.trading_idea: Muhle-Karbe/Shi/Yang show that with quadratic costs the traded price equals the frictionless price plus a *transitory* wedge exactly equal to (cost matrix) x (current signed trading rate), and that the equilibrium trading rate is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process whose mean-reversion speed is pinned down by the model as kappa ~ sigma / sqrt(Lambda) — i.e. illiquid names carry a LARGER but SLOWER-decaying wedge, liquid names a small fast-decaying one. This yields a non-monotone-in-liquidity reversal prediction that plain order-flow reversal misses: the expected return over the next h bars is minus the wedge times (1 - exp(-kappa_i h)), so the tradable edge peaks for names whose flow-decay half-life is comparable to the holding horizon, not for the most illiquid ones. The other side is the risk-sharing agent still working off an inventory shock (a slow-moving, mandate-constrained liquidity demander); the intermediary earns the wedge back as the rate decays. Falsification: if reversal strength is monotone increasing in Amihud illiquidity, or if scaling flow by the model-implied kappa adds nothing over a raw exponential-decay flow imbalance, the mechanism is wrong.

factors.name: Hawkes Saddle-Point Saturation: Cascade vs Exogenous Burst Impact Flip
factors.description: Per ticker on a rolling window, proxies discrete marked-Hawkes event counts from volume divided by a rolling typical trade size, estimates the branching ratio n by fixed-point inversion of the count dispersion index (mark CV corrected), converts the current short-window activity rate into the Hawkes saddle-point tilt theta* and normalises it by the branch point theta_c to get a cascade-saturation index S in (0,1); the factor is the vol-standardized recent return multiplied by (1 - 2S), cross-sectionally ranked, so that cascade-saturated bursts predict reversal and unsaturated (many-immigrant) bursts predict continuation.
factors.trading_idea: Precise-deviation theory for discrete marked Hawkes processes says an elevated activity level x is realised in two structurally different ways: for x below the critical rate the exponential tilt theta*(x) stays interior and the deviation is produced by MANY independent immigrant clusters (exogenous arrivals), while as theta*(x) approaches the branch point theta_c the same deviation is produced by ONE giant self-exciting cascade of offspring events. Economically these are different trades: a one-big-cascade volume burst is endogenous order-flow reflexivity (liquidity takers chasing each other, mechanical impact, no new information), so its contemporaneous price move should decay within a minute as market makers refill; a many-immigrant burst reflects genuinely dispersed information arrival and its move should persist. I therefore estimate the branching ratio n from the index of dispersion of bar-level activity counts (using eta''(0)/eta'(0) = (1+n^2 cv_mark^2)/(1-n)^2 from the paper's moderate-deviation constants), map the current burst to a saturation index S = theta*/theta_c in closed form (theta* = log X - n(X-1) with X = mu/((1-n)mu0 + n*mu), theta_c = n - 1 - log n), and flip the sign of the recent standardized return on S. This dies if burst reversal/continuation is invariant to the estimated branching ratio, i.e. if S adds nothing beyond a plain volume-ratio z-score; the counterparty is the impatient cascade participant, and the edge persists because inventory-constrained liquidity providers cannot distinguish endogenous from exogenous flow in real time.

factors.name: Signal-Precision Gated Bad-News Impulse Split
factors.description: Computes a per-name 'bad-news opacity' score from point-in-time fundamentals (EPS/revenue surprise magnitudes and sign disagreement, |incomeQuality-1|, intangiblesToAssets, bars since the last fundamental update), combines it with a volume-intensity-weighted, cross-sectionally demeaned short-horizon price impulse (~18-36 bars), and outputs impulse * (2*rank(opacity)-1) restricted/amplified within the negative-news cohort so opaque names load on continuation and transparent names on reversal.
factors.trading_idea: El Ghordaf & El Khamlichi show that the market's reaction to bad earnings news depends on the *precision* of the disclosure: quantitative (precise) warnings are impounded almost immediately around day 0, while qualitative (vague, unquantified) warnings produce a persistent post-event drift, i.e. systematic underreaction to imprecise signals. Mapping this to our point-in-time fundamentals, a name's 'bad-news state' (negative EPS/revenue surprise, shrinking earnings and FCF) can be paired with a *precision* score built from how internally consistent and hard-to-quantify that news is (EPS vs revenue surprise sign agreement, accrual quality |OCF/NI - 1|, intangibility of the asset base, staleness of the last report). The falsifiable claim is an interaction, not a level effect: among opaque bad-news names, a fresh intraday negative price impulse should *continue* over the next minute (slow-moving, uncertainty-averse capital keeps selling and market makers widen rather than lean), whereas among precise bad-news names the same impulse is liquidity noise and should *revert*. If the sign of the impulse-to-forward-return relation does not flip across the precision axis, the idea is dead; the inefficiency persists because valuation uncertainty raises inventory risk exactly where information is vague, so intraday liquidity providers refuse to absorb the flow.

factors.name: Deflator Degeneracy: Continuous-vs-Jump Split of Local Sharpe Blowup
factors.description: Over a rolling window of 10s bars, estimate the local drift a and continuous variance c (bipower/truncated) per name, accumulate the mean-variance trade-off K = sum(a^2/c) as a degeneracy score, decompose the same window into continuous vs jump variation and test whether the path approached/breached the rolling extreme continuously or by a gap; the cross-sectionally ranked signal is sign(a) * strength(K, extreme-proximity) with the sign flipped when the degeneracy is jump-driven.
factors.trading_idea: Fontana's results say that the weak no-arbitrage conditions (NIP/NSA/NA1) survive an absolutely continuous change of measure exactly when the density process Z can reach zero only *continuously*; if Z jumps to zero, an 'increasing profit' appears out of nowhere and the local model is degenerate. Empirically the analogue is the mean-variance trade-off density dK = a^2/c (local drift squared over local variance): when it explodes intrabar, the bar-level model is locally arbitrage-like, and the *way* it explodes decides what happens next. If the blowup is produced by a smooth grind (variance collapsing continuously while signed drift persists, price creeping toward a recent extreme without gapping through it) it is a real, slow-moving order-flow imbalance and the drift persists over the next few bars; if it is produced by a discontinuity (a single gap bar that jumps through the recent extreme, jump variation dominating bipower variation) the measured drift is a measure-change artifact — a fake increasing profit — and price snaps back as liquidity providers reprice. The trade is against dealers who cannot tell the two regimes apart in real time; it persists because the continuity/jump distinction requires within-window path decomposition, not just a return sign. Kill test: if replacing the continuity/jump gate by a constant leaves the IC unchanged, the mechanism is wrong and the factor is just short-horizon momentum.

factors.name: Monotone Mean-Variance Hedging-Demand Elasticity (sign-flipping rebalancing pressure)
factors.description: For each name, estimate the latent variance factor Z (short-window realized/Parkinson variance), its AR(1) mean-reversion speed kappa and vol-of-vol b from causal rolling regressions on log Z, the leverage correlation rho between standardized returns and variance innovations, and diffusive vol sigma; plug (kappa, b, rho, common lambda, T-t = 6 bars) into the paper's closed-form Riccati root solution to get A, form the demand elasticity P = lambda/sigma - rho*b*A/sigma, and multiply it by the negated vol-scaled recent price displacement (distance from a slow anchor), then cross-sectionally winsorize and rank-demean.
factors.trading_idea: Trybula–Zawisza show that the (monotone) mean-variance optimal position in a stochastic-variance market is pi* = -(wealth - target) * [lambda/sigma(Z) - rho*b*A(t)/sigma(Z)]: a contrarian 'distance-to-target' term multiplied by a demand elasticity that contains an intertemporal hedging piece driven by the return/variance correlation rho, the vol-of-vol b, the variance mean-reversion kappa, and the closed-form Riccati coefficient A(t) (A(t) <= 0). Mechanically, whenever a name moves, the marginal mean-variance / vol-targeting trader must rebalance against the move with intensity proportional to that elasticity, and their temporary price impact produces short-horizon reversal that is strongly cross-sectionally heterogeneous. The genuinely falsifiable twist is that the elasticity can change sign: for names with a strong leverage effect (rho << 0) and large vol-of-vol, |rho*b*A| exceeds the myopic lambda/sigma term, the optimal exposure sign flips, and the same trader now rebalances *with* the move, so those names should show continuation rather than reversal over the next minute. This survives arbitrage because it is a flow/impact effect of mandate-constrained risk-budgeted capital, not a mispriced cash flow; high-frequency liquidity providers price the myopic term but not the factor-hedging component.

factors.name: Sparse-Regime H0 Persistence Scaling Gate on Delay-Embedded Path
factors.description: For each ticker, embed the last W vol-normalized 10s returns as a 2-D delay point cloud, extract the H0 persistence diagram of the Cech filtration exactly via MST edge lengths (deaths), then compute (a) the sparse-regime scaling exponent d_eff from a log-log fit of #{deaths <= r} versus r and (b) the dominant-lifetime share (max death / total persistence, the alpha=1 total-persistence functional); the cross-sectionally ranked combination gates recent vol-normalized drift toward continuation when the path is topologically coherent and toward reversal when persistence mass is diagonal-concentrated.
factors.trading_idea: Owada's sparse-regime results say that for an i.i.d. point cloud the number of k-cycles alive at radius r obeys a clean power law (n^{k+2} r^{d(k+1)}), and that non-robust structure piles up near the diagonal of the persistence diagram while genuine structure sits far from it. Applied to the delay-embedded 10-second return path of a single name, this gives a scale-free discriminator between a path that is pure isotropic microstructure noise (death radii of H0 follow the i.i.d. power law with a full-dimensional exponent, persistence mass concentrated near the diagonal) and a path that has collapsed onto a low-dimensional filament or split into two well-separated plateaus (deflated scaling exponent, one dominant off-diagonal lifetime — i.e. an information-driven level shift). The falsifiable claim is that the sign of short-horizon return autocorrelation flips with this topological state: coherent/off-diagonal paths continue over the next ~1 minute, diffuse near-diagonal paths revert. The other side of the trade is liquidity provision that mean-reverts every move indiscriminately; the edge persists because separating a real repricing from noise in 10-second data is exactly the hard, capacity-constrained inference problem market makers must solve in real time, and moment-based tools (variance ratios, realized vol) are dominated by a few large returns whereas persistence lifetimes are outlier-robust and vol-scale-free.

factors.name: Gricean Relevance-Deficit Flow Drift, Opacity-Gated
factors.description: Within a ~30-bar window, computes signed volume (tick-rule) and a Gricean 'relevance' statistic — the normalized alignment between per-bar signed flow and per-bar returns — plus 'clarity' (net move / summed absolute moves); the factor is the window's net flow imbalance direction times the relevance deficit (1 - alignment), sector-demeaned and multiplied by a cross-sectional fundamental opacity gate built from intangiblesToAssets, rdToRevenue, goodwill/totalAssets, inverse incomeQuality and inverse marketCap rank.
factors.trading_idea: Liang & Carrasco Kind show that when managers fail to give *relevant* answers to explicit information demands, the market's information-processing cost rises and the news is incorporated only with a lag (amplified PEAD, higher volatility/volume/spreads), and that this effect lives almost entirely in opaque firms (multi-segment, R&D/intangible-heavy, low sophisticated-investor attention). The high-frequency analogue of an unanswered question is a burst of directional trade flow to which the price path fails to *respond bar-by-bar*: the demand for revaluation is public and observable, yet the quote path moves incoherently with it, so the flow's information stays unpriced. I therefore measure a bar-level 'relevance' score between signed flow and returns inside a short window and trade the residual flow direction when relevance is low, scaling exposure by a point-in-time fundamental opacity index, since opaque names are exactly where processing costs delay revelation. Falsifier: if low flow-return relevance is followed by reversal rather than continuation in the flow direction, or if the effect is equally strong in transparent (low-intangible, large, high-income-quality) names, the mechanism is wrong — the counterparty is the market maker/short-horizon trader who reads the muted price response as 'noise flow' and supplies liquidity against it, and the edge persists because attention and processing capacity are scarce precisely where fundamentals are hard to interpret.

factors.name: RINN Mediation-Depth of Order Flow (Sparse Redundant-Path Decomposition)
factors.description: For each name, run a rolling sparse (soft-thresholded, paper-style error-vs-L1 'distance-to-origin' threshold selection) regression of one-bar returns on four redundant copies of contemporaneous signed-flow — own, industry-peer mean ex-self, sector mean, market mean — then form the fitted flow impulse and multiply it by a mediation-depth score (|coefficient|-weighted mean level index), flipping sign for shallow/direct-only injection versus deep/hierarchically-propagated injection.
factors.trading_idea: Young et al. build a network in which a known cause is fed *redundantly* into every level of a latent hierarchy, and L1 sparsity reveals at which depth the cause actually enters and how far it propagates before reaching the output. Translated to markets: the observed cause is signed trade flow, the latent mediators are the peer-group (industry), sector and market states, and the output is the name's next return. Flow that only loads on the direct, unmediated path (a shock absorbed purely by the name's own quote, no peer co-movement) is inventory-driven liquidity demand and mechanically reverts as market makers unwind; flow that loads through the deeper mediated paths (industry/sector latent states also moving) is information whose repricing is staggered because sector-level hedging and slow-moving capital arrive over many bars, so it continues. The falsifier: if the sparse path coefficients on the direct versus mediated inputs carry the same forward-return sign, or if depth-of-injection has no persistence across estimation windows, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Haar Energy-Cascade Degradation Gate (Detail-per-Volume Flip)
factors.description: Computes causal undecimated (stationary) Haar detail energies of log mid-price at scales 1,2,4,8 bars over a rolling window, regresses log2 energy on log2 scale and takes the excess of the fitted slope over the random-walk benchmark; combines this with finest-scale detail energy normalised by traded volume to build a soft two-sided gate that weights (a) the signed low-frequency approximation drift (continuation when the path is over-smoothed / low detail-per-volume) against (b) the signed finest-scale detail coefficient (fade when detail is inflated per unit volume), then cross-sectionally standardises the blend within sector.
factors.trading_idea: GDSR's core observation is that a degraded (low-resolution) image keeps ~92% of its energy in the low-frequency band while the true high-resolution image keeps ~24% in high-frequency detail — degradation is a *low-pass filter*, and reconstruction requires knowing which branch (global/low-pass vs detail/high-pass) is trustworthy. The observed 10-second mid-price path is likewise a filtered view of the latent efficient price, but it is distorted in two opposite ways: quote staleness, tick-grid pinning and thin participation *attenuate* high-frequency detail (an over-smoothed, 'low-resolution' path whose low-frequency drift under-states information already arrived, so the next bars catch up), while bid-ask bounce and fleeting quotes *inflate* high-frequency detail (transitory wiggles that revert). Fitting the Haar detail-energy cascade across dyadic scales against the random-walk benchmark slope, and normalising finest-scale detail energy by contemporaneous traded volume ('detail per trade'), separates these two regimes per name per moment and tells us whether to ride the low-frequency drift or fade the finest-scale impulse. This should be falsified if the same directional carriers earn identical forward returns with the cascade/detail-per-volume gate held constant — i.e. if the interaction term is flat; the counterparty is the market maker whose stale or bouncing quotes create the distortion, and it persists because the decomposition is noisy per name, capacity-limited, and only pays over ~1 minute.

factors.name: Mean-Pooled Path Embedding vs Terminal-Token Collapse Gap
factors.description: For each name, build a per-bar embedding (signed log return, close location within the bar range, log-volume surprise vs rolling median, return x volume pressure, normalized range), form the uniform mean-pooled representation A over a ~30-bar window and the terminal/recency-weighted representation B, whiten both by rolling per-feature dispersion, and output the cross-sectionally ranked combination: directional component of A minus beta times the directional component of (B - A) scaled by tanh of the Mahalanobis distance ||B - A||.
factors.trading_idea: Guo & Hauptmann find that mean-pooled (aggregated) token representations forecast forward returns better than the single 'bottleneck' last-token vector, which suffers representation collapse / over-squashing. Read a stock's recent bar sequence as a token sequence with a small per-bar microstructure embedding: the uniform-pooled representation encodes the persistent, multi-bar informed order flow, while the terminal bar is the analogue of the collapse-prone last token — dominated by one aggressive print, a fleeting quote, or a stale mid. The bet is therefore two-sided: follow the whitened directional component of the pooled path representation, and fade the part of the terminal bar that the pooled representation does not support, with the fade weight scaling in the Mahalanobis 'collapse' distance between terminal and pooled vectors. Counterparties are last-print chasers and momentum-ignition flow; the edge persists because inventory-constrained market makers cannot instantly absorb the terminal-print dislocation. It is killed if the bottleneck-excess term loads positively (continuation) rather than negatively at 6 bars.

factors.name: Log-Periodic Oscillation Contraction Critical-Time Reversal
factors.description: Per ticker over a causal rolling window (~360 bars), extract alternating local extrema of the mid-price via a volatility-scaled zig-zag, regress log inter-extremum durations on extremum index to estimate the contraction factor λ and fit quality R², extrapolate the critical time Tc = t_last + d_last/(λ−1) from the convergent geometric series, and emit a signal equal to minus the sign of the current leg's direction, scaled by a Gaussian proximity kernel on |Tc − t| (peaking when Tc is ~6 bars ahead), by exp(-|log(λ/2)|) closeness to the preferred scaling factor, and by R²; the result is cross-sectionally demeaned and rank-normalised each bar, and set to zero for names with too few extrema, diverging λ≤1, or poor geometric fit.
factors.trading_idea: Drożdż & Oświęcimka argue that trends driven by positive feedback terminate when their internal oscillations accelerate geometrically toward a finite critical time, with a preferred contraction factor λ≈2. The same self-reinforcing mechanics exist intraday: momentum-chasing and stop-cascade order flow produce a sequence of pullbacks in the same direction whose durations shrink roughly geometrically as liquidity providers step away; once the geometric series converges, the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted and the micro-trend snaps back. The edge is therefore not the trend itself but the *timing signature of its exhaustion* — only names whose recent local-extremum spacings contract with a stable ratio near 2 and whose extrapolated critical time lands inside the next few bars are faded. Falsifiable: if the fade works equally well when the duration-contraction ratio is random (λ far from 2) or the geometric fit is poor, the log-periodic mechanism adds nothing beyond ordinary short-horizon reversal and the idea is dead. Who is on the other side: late trend-followers and passive VWAP slicers who cannot condition on path shape; the inefficiency persists because the pattern is short-lived, name-specific and requires per-stock path parsing rather than a cross-sectional score.

factors.name: Interventional Shock-Propagation Gain (Confounder-Adjusted Peer Relay)
factors.description: For each ordered same-sector pair (j->i), estimate an interventional propagation gain from past shock events in j (|standardized return| above a robust MAD threshold with confirming volume spike), regressing i's confounder-adjusted forward cumulative return over bars t+1..t+6 (residualized against the sector composite excluding i and j, i.e. back-door adjustment) on the signed shock magnitude of j; gains are shrunk to zero unless their sign is stable across two sub-windows (sticky-regime check) and links are dropped when i is itself under intervention. The live signal is the gain-weighted sum of currently fresh peer shocks, cross-sectionally demeaned within sector.
factors.trading_idea: CausalTimePrior's central lesson (Appendix J) is that observational co-movement is a bad guide to what happens after an intervention: a peer with -0.49 correlation can have ~zero causal effect, and correlation-fitted VAR mispredicts by 177x. Intraday, large idiosyncratic price jumps accompanied by abnormal volume act like hard interventions on a name — for a few bars its price is driven by exogenous order flow rather than by its usual factor parents — and only some peers genuinely absorb that shock over the next 1-5 bars, while most co-move only through the common sector/market confounder. Estimating propagation gains *conditional on past intervention events*, on returns that have been back-door adjusted for the sector composite, isolates true relay links; trading fresh shocks only through those validated links should earn the slow-diffusion premium while abstaining on spuriously correlated names. Falsifier: if event-conditional gains have no more forward predictive power than plain contemporaneous betas (or if sign-stability gating adds nothing), the causal framing is empty and the factor should collapse to noise.

factors.name: Sign-Concordance vs Linear Beta Wedge Catch-up/Overshoot Flip
factors.description: Over a rolling intraday window, per ticker compute (i) the sign-concordance-implied correlation with the cross-sectional market return, rho_sgn = sin(pi/2 * mean(sign(r_i)*sign(m))), (ii) the Pearson correlation rho_lin and implied beta = rho_sgn * sigma_i/sigma_m, and (iii) the wedge = rho_sgn - rho_lin (the paper's non-elliptical discrepancy, additionally conditioned on the |r_i|,|m| amplitude-coupling level). The factor is the cross-sectionally standardised, volatility-scaled residual (beta_implied * market cumulative return over the last few bars - stock cumulative return) multiplied by tanh of the scaled wedge, so positive-wedge names trade as catch-up and negative-wedge names trade as reversal.
factors.trading_idea: Chicheportiche & Bouchaud show that stock dependence is not elliptical: the copula centre point (pure sign concordance) implies a coupling strength that systematically disagrees with the Pearson correlation, because directional co-movement and amplitude (volatility-mode) co-movement are driven by different factors. I exploit that wedge as a state variable for how a stock is currently attached to the market: when sign-implied coupling EXCEEDS linear coupling, the name is directionally glued to the index but its magnitude response is diluted by idiosyncratic amplitude bursts, so a market impulse it has not yet matched in size is a reliable catch-up trade; when linear coupling EXCEEDS sign-implied coupling, the attachment is amplitude/co-jump driven (ETF and hedging flow slamming both together with unreliable direction), so the same gap is an overshoot that reverts. Practitioners hedge and forecast with Pearson betas only, so the nonlinear sign-vs-magnitude discrepancy is unpriced; it is killed if the wedge has no interaction with the sign of the market-impulse residual.

factors.name: Group-Delay Reassigned Transient Age & Concentration Flip
factors.description: For each ticker, causally convolve standardized log returns with analytic Morlet wavelets at several dyadic scales using only past bars, form the time-reassignment (group-delay) estimate tau_j = b - Re(W_{tg}/W_g) at each scale, refine it with 2-3 fixed-point iterations (the WTMSST correction) to get tau^[N], then build (i) impulse age = median_j(b - tau_j^[N]), (ii) a concentration score from low Renyi entropy of the synchrosqueezed energy along the lag axis plus low cross-scale dispersion of tau_j, and (iii) the volume-weighted signed return in a short window around the located event bar; the factor is the cross-sectionally standardized product of the signed impulse magnitude, an age-decay weight, and a concentration term that flips sign (reversal when the transient is sharply localized, continuation when its energy is smeared and its group delay drifts across scales).
factors.trading_idea: Dong & Yu's time-reassigned synchrosqueezing shows that for transient (impulse-like) signals the informative state variable is not instantaneous frequency but the GROUP DELAY — the time at which the burst's energy is truly centred — and that iterating the fixed-point GD estimate reveals whether the burst is a sharp one-off spike or a still-evolving, frequency-varying event. In 10-second equity bars, a return path is a superposition of such transients: sharp, time-concentrated bursts whose group delay agrees across scales are almost always liquidity/inventory shocks (one impatient parent order sweeping the book), and mechanical resilience of market makers pulls price back within a minute; bursts whose energy is smeared over many bars with scale-dependent, drifting group delay reflect gradual information diffusion by many participants and instead continue. The trade is therefore not 'reversal' or 'momentum' but a flip conditioned on the energy-concentration geometry of the transient, with the impulse's measured AGE (how many bars ago the reassigned energy centre sits) controlling how much of the response is already spent. It is falsified if, cross-sectionally, sign-flipped predictability disappears once one conditions on concentration — i.e. if concentrated and diffuse bursts have the same 6-bar continuation, or if the signal collapses to plain short-horizon reversal on raw returns. The other side is the liquidity demander who must trade now and cannot distinguish their own footprint from news; the edge persists because at 10-second scale the required inference (multi-scale phase geometry, not just return magnitude) is costly and capacity is small.

factors.name: Distress-Hazard-Gated Order-Flow Convexity (Entropy-Confidence Filtered)
factors.description: Builds a point-in-time distress-hazard state from cross-sectionally standardised Altman-style ratios (workingCapital/totalAssets, retainedEarnings/totalLiabilities, ebit/totalAssets, marketCap/totalLiabilities, revenue/totalAssets), converts each to a distress probability, and forms a confidence weight from the binary entropy of the averaged probability times component agreement (1 - normalised cross-component dispersion); this slow gate multiplies a fast normalised signed-volume pressure term (rolling sum of sign(close-open)*volume scaled by its own rolling volatility), so the factor is long flow-continuation in confidently high-hazard names and long flow-reversal in confidently low-hazard names, demeaned each bar.
factors.trading_idea: Kim & Yoon's hazard model treats failure risk as a latent state variable built from Altman-type balance-sheet ratios, and their key methodological move is to trust the signal only for observations whose evidence is unambiguous (low self-entropy pseudo-label filtering). I map both pieces to intraday equity microstructure: for a highly levered, low-retained-earnings, thin-market-value-of-equity-to-liabilities firm, the equity claim is a convex, option-like residual on asset value, so informed order flow is much more price-relevant and liquidity providers withdraw depth rather than absorb it — flow imbalance should CONTINUE over the next minute. For low-hazard, well-capitalised names the same imbalance is mostly inventory noise that market makers absorb and revert. The confidence filter is the analogue of self-entropy screening: only act when the several hazard components agree, because a hazard score assembled from mutually contradictory ratios is a noisy label. It persists because mandate constraints, short-sale frictions and risk limits keep slow institutional capital out of distress names, leaving intraday discovery to a thin set of liquidity providers who are undercompensated for adverse selection; it dies if the flow-continuation coefficient fails to increase monotonically across hazard quantiles.

factors.name: Capital-Structure-Elastic Earning-Yield Overshoot Snapback
factors.description: Converts recent multi-bar returns into implied earning-yield changes (ΔEY ≈ −(ebit/EV)·(marketCap/EV)·r), normalises this valuation-space move by contemporaneous traded volume (overshoot per unit of liquidity consumed), and takes its negated cross-sectional rank, with magnitude gated by whether the move contradicts or confirms a causal extrapolation of the firm's quarterly EBIT/EV path (level plus last report-to-report delta, supported by ebitGrowth / revenueGrowth / incomeQuality).
factors.trading_idea: The paper's object of interest is not price but the state variable EBIT/EV (earning yield) and its forward trajectory; because EV = equity + net debt, a given equity return translates into an earning-yield change amplified by the equity share of EV (marketCap/EV) and by the level of EBIT/EV itself. Intraday liquidity demanders trade percentage price moves and are blind to capital structure, so in valuation space a 30-basis-point move in a high-net-debt, high-EBIT-yield name is a far larger revision of the fundamental anchor than the same move in a debt-free name, and it is much more likely to be inventory-driven overshoot rather than information. The slow fundamental capital described in the paper re-anchors only on earning yield, so such valuation-space overshoots — especially those achieved on little traded volume and pointing *against* the firm's recently reported EBIT/EV trajectory — get refilled by market makers within roughly a minute, while moves that confirm the fundamental trajectory should not be shorted. Falsification: if the leverage/earning-yield elasticity weighting and the trajectory-agreement gate add no incremental IC over plain volume-normalised short-horizon reversal, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Sign-Split Hawkes Branching Asymmetry Cascade Projection
factors.description: For each ticker, builds up-flow and down-flow event series from volume signed by intra-bar direction, maintains exponentially decayed self/cross excitation states, estimates a 2x2 branching matrix G by rolling causal non-negative least squares, and outputs the (I-G)^{-1}-amplified projected net signed flow over the next 6 bars (scaled by baseline intensity, gated to subcritical spectral radius), cross-sectionally ranked and residualized against the trailing 6-bar return rank so it is not a restatement of short-horizon momentum.
factors.trading_idea: El Karmi's calibrations show equity order flow is strongly endogenous (branching ratio ~0.8) with a *multivariate* excitation matrix, so what matters is not only how much activity begets activity but whether buy-side events excite buys (diagonal G) or excite the opposite side (off-diagonal G, i.e. market-maker inventory unwinds and HFT ping-pong). I split each name's 10-second bar flow into up-tick and down-tick volume, fit a causal bivariate exponential-kernel excitation matrix G over a rolling intraday window, and project the current decayed excitation state forward through (I-G)^{-1} to get the expected *net signed* flow of the next few bars. Names whose branching structure is diagonal-dominant and near-critical will keep pushing price in the direction of the current cascade; names whose off-diagonal cross-excitation dominates should see the current imbalance absorbed and reversed. This is falsified if the diagonal-vs-off-diagonal split carries no incremental information beyond raw signed imbalance; it persists because inventory-constrained liquidity providers and latency-limited participants cannot instantaneously re-price the endogenous continuation of a cascade they are absorbing.

factors.name: Volatility-Timescale (Jensen-Gap / Comovement) Gated Barrier Bounce
factors.description: Over a trailing intraday window, computes per name (i) barrier position p = normalized location of close inside the window high-low range plus vol-scaled distance to the running low/high, (ii) a vol-timescale block from the per-bar vol proxy h (range/mid and |return|): Jensen gap G = sqrt(mean h^2)/mean h, AR(1)-based mean-reversion speed kappa = 1 - phi of log h, and comovement attenuation A = mean(h_i * h_mkt) / (rms_i * rms_mkt) with h_mkt the cross-sectional median vol; the factor is the cross-sectionally standardized barrier-reversal term multiplied by a centered gate combining ranks of kappa and G (transient, favour snapback) against the rank of A (systemic, favour continuation), so the reversal sign flips for persistent, market-comoving vol.
factors.trading_idea: Hambly & Kolliopoulos show that a stochastic-vol barrier system collapses onto a constant-vol one only in the fast-mean-reverting limit, and that the *effective* parameters differ: the relevant diffusion scale is the RMS vol sigma_2 = sqrt(E[h^2]), the relevant drift/market loading uses the mean vol sigma_1 = E[h], and the effective systemic correlation is scaled by sigma_tilde = sqrt(E[h_i h_j]) — the cross-name comovement of volatilities. Translated to intraday equities: a name pushed close to a local barrier (session-window low or high) by a *transient, idiosyncratic* vol burst (large Jensen gap sigma_2/sigma_1, fast-mean-reverting vol, low vol comovement with the market) has an absorption hazard that is overstated by the naive constant-vol read, so liquidity providers who widened out step back in and the move snaps back; a name at the barrier under *persistent, systemically comoving* vol has a genuinely elevated hazard and continues. The signal therefore flips the sign of short-horizon barrier reversal on vol timescale and vol comovement rather than trading reversal unconditionally. It is falsified if barrier-proximity reversal profit is invariant to the estimated vol mean-reversion speed / Jensen gap / vol-comovement gate; the counterparty is the fast trader who treats every vol spike as regime-persistent, and the edge persists because separating transient from persistent vol in real time requires the second-moment structure of the vol path, not just its level.

factors.name: Cross-Sector Co-Burst Attention Spillover Reversal
factors.description: Builds a rolling co-burst adjacency matrix from abnormal-volume burst indicators (double-centered and stripped of the same-sector pair average to remove fundamental linkage and market-wide burst factors), computes peer eigenvector centrality by power iteration, forms each stock's centrality-weighted joint co-burst intensity, orthogonalizes it cross-sectionally against its unaccompanied 'self-burst' intensity, and shorts high joint-attention names scaled by their contemporaneous run-up over the same window (long the mirror image).
factors.trading_idea: Guo-Peng-Tao-Tu show that *joint* coverage of firms spreads attention across investor bases, inflates prices contemporaneously and reverses shortly after, while purely idiosyncratic (self) coverage has no such aggregate reversal, and the effect survives orthogonalization against fundamental/topic linkages. At 10-second frequency the observable analogue of joint coverage is synchronous abnormal-volume bursting: when a stock repeatedly bursts in the *same bars* as high-centrality, non-same-sector peers, its order flow is being driven by broad attention-chasing (screeners, headline scans, index/basket clickthrough) rather than its own information, so the price impact is transitory. The counterparty is the attention-driven marginal buyer paying up during the shared burst; liquidity providers absorbing that flow require a small reversal to be compensated, and the effect persists because unwinding within a minute is only profitable to intermediaries already in the queue. Falsifiable: if the reversal instead comes from the same-sector (fundamentally linked) part of the co-burst matrix, or if the self-burst (idiosyncratic, unaccompanied) burst component carries the same predictive sign, the attention-spillover interpretation is dead.

factors.name: Latent-Alignment OOD Gate on Dynamics-Consistency Residual
factors.description: Per ticker, builds a 5-dim causal latent vector per bar (standardized return, |return|, high-low range over |close-open| roughness, de-medianed log volume, sign(return)*log volume), estimates the RBF-MMD between a short target window (~30 bars) and a lagged long source buffer (~360 bars) using fixed random Fourier features so the mean embeddings are rolling sums; separately fits a one-step linear forward-dynamics map on the source buffer and takes the mean target-window forward-prediction residual in the return coordinate (the drift the stock's own in-sample dynamics cannot explain). The factor is the cross-sectionally standardized dynamics residual multiplied by a gate tanh(k*(2*xs_rank(MMD)-1)) with a negative sign, so high-distribution-shift names get reversal weight and in-distribution names get continuation weight.
factors.trading_idea: ILA argues that a frozen policy keeps working only while the encoder's latent features stay in the distribution it was calibrated on; when the latent distribution shifts, the policy's outputs become unreliable and must be re-aligned. Market analogue: liquidity providers price a stock with a quoting/inventory rule calibrated to that stock's own recent microstructural 'latent' regime (return scale, path roughness, volume intensity, signed-flow mix). When the last few minutes of latent features are out-of-distribution relative to the stock's own reference buffer, the pricing rule is effectively running out-of-support, and the price drift it produces is a mechanical artefact of mis-calibrated liquidity provision (transient demand from hedging, index/basket flow, stale quoting) rather than information — it should snap back over the next minute. When the latents stay in-distribution, the same drift is generated by the rule operating normally on informed flow and tends to persist. The edge is the interaction, not the drift itself: it dies if the reversal/continuation coefficient on the drift residual is insensitive to the measured distribution shift.

factors.name: Grounded Latent-Action Manifold vs Off-Policy Transition Residual
factors.description: Per bar, build a causal 4-dim microstate (trailing-standardized return, relative range, close-location-in-range, log-volume), remove the pooled ridge-predicted part of the transition to get an innovation, take the top-k (k=2-3) rolling PCA directions of pooled innovations as the continuous latent action z, decode z into an expected forward return with a lag-safe rolling ridge (the 'action decoder'), and go long the cross-sectionally demeaned decoded latent action minus a weighted, demeaned off-manifold residual return component (reconstruction error of the forward model).
factors.trading_idea: CLAM's core object is a *continuous* latent action inferred from a state transition by an inverse dynamics model, kept honest by a forward model and grounded to real actions by a jointly-fit decoder. At 10-second resolution the unobserved 'action' driving a name's microstate transition is aggregate order-flow control: parent-order slicing, index/ETF hedging, market-maker inventory unwinds. Transitions that lie on the low-dimensional shared latent-action manifold are the footprint of an ongoing control input that has not finished executing, so their decoded (grounded) direction should persist over the next minute; transitions with large off-manifold reconstruction residual are idiosyncratic liquidity accidents that mean-revert, because the liquidity providers absorbing them cannot distinguish the two ex ante and demand compensation.
