This dies if the rolling decoder coefficients mapping latent actions to forward returns are unstable/insignificant, or if off-manifold residual return shows continuation rather than snapback.

factors.name: Water-Filled Liquidity-Yield Centroid Dislocation
factors.description: Over a rolling 60-bar window, build a price-level histogram (≈15 bins spanning the window high-low, anchored on the current close) of traded volume a_i and bar dwell time b_i, solve the paper's KKT water-filling allocation x_i = max(0, sqrt(a_i*b_i/(nu - c_i)) - b_i) by bisection on nu with sum(x)=1 (c_i a small linear inventory-depreciation tilt built from within-window up/down semivariance asymmetry and distance from the current price), then take the x-weighted bin-price centroid minus the last close, scaled by window range, and cross-sectionally residualise it against the volume-weighted (VWAP) centroid displacement computed on the same window.
factors.trading_idea: Powers (2024) shows that the fee-maximising allocation of liquidity across price ticks is NOT centred on the current price: because fees are shared pro rata, the marginal value of adding depth at a level scales with traded volume there but is discounted by the depth already resting there, so capital piles into 'wells' — levels with high trade intensity relative to standing liquidity — and tapers asymmetrically once inventory-depreciation is priced in. Mapping this to equities on a 10-second grid, volume executed inside a price bin proxies the fee revenue a_i of that tick, while the dwell time price spends inside the bin proxies the standing liquidity b_i (price crawls through thick books and jumps through thin ones). Solving the paper's concave water-filling program over the recent price-level grid yields a provision distribution whose centroid marks the level with the greatest unserved liquidity-yield, i.e. where marginal depth will actually be posted and where residual two-sided interest resides; over the next minute price is drawn toward that yield centroid rather than toward the plain volume centroid. The signal is the yield-centroid displacement from the last price, residualised cross-sectionally against the ordinary volume-profile (VWAP) displacement, so the edge is precisely the concave saturation/loss-avoidance correction that the paper isolates and that naive volume-profile reversion traders ignore; it dies if the residualised component carries no incremental information beyond VWAP pull-back.

factors.name: Saliency-Pivot Frame Opposition Volume Gate
factors.description: For each ticker over a trailing ~30-bar window, computes the exact gradient of the path-efficiency statistic R/S with respect to each bar return, normalises |g_t| to [0,1] and thresholds it (paper-style) to define the salient pivot-frame set; the factor is sign(R) times the negative volume-share tilt of those salient frames (volume share minus count share, scaled by |R/S|), cross-sectionally demeaned each bar.
factors.trading_idea: The stroke-rehab paper's core object is not a classifier but a *frame-level saliency map*: a small subset of frames carries almost all of the gradient of a path-level outcome, and whether those salient frames are 'compensatory' or 'normal' determines the label. Mapped to a price path, take the causal, analytically differentiable path-level readout f = (sum of bar log-returns) / sqrt(sum of squared bar log-returns) (directional efficiency of the last window) and compute its exact per-bar gradient g_t = 1/S - R*r_t/S^3. This gradient is largest precisely on the counter-trend 'pivot' frames — the bars where marginal flow would most change the path's directional efficiency — so a saliency map plus the paper's [0,1] normalisation and threshold rule isolates the pullback frames inside a directional move. The tradeable interaction is whether those pivot frames carry unusual *volume*: heavy opposing volume at the salient frames means real absorption by resting liquidity/informed sellers and the move mean-reverts over the next minute, while thin pivot frames mean the move is meeting no genuine resistance and continues. Falsified if the volume tilt of salient frames has no incremental sign predictability beyond raw window return and realized volatility; the counterparty is the trend-chasing taker who cannot see that his pullbacks were absorbed on size.

factors.name: MP-Edge Gated Saturated-Return Eigen-Residual Reversal
factors.description: Over a rolling window, standardise per-name 10s log returns, apply tanh, estimate theta1=E[f^2] and theta2=(E[f'])^2, eigendecompose the saturated cross-sectional Gram matrix, keep only eigen-directions above the Marchenko-Pastur edge (theta1-theta2)(1+sqrt(N/m))^2, and take the negative of each name's recent cumulative residual off that verified subspace, scaled by the above-edge eigenvalue mass share and tilted by the raw-vs-saturated loading gap (tail-manufactured beta).
factors.trading_idea: Benigni-Peche show that a pointwise nonlinearity f applied to a data matrix splits its Gram spectrum into a *linear-information* part with weight theta2(f)=(E f')^2, which faithfully carries the underlying factor structure, and an orthogonal part with weight theta1(f)-theta2(f) that behaves as pure isotropic Marchenko-Pastur noise. Translating this to a rolling panel of 10-second cross-sectional returns: a saturating transform tanh(z) keeps the persistent common-factor core while amortising tail bars, so the eigenvalues of the saturated Gram matrix that stand above the MP edge implied by the estimated (theta1-theta2) noise level are the only trustworthy factor directions. Idiosyncratic residuals measured against that verified subspace are genuine microstructural dislocations and revert over the next handful of bars, whereas in windows where almost no eigenvalue clears the MP edge the 'factor' is statistical noise and any residual is meaningless — hence the residual reversal must be gated by the above-edge eigenvalue mass. The extra tilt comes from names whose raw-return factor loading is much larger than their saturated loading: their apparent beta was manufactured by two or three outlier bars (a liquidity air-pocket, not real co-movement), so their attributed residual is even more likely to snap back. The trade is against liquidity-providers' inventory shocks and index/basket sweeps; it dies if residuals in high-signal-share windows continue to drift rather than revert.

factors.name: Sinkhorn Transport-Coherence Gated Price-Mass Displacement
factors.description: Per ticker over a rolling 60-bar window, build two discrete measures on a common range-normalized price grid (volume-weighted price mass of the first vs second half of the window, Dirichlet-shrunk toward uniform with strength inversely proportional to window volume to handle marginal uncertainty), solve the entropy-regularized OT problem with quadratic cost via a few vectorized Sinkhorn iterations, and form the signal as the cross-sectionally standardized net mass displacement multiplied by a demeaned coherence score (squared displacement over total transport work, combined with the negative KL of the optimal plan to the independent coupling), so coherent transport predicts continuation and diffuse transport predicts reversal.
factors.trading_idea: Following the FPD-OT view that a repricing is a transport plan between two volume-over-price measures, the *same* net price displacement can be achieved either by a cheap, near-monotone translation of traded mass (informed, one-sided demand consuming a level and re-anchoring the book) or by an expensive, high-entropy rearrangement in which mass is split and shuffled in both directions (two-sided liquidity churn / inventory recycling around an unchanged fair value). Standard drift/momentum measures collapse to the difference of the marginal means and are blind to this distinction, because with fixed marginals the mean shift is invariant to the plan; only the *cost and entropy of the optimal plan* reveal whether the move was coherent. Hypothesis: displacement accompanied by coherent (low excess-cost, low-KL-to-independence) transport persists over the next minute, while displacement achieved by diffuse transport reverses; falsified if the coherence gate carries no incremental IC over raw displacement, or if the sign of the interaction is unstable across volume terciles. The other side is the liquidity provider who cannot tell coherent from churned flow in real time; it persists because computing the plan requires resolving the intra-window price-mass geometry, which most short-horizon models compress into a single mean or VWAP.

factors.name: Square-Root Impact-Law Displacement Residual, Tail-Ratio Gated
factors.description: Per ticker, causally estimate (i) the local impact exponent beta_i from a rolling Hill tail-index ratio alpha_V/alpha_r of bar |returns| and bar volumes and (ii) a robust impact coefficient c_i as the rolling median of |r|/V^beta_i; then form the signed displacement residual u_t = sign(r_t)*(|r_t| - c_i*V_t^{beta_i}) scaled by rolling return dispersion, accumulate it with exponential decay over the last ~18 bars, cross-sectionally demean/rank it with a negative sign (excess displacement reverts, absorbed-volume deficit continues), and scale the reversal leg by the ranked tail-ratio ksi_i = alpha_r/alpha_V (more concave / more fragile impact => stronger snapback).
factors.trading_idea: Rak et al. show that the empirical price-impact map is concave, r ~ c*V^beta with beta ~ 1/2, and that the exponent is pinned by the ratio of the Hill tail indices of |return| and volume (beta = alpha_V/alpha_r). If that law is the *fair* exchange rate between traded quantity and price displacement, then the part of a bar's move NOT explained by its own volume is displacement bought without order flow — impatient/uninformed liquidity demand, stop cascades, or quote drift on thin books — and should be given back, whereas volume that is absorbed with less move than the law implies signals hidden supply/iceberg execution that keeps pushing the same way. The residual is falsifiable in a specific way: if the edge survives only as a function of raw signed return and dies once the volume-implied term is subtracted, the mechanism is wrong and it is just plain reversal. Who pays: liquidity-demanding traders crossing beyond the impact-implied price; who collects: market makers who must be compensated for inventory, and the persistence comes from their finite risk capital over seconds-to-minutes, not from mispriced fundamentals.

factors.name: Validated Pinball-Quantile Tail-Asymmetry Drift
factors.description: For each ticker, ridge-penalised linear quantile (pinball) regressions at tau=0.10 and tau=0.90 of realised 6-bar-ahead returns on a small causal state vector (signed flow imbalance, realised absolute-return level, range compression, volume surprise) are fit on a rolling window whose targets are fully realised; the fitted quantiles are evaluated at the current state, and the factor is the *sum* of the two quantile deviations from their unconditional in-window levels (the location/asymmetry component, with the symmetric widening component projected out), each tau weighted by a soft gate equal to its pinball-loss improvement over the naive unconditional quantile on a held-out validation tail of the window, then vol-scaled and cross-sectionally standardised.
factors.trading_idea: Chi et al. (2025) show that the informative, predictable part of a conditional distribution is often a *tail* shift rather than a mean shift, that pinball (quantile) loss recovers it far more robustly than squared loss under fat tails, and that such a forecast should only be trusted when it beats the unconditional quantile out-of-sample. At 10-second frequency the conditional mean of returns is almost pure microstructure noise, but the joint location shift of the upper and lower conditional quantiles given the current flow/liquidity state is a much more robust estimate of genuine short-horizon drift; liquidity providers quote roughly symmetric spreads around mid and price the median, not asymmetric tail risk, so this drift is only slowly impounded. The signal is deliberately orthogonalised against the symmetric (pure-volatility) quantile widening, so a purely vol-driven state must produce zero exposure — if the edge survives only through the symmetric component, the mechanism is falsified.

factors.name: Visibility-Graph Allometry Gate on Line-of-Sight Price Spikes
factors.description: On a rolling causal window of mid prices per ticker, build the natural visibility graph (bar i and j mutually visible if all intermediate mids lie below the connecting line), weight edges by average log-price acceleration as in the paper, extract a minimal-weight visibility parent tree, estimate the Banavar A/C allometric exponent eta by log-log OLS (falling back to normalized degree entropy if degenerate), and combine it with the latest bar's backward visibility degree and its signed distance from the window median: signal = (2*eta - 3) * (degree_t / window) * standardized signed protrusion, cross-sectionally ranked so star-like protrusions are faded and chain-like protrusions are followed.
factors.trading_idea: Qian, Jiang & Zhou map a price path into a visibility graph and show that the allometric exponent eta of its spanning tree (C ~ A^eta, eta in (1,2)) discriminates star-like paths — dominated by one spike that everything else can see — from chain-like paths, and that deviations from the Brownian benchmark are driven by fat tails plus nonlinear correlation, i.e. exactly the two microstructural regimes an intraday trader cares about. My claim is that the same topology tells you whether the *current* bar's protrusion above the local price hull is a liquidity accident or genuine information: in a star-like window (eta near 1, one dominant hub, fat-tailed single-print spike) the protruding bar is a transient liquidity vacuum print that market makers refill, so it mean-reverts over the next few bars; in a chain-like window (eta near 2, degrees spread along a persistent path, nonlinear long-memory drift) the same protrusion is a genuine breakout that continues. The other side of the trade is the marketable-order flow that pays up into thin books, and the edge persists because visibility-graph topology is a non-standard, path-shape statistic (not a moment of returns) that neither vol/momentum screens nor standard queue models encode. It is killed if the eta gate carries no incremental IC over the raw signed protrusion, i.e. if star-like and chain-like windows give the same forward sign.

factors.name: H0 Single-Linkage Attachment-Gated Intra-Cluster Snapback
factors.description: On a rolling window of 10-second returns, build d_ij = sqrt(2(1-rho_ij)), run the single-linkage (H0) filtration, and for each stock record (a) its merge/attachment height, (b) its cell membership at the epsilon given by the largest persistent gap in merge heights; the signal is minus the stock's recent return gap versus its cell mean (cell excluding self, vol-normalised), scaled by cross-sectional attachment tightness (low merge height = strong) and by a squashed Wasserstein-1 shift of the H0 merge-height diagram versus T bars earlier.
factors.trading_idea: The TDA literature builds market turbulence indices from the 0-dimensional persistent homology of the correlation-distance point cloud (Gidea 2017; Gidea-Katz 2018; Baitinger-Flegel PHTI), but the H0 filtration also carries per-name information that is normally thrown away: the filtration height at which each stock's connected component merges into a larger one is exactly how tightly that stock is welded to a comovement cell. My claim is that intra-cell dispersion and idiosyncratic dispersion are economically different objects at the 10-second scale: for a stock with a very low merge height (a near-duplicate of its neighbours in correlation-distance), a short-run gap versus its cell is almost always one-sided liquidity demand hitting a single leg, and market makers / cross-sectional stat-arb capital push it back within tens of seconds; for a topologically peripheral stock (high merge height, only joins at large epsilon) the same gap is genuine idiosyncratic news and does not revert. Additionally, when the H0 persistence diagram itself lurches (large Wasserstein-1 move in the multiset of merge heights versus a few minutes earlier — the PHTI raw index), correlations are tightening market-wide, cells become more binding, and the snapback is faster and more reliable, so the diagram-shift magnitude is the natural conditioning gate. Falsification: if reversion strength is flat or increasing in merge height, or if the PHTI-style diagram-shift gate does not amplify it, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Stock–Bar Activity Commonality (ACC) Split of Impulse Continuation
factors.description: Over a rolling causal window, build the stock×bar bipartite adjacency M[i,t] = 1{ (v_it / sum_t v_it) / (sum_i v_it / sum_i sum_t v_it) >= 1 }, compute bar commonality k_t = sum_i M[i,t] and each stock's Average Commonality Coefficient ACC_i = mean of k_t over its own active bars (method of reflections, first order), residualized cross-sectionally against its own degree/diversification k_i so it is not a volume-count proxy; the factor is the stock's activity-bar-weighted cumulative log return multiplied by the sign-flipping niche score -(rank(ACC_resid) - 0.5), i.e. continuation for niche-bar impulses and reversal for crowded-bar impulses.
factors.trading_idea: Flori et al. build a bipartite fund–asset network, define a link by a Revealed-Comparative-Advantage threshold on relative holdings, and show that agents whose portfolio sits on *niche* (low-commonality) nodes earn persistent alpha while those loaded on *popular* nodes earn none and get crushed in fire-sale episodes. The intraday analogue of 'holdings' is where a name spends its trading activity: replace funds by stocks and constituents by 10-second bars, and link stock i to bar t when i's relative volume share in t exceeds the market-average share (the RCA condition). A bar's commonality is then how many names burst simultaneously in it — high-commonality bars are market-wide/basket-ETF/news-window flow, low-commonality bars are idiosyncratic, likely informed flow. Hypothesis (falsifiable): a price impulse accumulated in *niche* bars is information and continues over the next ~6 bars, whereas the same impulse accumulated in *crowded* bars is undifferentiated liquidity demand shared with the whole cross-section and mean-reverts as the basket pressure clears; if impulses in crowded and niche bars decay identically, the factor dies. The other side is the index/basket liquidity taker who is mandate-forced to trade the whole cross-section at once and cannot distinguish its own footprint from information.

factors.name: Liquidity-Depletion Stock: Priced vs Physical Disaster-Hazard Wedge, Gated by Fiscal Space
factors.description: Builds a per-name decaying depletion stock F (EWMA of volume-weighted adverse price impact net of high-volume/low-impact replenishment bars), estimates the cross-sectional power-law physical adverse-jump intensity nu_P = a + b*F^psi from trailing tail-jump counts via robust log-log fit, estimates the market-implied sensitivity by regressing each name's sector-relative drawdown (its 'spread') on F^psi, and trades the standardized wedge (implied-minus-physical intensity) multiplied by a fiscal-space gate built from debtToAssets, interestCoverage, cashRatio and quickRatio ranks (positive for ample-space names, mildly negative for near-barrier levered names).
factors.trading_idea: Barucci-Marazzina-Nassigh model a slow-moving 'pollution stock' (extraction minus natural decay minus replenishment) that both damages drift and raises the intensity of rare disasters, and find that the market-implied disaster intensity calibrated from spreads is ~100x the physically estimated one — i.e. stock-driven catastrophe risk is grossly over-compensated, while the actual default barrier is only reached at extreme debt levels. The equity analogue: one-sided liquidity depletion accumulates as a decaying stock in a name, market makers and risk systems mark the name down (widen its 'spread' versus sector) in proportion to that stock, but the realized frequency of adverse jumps rises far less than the discount implies. Buying the wedge (priced sensitivity to depletion minus physically justified hazard) should earn short-horizon reversion, and — exactly as in the paper's default barrier and 'y >> B' abatement condition — only for names with ample balance-sheet fiscal space; for highly levered names, near the barrier, the discount is justified and should persist. Falsifier: if the wedge has no forward-return relation, or if it pays identically in high- and low-leverage names, the intensity-mispricing mechanism is wrong.

factors.name: Byzantine-Filtered Consensus Residual with Volume-Conditioned Sign Split
factors.description: Builds a K x H matrix of each ticker's last H=12 bar log-return path, runs a few iterations of Steinhardt-style robust mean estimation (weights c_i down-weighted by the squared projection of the residual onto the top eigenvector of the c-weighted covariance) to get the honest consensus path and per-name outlier score tau_i and corruption weight (1 - c_i); the signal is minus the signed projection of the name's residual path onto that dominant corruption direction, scaled by (1 - c_i), with its sign flipped for names whose recent traded volume is high relative to their own trailing norm (information-driven kappa) rather than low (batch-noise-driven), then cross-sectionally standardized.
factors.trading_idea: Data & Diggavi's robust accumulated-gradient estimator (RAGE / Steinhardt filtering) separates a cross-section of 'client updates' into an honest core with bounded covariance and a small set of outliers that get iteratively down-weighted along the top eigendirection of the weighted covariance. Treat each ticker's last-H-bar return path as its accumulated local update: the filter then recovers the *honest* market/sector consensus path and simultaneously flags which names are moving along a direction the consensus does not support. The paper's own error decomposition says outlier-ness has two sources — sampling noise sigma^2/b (small batch = thin trade count) and genuine gradient dissimilarity kappa (real heterogeneous information) — so the trade is a sign split: a flagged deviation carried on abnormally *low* traded volume is noise-driven and should snap back toward the robust consensus over the next few bars, while an equally large deviation carried on abnormally *high* volume is genuine idiosyncratic information (kappa) and should persist. The other side is liquidity providers and index/basket traders who mark all deviations from the naive cross-sectional mean as equally informative; the inefficiency persists because separating noise-outliers from information-outliers requires a high-dimensional robust estimate that fast market-makers approximate with a simple mean or beta. Falsified if, conditional on the filter's outlier score, low-volume deviations show no reversal and high-volume deviations no continuation over ~6 bars.

factors.name: Wayward-vs-Cohesive Volume Regime Flip (cross-sectional volume kurtosis gate)
factors.description: Per bar, volume is normalised by each stock's own trailing median volume, then the cross-section is summarised with robust Gram-Charlier cumulants (mean, median, MAD-based dispersion, excess kurtosis as in the paper); the signal is the stock's cross-sectional volume-surprise z-score times its standardised short-window return, sign-gated by a smoothed centred cross-sectional excess-kurtosis state (continuation when tail-driven/'wayward', reversal when cohesive), finally cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Graczyk & Duarte Queiros show that a rise in trading volume means two structurally different things: when the cross-sectional distribution of volume is strongly leptokurtic, the aggregate activity is carried by a few 'wayward' stocks digesting name-specific information, whereas when the cross-sectional distribution is near-mesokurtic the volume rise is a cohesive, market-wide phenomenon (session-clock / inventory / rebalancing flow with no name-specific news). A stock's own volume spike therefore carries information about the next few bars only in the tail-driven regime — the price impact of informed idiosyncratic flow persists — while in the cohesive regime the same spike is uninformative liquidity demand whose impact should be paid back. The factor thus takes the stock's cross-sectional volume-surprise z-score, multiplies it by the recent signed price move, and flips the sign of that continuation/reversal bet according to a causally estimated cross-sectional excess-kurtosis state variable. Falsification: if the interaction coefficient between (volume-surprise x recent return) and the kurtosis state is statistically indistinguishable from zero — i.e. spikes predict the same direction in both regimes — the mechanism is dead; the edge persists because market-makers and rebalancers cannot condition inventory replenishment on whether the day's flow is idiosyncratic or common, and slow-moving capital absorbs cohesive flow at a spread rather than a directional forecast.

factors.name: Optional-Pólya median-tree price profile: mode pull vs. vacuum continuation
factors.description: Over a trailing window, prices are mapped to [0,1) by window min/max and each bar contributes volume-weighted mass; an Optional Pólya Tree posterior (Beta(a,a) mass allocation, prior split odds p_l = Gamma^-l, max depth 6, log-space bottom-up recursion for the posterior split probabilities) yields a median tree whose interior nodes are those with posterior inclusion > 1/2, and hence a piecewise-constant adaptive profile density. The factor is the signed, range-normalised distance from the current price to the centroid of the dominant deep high-mass leaf, scaled by that leaf's sharpness (log height ratio vs. median leaf height), and switched in sign toward short-horizon drift continuation when the current price's own leaf is coarse (depth below the tree's median depth) and low-mass; the blended value is then cross-sectionally demeaned/ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Castillo & Randrianarisoa show that Optional Pólya Trees adapt their dyadic split depth to LOCAL regularity of a density: sharp, spiky regions get deep splits, smooth regions stay coarse. Applied to the recent volume-weighted distribution of prices actually visited by a name (a market/volume profile), this gives a principled, self-tuning way to tell a genuine high-volume accumulation shelf from a flat, featureless price region — something a fixed-bin histogram either over-smooths or over-fits. Inventory that was built at a sharp shelf makes that level a behavioural and hedging anchor, so over ~1 minute price is pulled back toward it; conversely, when the current price sits in a coarse, low-mass leaf (a liquidity vacuum with no established inventory) there is nothing to lean against and the prevailing micro-drift extends. The trade is falsified if the pull term has no edge conditional on high median-tree depth at the mode, or if replacing the adaptive OPT resolution by a fixed 32-bin histogram loses nothing; the counterparty is liquidity demanders who chase prints away from established value and market makers who must widen in vacuums.

factors.name: Sector-Basket Drag on Fundamentally Atypical Members (60s Snapback)
factors.description: For each name, estimate the sector-attributable component of its recent (~2 min) move as beta_i times the market-cap-weighted leave-one-out sector return, gate it by a sector basket-flow indicator (sign-synchronization of member returns times sector-wide volume z-score), and short that component in proportion to the stock's within-sector fundamental atypicality — a distance between its cross-sectionally ranked fundamental profile (EV/EBITDA, earnings & FCF yield, P/B, gross & net margin, ROE, debt/equity, asset turnover, revenue growth) and its sector's median profile.
factors.trading_idea: Sector-rotation capital arrives as basket flow: ETF/futures hedgers and sector-tilt programs buy or sell every member roughly in proportion to market cap, indifferent to whether an individual name actually shares its sector's economics. The rotation paper's core evidence is that sectors are coherent bundles of fundamental characteristics (multiples, margins, ROE, leverage, growth), so a member whose fundamental profile sits far from its sector's centroid is a poor economic substitute for the basket — when it is dragged by synchronized sector flow, that portion of its move is mechanical liquidity impact rather than information, and it should snap back within a minute while the typical members' sector-driven move persists. The counterparty is the basket trader who is deliberately price-insensitive at the single-name level plus market makers who must warehouse the imbalance; the edge persists because separating 'belongs to the basket' from 'merely classified in it' requires point-in-time fundamentals mapped onto 10-second flow, which basket desks do not do. It dies if the post-burst reversal of the beta-explained move is statistically independent of fundamental distance from the sector centroid (interaction coefficient ≈ 0), or if reversal is uniform across typical and atypical names.

factors.name: Shuffle-Residualised Multifractal Width Trend/Reversal Flip
factors.description: Per ticker over a rolling window of ~540 bars, estimate generalised scaling exponents H(q) by regressing log[ mean_t |sum of log-returns over s bars|^q ]^(1/q) on log s for aggregation scales s in {1,2,3,6,12,24,48} and q in {0.5,4}; the multifractal width is H(0.5)-H(4). Cross-sectionally residualise this width against a shuffle-invariant tail control (rank of realised kurtosis of |r| and rank of realised vol) — mimicking the paper's shuffled-series control so only temporal-dependence-driven multifractality survives — then multiply the recent vol-normalised 12-bar signed return by the negative of that residualised width rank (continuation for monofractal names, reversal for multifractal ones) and cross-sectionally demean.
factors.trading_idea: Pontiggia (2025) shows that realised-volatility paths need not admit a single Hölder/roughness exponent: the generalised scaling exponent H(q) bends with the moment order q, and this curvature collapses under shuffling, proving it comes from temporal dependence (intermittent bursts, cascade clustering) rather than fat marginal tails. Translate this diagnostic into a conditioning variable on the direction of a name's recent move: when a stock's local volatility path is close to monofractal (small H(0.5)-H(4) width, homogeneous scaling across scales), the recent drift is being produced by informed order flow that repeats coherently at every scale and should continue over the next few bars; when the path is strongly multifractal (large width), the same drift was manufactured by a handful of liquidity-vacuum bursts stitched together, and such cascades mean-revert once the transient depth is replenished. The other side of the trade is the impact-driven taker and the naive short-horizon trend chaser who cannot distinguish 'many small coherent increments' from 'a few violent ones' because both produce the same realised volatility and the same cumulative return. It is falsified if the interaction between width and recent signed move carries no incremental sign beyond the width term alone, or if the effect survives replacing the temporal-dependence width with its shuffle-invariant tail proxy.

factors.name: Adaptive-Ensemble Model-Bank Forecast with Memory-Regime Gate
factors.description: Per ticker, builds 12 causal ridge-estimated 6-bar-ahead return forecasts (AR-on-6-bar-returns, volume-weighted close-location pressure regression, and constant drift, each on 30/60/120/300-bar estimation windows), forms Adaptive-Ensemble weights by allocating 1/v0 to the argmin of an exponentially discounted (lambda~0.95) multi-valued forecast loss in each of the last v0=30 sub-windows, and outputs the cross-sectionally standardised ensemble forecast scaled by weight concentration (HHI) and amplified when the loss-selected estimation window has just contracted.
factors.trading_idea: Yang & Lucas show that the winning predictor of a financial series changes over time, that recency-discounted realised forecast loss (including the intermediate-horizon 'multi-valued' errors) is a better selector than cross-validation, and crucially that the *effective memory length* chosen by the selector collapses to its shortest setting exactly when the data-generating regime breaks. Most intraday participants trade one statically calibrated predictor (a fixed reversal coefficient, a fixed flow-impact beta), so their signal is systematically mis-signed for the subset of names that have just switched regime; the fixed-model portfolio in the paper broke even while the adaptively selected one earned. I therefore run a small bank of mechanistically distinct 6-bar predictors per name (short-memory AR on non-overlapping 6-bar returns, an intrabar volume-weighted close-location pressure regression, and a pure drift model, each estimated on four window lengths), weight them by the AE sub-sampling rule on recency-discounted multi-valued loss, and trade the cross-sectional dispersion of the resulting forecast — trusting it more where the loss surface picks a decisive winner and where the selected memory has just shortened (a fresh change-point, when slow-moving fixed-model capital is most stale). It is killed if the AE-weighted forecast has no higher IC than the equal-weight average of the same bank, i.e. if the realised-loss weights are pure noise.

factors.name: Quantitative-Probe Hit-Rate Trust Gate on Flow-Impact Estimand
factors.description: Per ticker, on a trailing causal window, estimate (i) the target estimand beta_hat = OLS slope of one-bar return on lagged volume-normalized signed flow, and (ii) a hit rate over five sign-known quantitative probes (volume-|return| impact > 0, sector-peer cohesion > 0, volume autocorr > 0, |return| autocorr > 0, 6-bar variance ratio within tolerance of 1); the factor is the cross-sectionally standardized product (2*hitRate - 1) * beta_hat * current signed flow, so trusted names extrapolate flow impact and probe-failing names take the refuted (reversal) side.
factors.trading_idea: Grunbaum et al. argue that an estimated causal effect deserves trust only if the same estimation machinery simultaneously reproduces *non-target* effects whose signs we already know from domain knowledge; failed probes mean the pipeline (or the regime it is fitted in) is misspecified, so the target estimate must be discounted or refuted. In intraday equity data we genuinely do know the sign of several stylized-fact 'probes' for a well-behaved auction: Kyle-style price impact (|return| rises with volume), positive contemporaneous sector cohesion, positive volume clustering, positive volatility clustering, and a variance ratio near one. When all probes hold, a rolling per-name regression of next-bar return on lagged signed flow is a credible local impact/continuation estimand and its extrapolation of current flow should keep paying for a few bars; when probes break (stale mid, one-sided repricing, idiosyncratic decoupling, mechanical noise), the same fitted slope is confounded and the flow-implied drift typically over-shoots and snaps back. The trade is against liquidity demanders whose flow extrapolation is priced by market makers only in trustworthy regimes; it persists because nobody conditions impact models on the health of the regime they were fitted in. Falsifier: if the IC of beta_hat * current_flow is statistically indistinguishable across high- and low-probe-hit-rate buckets, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Negotiable vs Idiosyncratic Flow Split, Gated by Credit-Standing Eligibility
factors.description: Decomposes each stock's standardized bar-volume surprise into a common part (causal rolling loading on the cross-sectional median volume surprise) and an idiosyncratic residual, forms two volume-weighted path integrals of recent log returns (return earned on common flow vs on residual flow), and outputs the cross-sectionally neutralized combination -w_common*R_common + w_idio*R_idio, where the two weights are tilted by a point-in-time 'acceptance eligibility' score built from interestCoverage, currentRatio, debtToAssets and marketCap ranks.
factors.trading_idea: Accominotti & Ugolini's history of trade finance turns on one distinction: a claim financed by the broad, standardized ('negotiable') market behaves differently from a claim financed inside a closed specialist network, and access to the broad market was rationed by gatekeepers who screened issuers on credit standing. Mapping this to intraday equities: a stock's bar volume splits into a component co-moving with market-wide activity (the anonymous, standardized liquidity pool — crowd/index/ETF-driven flow whose price impact is largely a rent paid to liquidity providers and therefore transient) and an idiosyncratic residual component (specialist, name-specific participation, which is more likely information-bearing and whose impact should persist). Price moves manufactured on 'negotiable' common flow should snap back over the next minute, while moves manufactured on residual specialist flow should extend; the split should be sharpest where balance-sheet eligibility (interest coverage, current ratio, low leverage, size) determines whether a name actually has deep anonymous liquidity or is left to a narrow dealer network. This is falsified if the two flow channels produce statistically indistinguishable forward-return signs, or if the eligibility gate has no interaction — and it persists because separating common from name-specific volume in real time requires cross-sectional state that single-name market makers do not maintain.

factors.name: Darcy Pressure Residual on a Permeability-Weighted Peer Network
factors.description: Per bar, build a peer graph (same industry/sector plus top correlated names over a rolling window) with edge conductances equal to the harmonic mean of node permeabilities K_i = rolling dollar volume / rolling sum |return| (inverse Amihud), form the cross-sectionally demeaned signed-volume source f_i (sign(close-open)*volume over the last few bars, normalized by own average volume), solve the weighted graph-Laplacian Poisson system L_K p = f under a zero-mean constraint (pseudo-inverse / conjugate-gradient iterations), and take the factor as z-score(implied pressure p) minus z-score(realized cumulative displacement over the same lookback), scaled by the cross-sectional rank of low permeability (slow-discharge nodes).
factors.trading_idea: The source paper's physical object is single-phase Darcy flow through a *heterogeneous* permeability field: injection/production wells inject a source term f, and the pressure field solves -div(K grad p) = f with no-flux boundaries and a zero-mean constraint, so pressure piles up exactly where permeability K is low and the flow cannot discharge. Markets have the same structure at 10-second scale: net signed order flow is the well term, the peer/sector network is the porous medium, and per-name liquidity (dollar volume per unit of realized price move, i.e. inverse Amihud) is the local permeability. Solving the discrete Darcy problem gives the pressure field that *should* prevail given today's injections and the liquidity heterogeneity; where the realized price displacement has not yet caught up to that implied pressure, flow (price adjustment) is still pending and should be discharged over the next few bars, most slowly in low-permeability names where market makers widen and adjustment is impeded. The trade is against liquidity demanders who dumped flow into a locally resistive name and against quote-setters who mark that name off its peer network with a lag; it persists because harvesting it requires simultaneous multi-name execution across the peer graph on a seconds clock. It would be falsified if the pressure residual carried no forward return beyond the raw own-name signed-flow imbalance, or if the sign flipped for low-permeability names (i.e. impeded nodes overshoot rather than lag).

factors.name: Preferential-Attachment Attention Residual with Exploration-Rate Gate
factors.description: Over a rolling window, computes each name's share of total market volume and the share predicted by a one-parameter mixed preferential-attachment fit (uniform-exploration weight gamma_t estimated cross-sectionally each bar from current share on lagged share); the standardized attention residual (actual minus predicted share) is then interacted with the name's cross-sectionally demeaned window return and scaled by the implied exploitation intensity (1 - gamma_t, equivalently proximity of the implied tail exponent to 2), giving continuation for excess-attention movers and reversal for proportional-flow movers.
factors.trading_idea: Strauss-Yang-Mazzucato model attention allocation as a mixed preferential-attachment process: with probability gamma a new attention unit is allocated uniformly (exploration), otherwise in proportion to existing popularity (exploitation), yielding tail exponent alpha = 1 + 1/(1-gamma). Intraday trading volume is allocated the same way: a large mechanical share of each bar's volume goes to names in proportion to their own recent turnover (VWAP/participation-rate slicers, basket and ETF-hedge flow are mandated to trade proportional to historic volume), while genuine information/discovery flow arrives *in excess* of that proportional prediction. Proportional 'exploitation' volume is uninformative and its price impact is transient (liquidity providers happily absorb it), whereas the residual 'exploration' volume is self-reinforcing over the next minute (rich-get-richer), so the price move it accompanies persists. The trade is therefore: continue moves made on excess-attention volume, fade moves made on merely proportional volume, with the tilt scaled by the market-wide exploitation intensity (1 - gamma) estimated in the cross-section — it dies if the residual carries no directional information or if reversal dominates irrespective of gamma.

factors.name: Wong–Zakai Area Anomaly: Sub-Block Price/Flow Rotation Drift
factors.description: Builds two causal channels per name over a rolling window — x = cumulative log return, y = cumulative volume-normalised signed flow (volume x sign(close-open), with a sub-bar OHLC shape correction from (close+open-high-low) capturing intra-bar path orientation) — computes the discrete Lévy area 0.5*sum(x_{t-1}dy_t - y_{t-1}dx_t) at native bar resolution and again on k-bar block increments, and takes the anomaly Γ = A_fine - A_coarse; the cross-sectionally ranked Γ, sign-oriented by and gated on the magnitude of the coarse net displacement, is the signal.
factors.trading_idea: Friz–Oberhauser show that solutions of noise-driven evolution equations are NOT continuous in the uniform (endpoint) topology: two driving signals can agree arbitrarily well on sampled values yet produce different dynamics, and the entire difference is carried by the Lévy area, appearing as a deterministic commutator drift [Λ_i,Λ_j]dΓ^{ij} (their 'twisted approximation' and delayed-Brownian-input examples). Market participants who model on coarsely sampled bars are implicitly using the piecewise-linear (Wong–Zakai) reconstruction of the tape: it preserves block endpoints and therefore destroys exactly the sub-block area between the price channel and the order-flow channel. That destroyed area is not noise — it encodes whether flow rotates ahead of price (impact still to be paid out, continuation) or price rotates ahead of flow (unsupported displacement, snap-back) — and it is invisible to any endpoint-based model, so slow, coarse-sampling capital cannot arbitrage it away. Falsifiable: if the area *defect* (fine-resolution area minus block-resolution area) carries no forward information once the coarse area and coarse net displacement are controlled for, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Intraday Investment-Factor Premium AR-Timing Tilt
factors.description: Builds a dollar-neutral conservative-minus-aggressive investment basket from cross-sectional ranks of assetGrowth, capexToRevenue and debtGrowth/netStockIssuance, computes its bar-by-bar realized premium, forecasts the next-6-bar premium with a rolling ridge-shrunk AR regression scaled by inverse rolling premium variance (with negative forecasts shrunk and the multiplier EWMA-smoothed), and outputs each stock's exposure (blend of its characteristic weight and its causal rolling beta to the basket return) multiplied by that timing multiplier.
factors.trading_idea: Panda et al. find that, after multicollinearity inflates everything else, the one robustly significant predictor of the CMA (conservative-minus-aggressive investment) premium is its own lag, and that utility-optimal factor weights scale as E[r]/sigma^2 but must be shrunk/smoothed or turnover destroys the edge. I map that mechanism to the 10-second clock: the intraday return of a dollar-neutral basket built on investment-intensity characteristics (asset growth, capex intensity, debt/share issuance) is serially correlated over ~1 minute because large style/basket orders are sliced across time and index/ETF-driven flow reaches high-investment names with a lag, so the basket-level premium drifts before it decays. The factor therefore times the style basket with a ridge-shrunk AR forecast of its own next-6-bar premium, scales it by inverse realized basket variance (the utility-optimal weight), softens negative forecasts in Campbell-Thompson spirit, and smooths the timing multiplier to control turnover; each stock's tilt is its exposure to that basket. It dies if the basket premium shows no positive autocorrelation at the 6-bar horizon (then the timing multiplier is noise and the whole signal is an unconditional style bet); the counterparty is the slow-moving/mandated basket trader who must complete a schedule regardless of short-term price path.

factors.name: Direct-minus-Recursive Multi-Horizon Forecast Wedge
factors.description: Per bar, build a small causal state vector per ticker (1-bar return, 3-bar return, volume-weighted signed return, range/realized-vol ratio, volume surprise), cross-sectionally demeaned and scaled; on a rolling causal window fit (a) a pooled one-step VAR companion map plus one-step return loading and iterate it 6 steps, and (b) a pooled direct ridge regression of the fully-realized 6-bar forward return on the same state (targets masked to t-6 so no look-ahead). The factor is the cross-sectional rank of the difference (direct forecast minus iterated recursive forecast), damped to zero when the estimated companion matrix is non-stationary (spectral radius >= 1) or the window fit is degenerate.
factors.trading_idea: Wen et al. show that iterating a one-step model to build multi-step forecasts (the Recursive strategy) is biased, flat and fragile to mis-specification, whereas a Direct multi-horizon fit of the same state is sharper and less biased. Most fast market participants effectively forecast recursively: they run one-step AR/impact models and extrapolate, which mechanically attenuates the forecast (spectral-radius decay of the iterated companion matrix) and ignores the non-Markovian components of order-flow and volatility state that only show up in the true h-step map. The wedge between a directly-fitted 6-bar forecast and the recursively-iterated forecast from the same state vector is therefore an estimate of the drift the recursive crowd is structurally under-pricing; it should not be arbitraged away because fitting direct maps at every horizon is more data- and infrastructure-expensive than iterating one model, and because the mis-specification is small in one-step R-squared terms while accumulating over the horizon. Falsifier: if the wedge has no forward IC at 6 bars, or if its IC is fully explained by the level of either component forecast alone (i.e. it is just a repackaged one-step signal), the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: EWC-Consolidated vs Plastic Online-Forecast Wedge
factors.description: Per ticker, two recursive weighted least-squares predictors of next-bar return are run causally on the same small feature vector (1-bar return, signed volume pressure, intra-bar close location) with a fast forgetting factor (~30-bar memory) and a slow one (~1500-bar memory); the slow coefficients are additionally EWC-anchored toward their long-run means with per-coefficient weights proportional to accumulated squared gradients (diagonal Fisher importance). The factor is the cross-sectionally standardised difference between the consolidated and plastic one-step forecasts, multiplied by a replay/novelty gate equal to the Mahalanobis distance of the current feature vector from its recent short-window centroid (scaled by long-window covariance).
factors.trading_idea: The continual-learning literature shows that fast-adapting sequence learners suffer catastrophic forgetting: they overwrite relationships learned across earlier regimes with whatever the most recent (short) data stream implies, and only importance-weighted consolidation (EWC-style Fisher anchoring) or replay preserves the older, still-valid structure. Much of the fast money re-fits intraday microstructure models on rolling recent windows, so quotes drift toward the *plastic* mapping from local order-flow/path features to next-bar returns while the *consolidated* mapping — stable across many regimes and heavily weighted on parameters the data says are important — is under-priced. Trading the wedge (consolidated forecast minus plastic forecast) is a bet that the forgotten-but-durable relation reasserts itself within a few bars, and the trade is strongest when the current feature state has NOT been rehearsed recently (novel relative to the last few minutes but familiar over the long window), exactly the regime the papers identify as maximal forgetting. It dies if the plastic forecast is genuinely the better out-of-sample predictor, i.e. if the wedge's sign flips persistently — a clean falsification test.

factors.name: WaX-Attributed Sliced Transport: Broadness & Volume-Corroboration Gate
factors.description: Over two adjacent causal windows (source = bars t-2W..t-W, target = bars t-W..t) of standardized 2-D points (bar log-return, bar log-volume), computes a sliced Wasserstein model over several fixed projection directions (exact 1-D OT = rank matching), then applies WaX relevance propagation to obtain (i) the quantile-displacement translation in the return coordinate, (ii) the relevance concentration across coupled quantile pairs (participation-ratio broadness), and (iii) the feature-relevance share carried by the volume coordinate; the signal is the signed translation multiplied by a gate that is positive (continuation) when the shift is broad and volume-corroborated and negative (reversal) when it is tail-concentrated and price-only, cross-sectionally standardized.
factors.trading_idea: Naumann et al. show that a distribution shift can be decomposed (via LRP on the primal optimal-transport objective) into how much each coupled instance pair and each input feature contributes to the Wasserstein distance — separating a broad, translation-like transport from a shift carried by a handful of extreme points, and separating which coordinate actually moved. Applied to a stock's recent joint distribution of (bar return, bar log-volume), this distinguishes two very different micro-events that look identical in a simple mean return: (a) a broad-based repricing where the whole return distribution translates and the volume distribution shifts with it (participation-corroborated, information-driven — it keeps drifting for the next minute as slow-moving liquidity providers reprice), versus (b) a shift whose transport relevance concentrates on a few tail quantile pairs with no accompanying change in the volume distribution (one or two aggressive prints or a quote pop against a thin book — mechanically transient, it snaps back). The edge persists because market participants condition on realised mean/momentum rather than on the *shape* and *feature attribution* of the distributional move, and because distinguishing the two requires distribution-level, not path-level, statistics. Falsification: if the gate has no sign-flipping power — i.e. if tail-concentrated, volume-uncorroborated shifts continue at the same rate as broad, volume-corroborated ones — the factor collapses to plain short-horizon drift and dies.

factors.name: Arrow-of-Time Ordinal Asymmetry Gate on Inferred Latent Action
factors.description: Per ticker over a rolling causal window of 10s bars, compute an ordinal-pattern (length-3 permutation) histogram of mid-price returns and measure time-irreversibility as the total-variation distance between each pattern's frequency and that of its time-reversed mirror pattern; separately infer a volume-weighted latent 'action' from intrabar close-minus-open scaled by bar range. The factor is the cross-sectionally standardised latent action multiplied by a gate that is +1 for the most time-irreversible names and -1 for the most reversible ones (continuation vs reversal), then cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Racah & Pal show that two self-supervised probes extract very different structure: temporal-order / tuple-verification heads learn whether a short frame sequence is distinguishable from its shuffled or reversed version, while inverse models recover the latent *action* that drove a state transition. Ported to a limit-order book, the analogue of tuple verification is time-irreversibility of the local mid-price path: a path driven by a persistent, informed metaorder is statistically distinguishable from its time reversal (asymmetric ramp-up / discharge ordinal patterns), whereas a path generated by market-maker inventory round-tripping and uninformed two-sided noise is essentially reversible (detailed-balance diffusion). The analogue of the inverse model is the latent directional 'action' inferred from where the bar closed inside its own range, volume-weighted, i.e. the drive that must have produced the observed transition. The bet: the inferred action predicts continuation only where the arrow of time is detectable, and predicts reversal where the path is reversible — because in the reversible regime the same drive is inventory noise that liquidity providers will unwind. Liquidity providers price level and volatility, not path-orientation asymmetry, so this conditioning survives; it dies if continuation of the drive is flat in irreversibility.

factors.name: Zero-Shot Path-Prototype Drift with Calibrated Novelty Split
factors.description: For each ticker/bar, build a shape-attribute vector over a trailing window of 10s bars (normalised argmax/argmin position of the intra-window price path, return skew, kurtosis, approximate/sample entropy, high-low range over realised vol, volume concentration Gini, signed volume-weighted tilt), z-scored cross-sectionally; cluster attribute vectors pooled from a strictly lagged history block into K prototypes, tag each prototype with its historically realised mean forward 6-bar return, then score each current observation as temperature-softmax similarity to prototypes minus a calibration constant, emitting prototype-drift when the calibrated seen-score clears the gate and minus the recent window return (reversal) scaled by novelty distance when it does not, cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: LETS-GZSL's core insight is that a time series is classified by projecting a learned embedding *together with* a hand-built statistical attribute vector (argmax/argmin location, skew, kurtosis, approximate entropy) into a latent space, and that seen-class confidence must be penalised by a calibration factor because genuinely novel ('unseen') series get force-fit onto familiar prototypes. Markets have the same pathology: most execution algos and short-horizon predictors pattern-match the last few minutes of tape onto a small library of recurring micro-shapes (grind-up, V-bounce, chop, one-sided liquidation) and act on the shape's historical continuation. When the current path really is a member of a well-populated prototype (high softmax confidence, small latent distance), that conditional continuation is real and persists for a handful of bars — the crowd trading it *is* the mechanism. When the path is out-of-library (high distance to every prototype, flat softmax), the same machinery misclassifies it, supplies liquidity or takes direction on a false analogy, and the resulting print is an idiosyncratic dislocation that snaps back. So: trade prototype-conditioned drift when confidence survives calibration, and trade reversal of the just-realised move when the bar-path is novel. Falsifier: if forward 6-bar returns conditioned on prototype membership are indistinguishable from unconditional returns, or if the novelty bucket shows continuation rather than snap-back, the mechanism is dead. It persists because building and maintaining a leak-free path-prototype library with a calibrated novelty gate is operationally costly relative to the per-trade edge, and because the losing side (analogy-driven short-horizon models) is structurally committed to firing on every bar.

factors.name: Bagged MCI Lead-Lag Edge-Confidence Relay
factors.description: For each ticker, forms the peer/sector-aggregate return series, estimates the lagged peer->stock partial correlation conditioning on the stock's own lag and the peer's prior lag (MCI-style), re-estimates it on B bootstrap resamples of the aligned lag-windows, and defines edge confidence as the fraction of resamples where the link exceeds a significance threshold with the majority sign; the factor is the confidence-gated (2c-1)+ times the bagged median coefficient times the latest realized peer-lag shock, cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Cross-stock lead-lag propagation is real but its estimates are dominated by finite-sample noise and by autocorrelation-induced spurious links, so naive Granger/lagged-beta signals trade mostly on estimation error. Debeire et al. (2024) show two fixes that transfer directly: (i) MCI-style conditioning — partial out the target's own recent past and the source's own past, which makes the link test well calibrated precisely in the high-autocorrelation regime that 10-second bars live in; and (ii) bootstrap-bagged edge frequency — resample the aligned lag-windows with replacement and measure how often the link survives with a consistent sign, giving a confidence score that filters false positives. The edge should therefore be concentrated in the small subset of (peer -> stock) links whose bootstrap edge frequency is high, and vanish (or invert, through overfit-driven reversal) where frequency sits near the coin-flip 50% band; the trade is against desks that fit a single in-sample lead-lag matrix and cannot tell a stable channel from a lucky one. Falsification: if sorting on bootstrap edge frequency adds no information beyond the raw magnitude of the same partial correlation, the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Volatility-Granularity Cascade Asymmetry Gate
factors.description: For each ticker, build three volatility granularities from the same windows — finest = mean intrabar range (high-low)/close, medium = mean |1-bar log return|, coarse = |6-bar log return|/sqrt(6) — then compute a rolling-window time-reversal statistic A = corr(fine_vol(t-6), coarse_vol(t)) - corr(coarse_vol(t-6), fine_vol(t)); the factor is the cross-sectionally demeaned, vol-scaled last-6-bar residual return multiplied by tanh of the z-scored A (continuation when the cascade is forward, reversal when inverted) and weighted by the magnitude of the recent short-vs-long vol increment.
factors.trading_idea: Zumbach shows that empirical price series break time-reversal invariance in a very specific way: the correlation between *fine*-granularity past volatility and *coarse*-granularity future volatility exceeds the reverse pairing, i.e. volatility cascades from short to long timescales via return-on-volatility feedback (multiscale ARCH), not via an exogenous hidden vol process. I estimate this granularity asymmetry causally per name over a rolling window and use its sign as a state variable for how the last ~minute of price movement should be interpreted: when the local cascade runs forward (tick-level agitation leading the coarse swing) the move is a shock being integrated by heterogeneous horizons and the drift persists over the next few bars; when the cascade is locally inverted (a coarse swing arriving *before* fine-scale churn, a time-reversed signature typical of inventory unwinding / liquidity withdrawal rather than information), the swing is endogenous overshoot and snaps back. The other side is short-horizon liquidity providers and blanket reversal traders who treat every vol burst identically; the edge persists because the conditioning variable needs a two-timescale rolling cross-correlation estimate per name, which is noisy, non-obvious and only monetisable at sub-minute horizons. Falsifier: if the cascade-asymmetry gate has no interaction with subsequent 6-bar returns (interaction coefficient indistinguishable from zero, factor IC collapsing to that of raw 6-bar reversal), the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Intensive-vs-Casual Flow-Consumption Beta Premium
factors.description: Builds a rolling PC1 'flow-consumption factor' from standardized log growth of market-wide share volume, dollar volume, and trading breadth, split into an intensive leg (bars whose volume exceeds each name's trailing 75th-percentile) and a casual leg (the rest); each stock's return is regressed causally on the market return plus both legs over a rolling window, and the signal is the cross-sectional rank of the intensive-leg beta orthogonalized against the casual-leg beta.
factors.trading_idea: Borri-Liu-Tsyvinski build an aggregate 'consumption' factor from three growth margins (quantity=tokens, expenditure=dollars, reach=distinct users), estimate rolling firm betas on it, and find the premium is earned only on the INTENSIVE, frontier margin (long prompts, seasoned/paying users) and not on the casual/extensive margin. The intraday analogue of realized AI consumption is realized liquidity consumption: bar volume (quantity), dollar volume (expenditure), and the fraction of names actually printing (reach). Aggregate liquidity-demand shocks are self-exciting and only partially absorbed within one bar because market makers and slow-moving intraday capital cannot instantly re-hedge systematic exposure, so names that load on the intensive (large-print) component of the shock keep being pushed over the next minute, while loading on the small-print/casual component is uninformed noise and should carry no drift. Falsifiable: if the casual-margin beta is priced as strongly as the intensive-margin beta (or if the intensive-beta spread is flat/negative once the market factor is controlled for), the mechanism is dead.

factors.name: Boosted-Stump Nonlinearity Premium over Linear AR Forecast (leaf-occupancy gated)
factors.description: On a rolling causal window of pooled cross-sectional observations (features = lags 1-3 of 1-bar returns, the 6-bar past return, normalized intrabar range, and volume z-score; target = realized 6-bar-ahead return whose window is fully in the past), fit a ridge linear forecast and then an LSBoost ensemble of shallow (depth<=2, min-leaf-size constrained, learning rate ~0.25) regression trees on the ridge residuals; the factor is the current-bar boosted-tree increment (tree forecast minus ridge forecast) multiplied by a sqrt-leaf-occupancy confidence weight, then cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Fata-Kadota-Schneider find that regression-tree ensembles beat ARIMA by ~90% on short-horizon price forecasting even though both use essentially the same lagged-price inputs, and that boosted stumps with small learning rate and a minimum leaf size dominate; the gain therefore comes purely from *threshold/regime nonlinearity* in the conditional mean, not from new information. Mapping that to 10-second equity bars: the linear (AR/ridge) part of short-horizon return predictability is exactly the part that fast statistical arbitrageurs already trade away, while the piecewise, state-dependent part (e.g. continuation only when the lag-6 move is large AND intrabar range is compressed, reversal otherwise) survives because it requires a nonlinear conditioning that simple linear alpha stacks cannot express. I trade the *increment* of a causally-refit LSBoost stump ensemble over its own ridge-AR baseline, and shrink it by leaf occupancy because the paper's own diagnostic shows tree/RNN forecasts fail precisely in sparsely populated tail states (price spikes). Falsifiable: if the pooled conditional mean of forward returns is linear in the lag features, the boosted increment collapses to noise and the factor earns nothing; it should also decay to zero if the nonlinear kink is arbitraged (increment shrinks toward the ridge fit over time).

factors.name: Non-Crossing vs Interval Cumulant Wedge Regime Gate
factors.description: From a causal rolling window of standardized 10s returns, estimate all 15 lagged joint moments of the ordered 4-bar word (lags 3,2,1,0), then Moebius-invert them over three partition lattices to get the classical (all partitions), free (non-crossing) and Boolean (interval) fourth cumulants; define nesting = free - Boolean and crossing = classical - free, cross-sectionally standardize both, and multiply a bounded 'nesting-minus-crossing' regime score by the standardized last-3-bar displacement so that nesting-dominated names are traded for continuation and crossing-dominated names for reversal.
factors.trading_idea: Chevyrev–Ebrahimi-Fard–Patras show that the SAME 4-point moment data of an ordered word admits several cumulant coordinate systems, distinguished only by which lattice of partitions supports it: interval partitions (Boolean = purely adjacent dependence), non-crossing partitions (free = adjacency plus NESTED/bracketing dependence), and all partitions (classical = additionally CROSSING/interleaved dependence). Applied to the ordered word of the last four 10-second returns, the wedges between these cumulants are a direct read-out of the microstructural mechanism generating serial dependence: a Boolean/interval regime is plain queue-continuation, a nested regime is an echo (child-order slicing, iceberg refill, latency-delayed liquidity replenishment where a shock at t reappears at t+3 while the intervening bars are noise), and a crossing regime is two interleaved alternating processes (bid-ask bounce, alternating maker/taker aggression). Names whose 4-point structure is nesting-dominated should CONTINUE over the next few bars because the echo leg is still incomplete, while crossing-dominated names should REVERSE because their dependence is a mechanical alternation rather than information. This is falsifiable: if the wedges were pure high-order estimation noise, conditioning short-horizon displacement on them would add nothing over unconditional reversal; the trade is against slicing algorithms (which manufacture the nested echoes) and against market-makers whose bounce manufactures the crossing structure, and it persists because estimating and monitoring fourth-order lag-moment lattices per name at 10-second resolution is costly relative to the per-trade edge.

factors.name: Concentration-Gated Incumbent-to-Fringe Relay with Differentiation Shield
factors.description: Within each PIT industry, builds an incumbent impulse as the market-cap-share-weighted excess return of the top-share firms (net of the cross-sectional mean return), then forms per-name signal = vol-scaled (incumbent impulse − own return over the same short window) multiplied by an industry HHI rank and by a 'predation vulnerability' weight that rises with low market-cap share and falls with within-industry ranks of rdToRevenue, grossMargin, cashRatio and interestCoverage; the result is sector-demeaned cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: Zhang (2023) shows the economic coupling between dominant incumbents and fringe entrants is strongest in concentrated industries and is muted for firms that innovate enough to differentiate their product. Translated to intraday microstructure: industry-specific information is discovered first in the cap-dominant incumbents (they carry the informed flow, index/ETF hedging and analyst attention), and fringe, low-share names in concentrated industries are economically levered to that same industry news yet repriced with a lag because nobody is watching them; firms with genuine differentiation (high R&D intensity, high gross margin) or deep financial slack are legitimately less coupled, so treating them as laggards is noise. The factor therefore buys the concentration-weighted, vulnerability-weighted catch-up gap between the incumbent impulse and the fringe firm's own move, and deliberately zeroes it out for differentiated/insulated names. It dies if the catch-up drift is invariant to industry HHI and to R&D-intensity/margin ranks — i.e. if the relay is just generic peer lead-lag rather than a dominance-exposure phenomenon.

factors.name: SPT Relative-Weight Displacement Scaled by Relative Excess Growth, Diversity-Regime Gated
factors.description: Builds an intraday relative-capitalization weight mu_i = close_i * sharesOutstanding_i / sum(cap) each 10s bar, computes the causal z-scored displacement of log(mu_i) from an EWMA-smoothed level, multiplies the negated displacement by a cross-sectionally normalized rolling estimate of the stock's variance relative to the cap-weighted market return (tau_ii = var(r_i - r_M)), and damps or attenuates the whole signal by a market-level gate built from the recent log-change of a diversity functional G(mu) = (sum mu^0.5)^2 (or Shannon entropy of mu), so reversion is expressed strongest when diversity is flat/rising and suppressed in concentrating regimes.
factors.trading_idea: Stochastic Portfolio Theory (Fernholz, discussed in the source paper) says a functionally generated / diversity-weighted portfolio's relative performance decomposes into the change in the diversity functional G(mu) plus an always-positive drift whose intensity is the excess growth rate, i.e. one half of each name's variance *relative to the market portfolio* (tau_ii = sigma_ii - 2*sigma_iM + sigma_MM). The economic content is that, absent a genuine change in market diversity, a stock's log relative capitalization weight log(mu_i) behaves like a mean-reverting state variable whose pull-back drift scales with its relative variance — high-tau names are exactly where rebalancing flow (index-relative books, vol-harvesting market makers, equal/diversity-weighted mandates) mechanically buys the displaced-down name and sells the displaced-up one. So intraday displacement of log(mu_i) from its slow level should revert, and revert *faster where tau_ii is large*, while genuine concentration regimes (market-wide diversity functional trending down) are precisely when the displacement is a real weight migration rather than noise and reversion should be damped. Falsifiable: if the interaction term (displacement x relative-variance rank) carries no incremental IC over the raw displacement, or if the diversity-trend gate has no conditioning effect, the SPT drift mechanism is not what is driving the reversion and the idea dies.

factors.name: Bandlimited Fundamental-Graph Interpolation Wedge from D-Optimal Liquidity Anchors
factors.description: Builds a sparse kNN peer graph from point-in-time fundamental characteristics and sector labels, takes the |F| lowest Laplacian eigenvectors as the bandlimited subspace, greedily selects a D-optimal anchor sampling set using inverse recent volume as noise variance, robustly (IRLS l1) reconstructs the standardised recent-return cross-section from anchors only, and scores each name by the reliability-weighted wedge between its peer-interpolated value and its own realised return, damped where the name's own volume spike suggests an informed idiosyncratic shock rather than a lag.
factors.trading_idea: Di Lorenzo et al. show that a smooth (bandlimited) signal on a graph can be perfectly reconstructed from a well-chosen subset of nodes, that the best sampling set is the one that maximises the information volume of the rows of the Fourier basis weighted by inverse observation noise, and that sparse impulsive corruption is best handled by an l1 fit. Markets have exactly this structure at high frequency: common information hits the liquid, heavily-traded 'anchor' names first and then diffuses to fundamentally similar but thinner peers, so the cross-section of recent returns is approximately a smooth function on a peer graph, sampled cleanly only at the anchors. If I build the peer graph from point-in-time fundamentals (sector plus valuation/profitability/size proximity — deliberately NOT from return correlations, which would just re-learn the price signal), take the low-frequency Laplacian eigen-subspace as the 'bandlimited' model, and reconstruct the whole cross-section from a D-optimally selected anchor set whose 'noise variance' is the inverse of recent traded volume, then the gap between a name's peer-implied value and its own realised move is a lead-lag dislocation that should close over the next few bars. The trade is falsified if the wedge has zero IC on names where the reconstruction is well-conditioned, or if it only works on the anchors themselves (which would mean the graph is picking up sector beta rather than diffusion); the other side is the liquidity provider absorbing uninformed flow in the thin peer, and the edge persists because harvesting it requires simultaneously pricing and trading a whole peer basket within a minute, which is capacity- and infrastructure-constrained.

factors.name: Sign-Conditional Variance Feedback Gain (GJR wedge) Gated Move Continuation
factors.description: Per ticker, run causal symmetric and sign-split (GJR-style) conditional-variance recursions on 10s log returns, estimate the down-shock and up-shock variance feedback gains (rolling E[r_t^2 | r_{t-1}<0] and E[r_t^2 | r_{t-1}>0] scaled by the unconditional recursion level), cross-sectionally z-score each gain, and multiply the corresponding gain by the recent standardized signed move (down-gain times the negative part, up-gain times the positive part), shrunk by a trust weight equal to the rolling tracking quality of the symmetric GARCH variance forecast versus realized squared returns.
factors.trading_idea: The GINN paper's own diagnostics show that what matters is not the level of forecast variance but *where the GARCH recursion misspecifies the feedback from shocks to variance* — the asymmetric (GJR/TGARCH) terms and the high-frequency residual band. At 10-second resolution the asymmetric shock-to-variance loading is a direct proxy for how liquidity providers react to a signed price shock: in names with a high downside feedback gain, a down-tick genuinely widens the quoted risk and withdraws depth, so the move self-excites and continues; in names whose variance response to a signed shock is flat or dampening, market makers absorb the shock and the print mean-reverts. Cross-sectionally, I therefore expect the *sign-conditional variance feedback gain* to determine the sign of short-horizon continuation vs reversal on a fresh move, and I weight the signal by how well a plain symmetric GARCH recursion is tracking realized variance (the GINN lambda idea: trust the parametric structure only where it fits). Falsification: if the down-shock and up-shock variance loadings carry no cross-sectional dispersion beyond estimation noise, or if high-gain names revert just like low-gain names, the factor has no edge. The other side is the liquidity provider whose inventory-risk asymmetry is mandated/structural, and the inefficiency persists because estimating a per-name asymmetric variance recursion intraday is costly relative to the small per-trade edge.

factors.name: Innovation-Adoption Payoff: Peer Coupling, Idiosyncratic Resistance and Saturation Flip
factors.description: For each bar, compute each stock's short-horizon vol-normalised directional state, form a leave-one-out signed adoption fraction over its industry peer group and a market-wide 'advertising' field, estimate per-name causal coupling J_i (rolling slope of next-bar residual return on lagged peer adoption fraction) and resistance u_i (rolling non-response rate to strong peer pressure), then build a payoff score J_i*peer_fraction*(1-u_i) + field term, gated to zero below a critical breadth threshold and sign-flipped in the near-saturated breadth regime, finally cross-sectionally standardised.
factors.trading_idea: Gonçalves-Laguna-Iglesias model adoption of a novelty via a payoff P = A - u_i + J_i*n, where n is the adopted fraction of an agent's influence group, u_i is idiosyncratic resistance, J_i is a signed social coupling (imitators J>0, contrarians J<0), and adoption saturates at 1-f_c. Read a directional intraday move as an 'innovation' diffusing through a stock's influence group (its industry peers) rather than through the whole market: names with an empirically positive coupling to leave-one-out peer breadth should keep adopting the peer direction over the next few bars, names with negative estimated coupling (structural liquidity providers / mean-reverting inventory holders) should push back, and high-resistance names (chronic non-responders) should be discounted because their payoff never crosses zero. The paper's saturation result gives the falsifiable twist: once peer breadth is near-complete (|signed adoption fraction| beyond a critical level, i.e. no susceptible agents left), incremental adoption is impossible and the sign of the expected drift flips to exhaustion/reversal rather than continuation. This survives because the marginal adopters are slow, mandate-constrained sector traders and index/basket flow that arrive with a lag, while the contrarian side is market-makers absorbing inventory; the signal dies if peer-conditional drift is symmetric in breadth (no threshold/saturation nonlinearity) or if estimated J_i has no out-of-sample persistence.

factors.name: Inverse-RDE Reconstructed Lévy Area Residual (rank-gated)
