factors.description: Over a rolling window of ~60 bars, builds for each name a 2-D path (cumulative log return, cumulative signed flow = sign(close-open)*volume normalised by its own rolling scale), computes its discrete Lévy area A_i = Σ(f-f_s)Δr - Σ(r-r_s)Δf, estimates a 2x2 loading matrix V_i by causal regression of its increments on two latent driver channels (cross-sectional mean return and mean signed flow), reconstructs the latent driver area by cross-sectionally regressing observed A_i on det(V_i) (multi-point reconstruction), and takes the residual ε_i = A_i - det(V_i)·Â_latent; the factor is the standardized ε_i interacted with the standardized window return sign, multiplied by an identifiability gate that shrinks names whose reconstruction matrix is ill-conditioned (small |det(V_i)|, low regression R², or degenerate cross-sectional dispersion of loadings).
factors.trading_idea: Bailleul–Diehl show that the second level of a driving rough path (its Lévy area, i.e. the order in which two channels moved) is invisible in the first-order response but IS recoverable from a driven system observed at several distinct points, provided a rank/non-degeneracy condition on the driving vector fields holds. Map this to markets: treat each name's 2-D observed path (log-price, signed order-flow) as the solution flow of an RDE driven by a low-dimensional latent market driver; estimate each name's loading matrix from first-level increments, reconstruct the latent driver's area by pooling many names (the paper's c observation points), and keep the *unexplained* idiosyncratic area — the stock-specific rotation between its own flow and its own price that the common driver cannot account for. Economically, a positive idiosyncratic area means flow led price (informed pressure still being worked, so the move extends), while a negative area means price led flow (liquidity-demanding chasers arriving after the print, so the move gives back). The trade persists because the ordering information lives only in the second-level object, is destroyed by any first-order (beta/return) decomposition, and is unobservable to anyone who nets flow and returns within the bar; it should be killed if the residual area carries no forward information once we condition on plain signed-flow imbalance, or if the signal survives equally when the loading matrix is near-degenerate (which the paper says must destroy identifiability).

factors.name: Density-Dependent Participation Ceiling Residual (Logistic-MARS Hybrid, Trust-Region Gated)
factors.description: Per ticker, fit a causal trailing logistic reproduction surface for detrended log-volume growth, R_t = r_max - exp(-a0 - a1 v_{t-1} - a2 v_{t-2}) (r_max from a trailing high quantile of R, then closed-form OLS on log(r_max - R)); take the standardized residual (excess participation growth), weight it by a Mahalanobis trust gate that shrinks it toward zero when the current state (v_{t-1}, v_{t-2}) leaves the trailing data-rich ellipse (paper's PCA +/-3 sigma region S), multiply by the sign of the contemporaneous 2-3 bar return, and cross-sectionally (sector-neutrally) z-score the result.
factors.trading_idea: Lai & Wong's lynx analysis models a population's log reproduction rate as a saturating, density-dependent surface R_t = r_max - exp(-a0 - a1 X_{t-1} - a2 X_{t-2}) and only trusts an empirical (spline) correction inside the data-rich region of the state space. Intraday participation behaves the same way: bar-to-bar log-volume growth has a hard biological-style ceiling (schedule traders, market makers and VWAP algos cannot expand size without bound) and is strongly density-dependent (already-crowded bars mechanically decay, giving the familiar volume cycle), so most volume growth is mechanistically predictable and carries no information. The tradable object is the *residual* reproduction rate: participation growth that exceeds the fitted density-dependent capacity law is genuine new information arrival rather than schedule/queue mechanics, and price moves accompanied by such excess participation continue over the next few bars, while moves whose participation sits below the capacity law (the 'extinction' corner of the surface) are unsupported and snap back. Falsifiable: if signed excess-reproduction has no 6-bar continuation edge — i.e. if raw signed volume growth works just as well as the capacity-law residual — the mechanism is dead; the trade is against schedule-driven flow whose volume path is predictable and against traders who read total volume as conviction instead of volume-above-capacity.

factors.name: Implied Liquidity Buffer Depth from Busy-Period Loss Statistics
factors.description: Per ticker, over a causal rolling window, segment bars into busy periods (runs of bars whose volume exceeds a rolling threshold), measure mean served count m-hat per busy period and mean loss count L-hat (bars whose |close-open| divided by sqrt(volume) exceeds the name's own rolling high quantile of that absorption ratio), invert rho-hat = 1 - (1 - L-hat)/m-hat and n-hat = log(L-hat)/log(rho-hat) - 1; the factor is the volatility-normalised signed displacement of the currently active busy period multiplied by a cross-sectionally centred thin-buffer weight (continuation where n-hat is low, reversal where n-hat is high), then cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Abramov's loss-queue results tie three observables of an A/B/1/n system together: the mean number served per busy period (E[nu_n] = sum_i rho^i), the expected losses per busy period (E[L_n] ~ rho^{n+1}), and the buffer size n. Treat resting liquidity in a name as exactly such a finite buffer: a 'busy period' is a maximal run of active bars where flow keeps arriving before the previous impulse is absorbed, and a 'loss' is flow the buffer cannot take at the standing price, which shows up as displacement per unit volume far above the name's own absorption calibration. Inverting the two moment relations gives a causally estimable state variable per name — an implied buffer depth n-hat — that says whether the current burst is being absorbed (deep buffer, rejected flow is rare, displacement is noise to be given back) or is overflowing (shallow buffer, rejected flow re-enters and keeps pushing, so displacement propagates). The edge persists because market makers recondition quoted size on realised volatility, not on the joint loss/busy-period geometry, so the overflow state is systematically under-priced for a minute or so; it is falsified if the forward autocorrelation of signed burst displacement is statistically identical across the thin- and deep-buffer cross-sectional halves.

factors.name: Non-Parametric Win-Rate Calibration of Peer Dislocation with Consensus Gate
factors.description: For each name, compute vol-normalised dislocation of its recent return versus its sector/industry peer median over several windows, quantise each into fixed-width 'spread' buckets (with a half-width hook to avoid ties), and estimate, from strictly past realised data only (expanding pooled cross-sectional history, lagged past the forecast horizon), the empirical conditional up-rate of the 6-bar forward return within each bucket; the signal is the frequency-weighted ensemble edge (p−0.5) across window/grid variants, zeroed when the edge is below an EV threshold, when bucket sample support is too thin, or when cross-variant disagreement in implied probability is high, then cross-sectionally demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Ramesh et al. beat sportsbooks not with a parametric price model but with a purely empirical map P(win | point spread) = historical win rate at that spread, plus two discipline gates: an epsilon band that discards states where the non-parametric estimate has no sample support (the mispriced tails), and an EV threshold that forbids betting on thin edges. The equity analogue is that the response of 1-minute-scale forward returns to a vol-normalised peer-relative dislocation is strongly non-monotone — small dislocations mean-revert (noise/inventory), large ones continue (genuine information, the favourite-longshot analogue) — so linear reversal factors systematically overbet the tails, and the edge lies in estimating the conditional response empirically per quantised 'spread' bucket and abstaining where support or consensus is lacking. Multiple bucket grids and measurement windows act like multiple sportsbooks quoting the same game: agreement across them is a fair-value consensus, disagreement means the state is unpriceable and we should not bet. This dies if the dislocation→forward-return map turns out to be linear and stable (then the calibration table adds nothing) or if bucket win rates are pure sampling noise out-of-sample; it persists because slow, mandate-constrained liquidity providers supply the reversion premium in the crowded middle buckets while news-driven demanders dominate the tails.
